    export async function importStagedArtifact(stateDir, { runId, file, sha256: wantSha, stagedPath }) {
      const stageRoot = resolve(artifactStagingDir(stateDir));
      const src = resolve(stagedPath);
      if (!src.startsWith(`${stageRoot}${sep}`)) {
        throw new RuntimeError('artifact_path_escape', `staged path ${stagedPath} escapes the staging root`);
      }
      const content = await fs.readFile(src);
      const gotSha = createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex');
      if (wantSha && gotSha !== wantSha) {
        throw new RuntimeError('artifact_hash_mismatch',
          `staged artifact sha256 ${gotSha} != recorded ${wantSha}`);
      }
      const dir = runArtifactsDir(stateDir, runId);
      await ensureDir(dir);
      await atomicWriteFile(join(dir, file), content, 0o640);
      await fs.rm(src, { force: true }).catch(() => {});
      return { file, bytes: content.length, sha256: gotSha };
    }
    
    export async function writeRunArtifact(stateDir, runId, name, content) {
      if (typeof name !== 'string' || !ARTIFACT_NAME_RE.test(name)) {
        throw new RuntimeError('invalid_argument', `artifact name must match ${ARTIFACT_NAME_RE}: ${JSON.stringify(name)}`);
      }
      const dir = runArtifactsDir(stateDir, runId);
      await ensureDir(dir);
      const file = join(dir, name);
      const resolved = resolve(dir, name);
      if (resolved !== join(dir, name) || name.includes('/') || name.includes('\\')) {
        throw new RuntimeError('invalid_argument', `artifact name escapes the run dir: ${name}`);
      }
      await atomicWriteFile(file, content, 0o640);
      const buf = await fs.readFile(file);
      return {
        file: name,
        bytes: buf.length,
        sha256: createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest('hex'),
      };
    }

    async function cmdRecordEvent(ctx, aggregate, payload, now) {
      const run = runOf(aggregate, reqStr(payload.runId, 'runId'));
      if (!run) throw new CommandError(404, 'run_not_found', `run ${payload.runId} does not exist`);
      const type = reqStr(payload.type, 'type');
      if (!EVENT_TYPE_RE.test(type)) {
        throw new CommandError(422, 'invalid_argument', `event type must match ${EVENT_TYPE_RE}`);
      }
      const data = payload.data === undefined ? null : payload.data;
      const bytes = Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(data ?? null), 'utf8');
      if (bytes > EVENT_MAX_BYTES) {
        throw new CommandError(413, 'event_too_large', `event data exceeds ${EVENT_MAX_BYTES} bytes`);
      }
      // Event authority: an event tied to an attempt requires that attempt's
      // owner instance; a run-level event requires the last attempt's owner
      // (or, before attempts exist, the bound workspace's env authority). A run
      // that has established no authority yet accepts diagnostic events from
      // any authenticated internal caller.
      if (payload.attemptId) {
        // Explicit attempt binding: EXACTLY that attempt's owner — never the
        // validation owner, never a predecessor.
        const refAtt = findAttempt(run, reqStr(payload.attemptId, 'attemptId'));
        if (!refAtt) {
          throw new CommandError(404, 'attempt_not_found', `attempt ${payload.attemptId} unknown`);
        }
        if (!ownsResource(refAtt.owner, payload)) {
          throw new CommandError(409, 'not_attempt_owner',
            `events on ${refAtt.id} require its owner instance`);
        }
      } else {
        // Run-level event authority, in precedence order:
        //   1. the CURRENT validation reservation owner — after a dead-owner
        //      adoption it holds the run's execution duty even while stale
        //      attempt/workspace records still name the predecessor;
        //   2. the last attempt's owner;
        //   3. the bound workspace's env authority;
        //   (a run with no established authority accepts diagnostics from any
        //   authenticated internal caller).
        const v = run.validation;
        const vOwner = v && (v.status === 'active' || v.status === 'unproven')
          ? v.owner : null;
        const refAtt = run.attempts[run.attempts.length - 1] ?? null;
        if (vOwner) {
          if (!ownsResource(vOwner, payload)) {
            throw new CommandError(409, 'not_validation_owner',
              'run-level events during an open validation require its owner instance');
          }
        } else if (refAtt) {
          if (!ownsResource(refAtt.owner, payload)) {
            throw new CommandError(409, 'not_attempt_owner',
              `events on ${refAtt.id} require its owner instance`);
          }
        } else if (run.workspaceId) {
          const ws = aggregate.workspaces?.[run.workspaceId];
          if (ws && ws.owner && !ownsResource(ws.owner, payload)) {
            throw new CommandError(409, 'not_workspace_owner',
              'run-level events require the bound workspace\u2019s owner instance');
          }
        }
      }
      const ev = { seq: run.eventsCursor ?? 0, at: now, type, data };
      run.eventsCursor = (run.eventsCursor ?? 0) + 1;
      // The aggregate is authoritative for events; runs/<id>.events.jsonl is a
      // canonical atomic projection rewritten on flush. A torn/partial file
      // cannot lose an accepted event — the aggregate replays it.
      run.events = Array.isArray(run.events) ? run.events : [];
      run.events.push(ev);
      ctx.appendRunEvent(run.id, run.events);
      // Blocked/ambiguous diagnostics must be durable on the RUN record itself —
      // the attempt stays nonterminal (reservation retained), but the diagnosis
      // survives restarts and is queryable without paging through events.
      if (DIAG_EVENT_TYPES.has(type)) {
        applyDiag(run, type, data, refAtt?.id ?? null, now);
      }
      stageRun(aggregate, run, ctx);
      return { aggregate, result: { runId: run.id, seq: ev.seq } };
    }

      async function scanPredecessors() {
        const mine = selfEnv();
        let files = null;
        try {
          files = await fsp.readdir(journalDir);
        } catch (e) {
          if (!e || e.code !== 'ENOENT') {
            // EACCES/EIO/etc: a spool directory we cannot read may hide a dead
            // predecessor's tracked work — degrade, never pretend "first boot".
            journalDegraded = true;
            lastJournalError = `journal dir unreadable: ${e?.code || e?.message || e}`;
          }
        }
        // Instance ids may contain '-'; the runner/instance boundary cannot be
        // split by regex on the LAST dash. The same-runner test is a PREFIX
        // match against OUR runnerId — everything prefixed 'recovery-<runnerId>-'
        // is potentially ours and must parse/degrade, never skip silently.
        const ownPrefix = `recovery-${runnerId}-`;
        for (const f of files || []) {
          if (!f.startsWith(ownPrefix) || !f.endsWith('.json')) continue;
          if (f === `recovery-${runnerId}-${instanceId}.json`) continue;
          const srcInst = f.slice(ownPrefix.length, -'.json'.length);
          // A dead predecessor's snapshot is consumed once — re-reading it
          // would resurrect already-drained tracked entries every tick.
          if (seenPredecessors.has(srcInst)) continue;
          let doc = null;
          try {
            doc = JSON.parse(await fsp.readFile(join(journalDir, f), 'utf8'));
          } catch {
            // Same-runner file we cannot read: it may be a live peer's snapshot
            // we must not discard — degrade rather than silently skip.
            journalDegraded = true;
            lastJournalError = `recovery snapshot unreadable: ${f}`;
            continue;
          }
          if (!doc || typeof doc !== 'object' || doc.runnerId !== runnerId
            || !SAFE_ID_RE.test(srcInst)) {
            journalDegraded = true;
            lastJournalError = `recovery snapshot corrupt: ${f}`;
            continue;
          }
          if (!envKeyEqual(doc.envKey, mine)) continue;          // different env — never ours
          if (!envInstanceEqual(doc.envInstance, selfEnvInstance())) continue;
          // The filename suffix is the identity; a doc claiming a different
          // instanceId is corrupt — degrade, never inherit authority from it.
          if (doc.instanceId !== srcInst) {
            journalDegraded = true;
            lastJournalError = `recovery snapshot instance mismatch: ${f}`;
            continue;
          }
          // Same container, different instance: inherit ONLY when the recorded
          // owner process is proven dead in this very pid namespace.
          const probe = Number.isInteger(doc.pid)
            ? runtime.processIdentity(doc.pid) : null;
          const dead = probe && probe.exists === true
            ? (probe.state === 'Z'
              || (probe.readable && probe.starttime && doc.pidStarttime && probe.starttime !== doc.pidStarttime))
            : probe && probe.exists === false;

                ...t, owned: false, inheritedFrom: srcInst,

          const spoolFile = join(journalDir, `u4-journal-${runnerId}-${srcInst}.jsonl`);

          try {
            raw = await fsp.readFile(spoolFile, 'utf8');
          } catch (e) {
            if (e && e.code !== 'ENOENT') {
              journalDegraded = true;
              lastJournalError = `predecessor journal unreadable: ${e?.code || e?.message || e}`;
            }
          }
          if (raw) {
            const entries = [];
            for (const line of raw.split('\n')) {
              const tt = line.trim();
              if (!tt) continue;
              let entry;
              try {
                entry = JSON.parse(tt);
              } catch {
                entry = { kind: 'corrupt', raw: tt.slice(0, 500) };
              }
              entry.srcInstance = srcInst;
              entries.push(entry);
            }
            if (entries.length) {
              inheritedSpools.set(srcInst, { file: spoolFile, entries });
            }
          }

        // entry — later sends inherit the post-command revision automatically.

        if (att.supervisor && Number.isInteger(att.supervisor.pid)) return null;

          starttime: proc?.starttime ?? null,
          pidNs: proc?.pidNs ?? null,

        };
        // Child identity is captured only when the child reads positively LIVE
        // and fully readable — a half-visible child is recorded as nothing rather
        // than as an unverifiable identity.
        if (out.childPid !== null) {

      const { svc, projectDir } = env;
      await seedBase(svc, projectDir);
      const runId = await mkManagedRun(svc);
      const { sched, runtime } = mkSched(env, { behavior: { outcome: 'never' } });
      // A porch-like runtime: serialized child_pid but NO spawn attestation
      // (child_spawned absent). The stricter gate must NOT infer no-child.
      const origStatus = runtime.status.bind(runtime);
      let attest = false;
      runtime.status = async (rid) => {
        const st = await origStatus(rid);
        if (st?.ok && !attest) delete st.childSpawned;
        return st;
      };
      await sched.tick();                    // launch; sup bound WITHOUT childNone
      const att = attemptsOf(await runView(svc, runId))[0];
      assert.ok(att.supervisor?.pid, 'supervisor bound at launch');
      assert.equal(att.supervisor.childPid ?? null, null);
      assert.notEqual(att.supervisor.childNone, true,
        'no immutable no-child attestation was recorded');
      const pid = runtime._runs.get(att.porchRunId).pid;
      runtime._force(att.porchRunId, { status: 'completed', finalText: 'done' });
      runtime._setProc(pid, { exists: false });   // recorded supervisor provably dead
      for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) await sched.tick();
      let run = await runView(svc, runId);
      assert.equal(attemptsOf(run)[0].status, 'running',
        'terminal metadata with an unattested child state never resolves');
      const evs = (await getEvents(svc, runId)).json;
      assert.ok((evs.events || []).some(
        (e) => e.type === 'terminal_unproven' && e.data?.code === 'child_unknown'),
        'durable diagnostic names the unattested child state: ' + J(evs.events?.slice(-3)));
      // Positive attestation restores discharge of the same terminal run.
      attest = true;
      await sched.tick();
      run = await runView(svc, runId);
      assert.equal(attemptsOf(run)[0].status, 'completed',
        'the same run resolves once the runtime attests no child (childSpawned:false)');
    });
    
    test('outage: journaled resolve — unrecorded child retains; already-terminal still requires proof', async () => {
      const env = await mkEnv();
      const { svc, projectDir } = env;
      await seedBase(svc, projectDir);
      const runId = await mkManagedRun(svc);
      const swx = { down: false };
      const { sched, runtime } = mkSched(env, { sw: swx, behavior: { outcome: 'never' } });
      await sched.tick();                          // launch; sup bound WITH childNone:true
      const att = attemptsOf(await runView(svc, runId))[0];
      const porchRunId = att.porchRunId;
      const supPid = runtime._runs.get(porchRunId).pid;
      swx.down = true;
      runtime._force(porchRunId, { status: 'completed', finalText: 'fake result' });
      runtime._setProc(supPid, { exists: false }); // supervisor dead mid-outage
      await sched.tick();                          // terminal proof passed → resolve journaled
      const jrnl = await fs.readFile(sched._journalFile, 'utf8');
      assert.match(jrnl, /"kind":"resolve"/, 'resolve duty journaled during outage');
      const resolveEntry = jrnl.split('\n').find((l) => l.includes('"kind":"resolve"'));
      assert.ok(resolveEntry, 'resolve entry captured for re-append');
    
      // The runtime now reports a child pid that was NEVER recorded while live —
      // journaled resolve must retain: the unrecorded child is never probed.
      const fakeChild = 99177;
      runtime._runs.get(porchRunId).childPid = fakeChild;
      runtime._procs.set(fakeChild, {
        exists: true, readable: true, state: 'R',
        starttime: 'cst-unrecorded', pidNs: 'ns-foreign-to-recording',
      });
      const probesOf = (pid) =>
        runtime._calls.filter((c) => c.m === 'processIdentity' && c.pid === pid).length;
      swx.down = false;
      for (let i = 0; i < 4; i += 1) await sched.tick();
      let run = await runView(svc, runId);
      assert.equal(attemptsOf(run)[0].status, 'running',
        'a status-reported but never-recorded child retains the journaled resolve');
      const jrnl2 = await fs.readFile(sched._journalFile, 'utf8');
      assert.match(jrnl2, /"kind":"resolve"/, 'the duty is retained, not dropped');
      assert.match(jrnl2, /child_unproven|child_unknown/,
        'retained diagnostic names the unproven child state');
      assert.equal(probesOf(fakeChild), 0,
        'an unrecorded child pid is NEVER probed');
      assert.equal(cancels(runtime).length, 0, 'nothing is signalled');
    
      // Restore the no-child truth — explicit attestation discharges the duty.
      runtime._runs.get(porchRunId).childPid = null;
      await sched.tick();
      run = await runView(svc, runId);
      assert.equal(attemptsOf(run)[0].status, 'completed',
        'explicit no-child attestation discharges the journaled resolve');
    
      // Re-append the same entry — the attempt is now already terminal in the
      // authoritative record. An unproven child must STILL retain: terminal
      // metadata alone never substitutes for the positive child proof.
      await fs.appendFile(sched._journalFile, resolveEntry + '\n');
      runtime._runs.get(porchRunId).childPid = fakeChild;
      await sched.tick();
      const jrnl3 = await fs.readFile(sched._journalFile, 'utf8');
      assert.match(jrnl3, /"kind":"resolve"/,
        'already-terminal + unproven child retains — metadata alone never discharges');

    // record_event authority after a real adoption: the CURRENT validation owner
    // writes run-level events even though the run's last attempt belonged to the
    // dead predecessor; an unrelated instance is refused; an attempt-scoped
    // event still requires the exact attempt owner — never the adopter.
    // ============================================================================
    
    test('U5 event authority: adopted validation owner writes run-level; attempt events stay exact-owner', async () => {
      const env = await mkEnv();
      const { svc, projectDir, stateDir } = env;
      await seedBase(svc, projectDir);
      const registry = { runs: new Map(), records: new Map(), usedAttempts: new Set(),
        procs: new Map(), unreadable: new Map(), listFails: 0, seq: 0 };
      const pidA = 93001;
      // A long check keeps the validation genuinely active through the probe.
      const runId = await mkValidationRun(svc, 'card-a', [{ run: 'sleep 30', timeoutSec: 60 }]);
      const a = mkSched(env, { registry, instanceId: 'instA', instPid: pidA, leaseMs: 30_000 });
      let b = null;
      try {
        let run = await drive(svc, a.sched, runId,
          (r) => r.validation?.status === 'active'
            && (r.attempts || []).some((x) => x.role === 'implementer'
              && ['completed', 'failed', 'cancelled'].includes(x.status)),
          { maxTicks: 240, delayMs: 60 });
        const implAtt = run.attempts.find((x) => x.role === 'implementer');
        assert.ok(implAtt && implAtt.status === 'completed',
          'the implementer completed under A before the handoff');
        assert.equal(run.validation?.owner?.instanceId, 'instA');
    
        // Positive death → B adopts the validation.
        registry.procs.set(pidA, { exists: false });
        b = mkSched(env, { registry, instanceId: 'instB', instPid: 93002, leaseMs: 30_000 });
        run = await drive(svc, b.sched, runId,
          (r) => r.validation?.owner?.instanceId === 'instB', { maxTicks: 240, delayMs: 60 });
        assert.ok((run.validation?.adoptions || [])
          .some((x) => x.kind === 'process_dead'), 'B adopted under process_dead proof');
    
        const cli = mkClient(svc, stateDir);
        const rev = async () => (await getCard(svc, 'card-a')).json.internalRevision;
        const evt = async (body, tries = 8) => {
          let res;
          for (let i = 0; i < tries; i += 1) {
            res = await cli.command('card-a', {
              ...body, expectedInternalRevision: await rev(),
            }).catch((e) => ({ status: e.status ?? 0, code: e.code, message: e.message }));
            if (res?.code !== 'revision_conflict') return res;
          }
          return res;
        };
        const selfOf = (inst) => ({ runnerId: 'host-runner', instanceId: inst });
    
        // The CURRENT validation owner (B) writes a run-level event — the stale
        // last-attempt owner A must NOT shadow the live reservation authority.
        const okB = await evt({
          commandId: `ev-b-${randomUUID().slice(0, 6)}`, type: 'record_event',
          payload: { runId, type: 'recovery_note',
            data: { note: 'adopter holds the duty' }, ...selfOf('instB') },
        });
        assert.equal(okB.ok, true, `adopter's run-level event accepted: ${J(okB)}`);
    
        // An unrelated third instance may never write run-level events.
        const noC = await evt({
          commandId: `ev-c-${randomUUID().slice(0, 6)}`, type: 'record_event',
          payload: { runId, type: 'recovery_note',
            data: { note: 'unrelated' }, ...selfOf('instC') },

    ### U5 — Проверки, ревью, исправления и приёмка
    
    **Covers:** R4, R6, R7; KTD5, KTD7. **Зависимости:** U4.
    
    Создать validation-worktree из точного результата, выполнить принятые setup/checks, сохранить логи. Подключить существующие review/checker-правила через managed артефакты/API и boardctl. Реализовать ограниченные циклы исправлений и приёмку по hash. Проверяющие роли не должны вносить изменения в принимаемый workspace; передавать им копию результата, а её изменения не включать в результат задачи.
    
    **Сценарии:** exit=0 агента при failed checks не даёт готовность; проверки не изменяют workspace задачи; новый/удалённый/незакоммиченный файл входит в снимок; отсутствующий verdict блокирует готовность; disputed/unvetted блокируют; отклонённое замечание не блокирует; открытое неблокирующее замечание сохраняется в отчёте и не блокирует готовность; лимит цикла даёт blocked; исправления запускают новые проверки; изменение результата перед accept отклоняет приёмку; остановка проверки завершает только её process group.
    
    ### U6 — Документы, согласования и выполнение в карточке и Workflow
    
    **Covers:** R1–R3, R5–R8; KTD3, KTD5. **Зависимости:** API U2; полный поток после U5.
    
    Добавить `src/stores/execution.ts`, типы и API-клиент. В `CardDrawer.vue` показать документы/версии, две кнопки согласования, состав, ветку, состояние, stop/change/continue и историю. Учитывать серверную карточку при отображении доски; обычный autosave не пишет lifecycle-поля. Использовать существующие ACP-сессии для связанного обсуждения.
    
    В Workflow добавить managed-прогоны с отдельным источником событий. porchRunId не является ACP sessionId: «открыть запуск» ведёт в детали выполнения, «открыть обсуждение» — в связанный чат. Сохранить существующий reader внешних porch-прогонов. Показать причины недоступности действий и ошибки 409 с обновлением состояния.
    
    **Сценарии:** полный путь требования→план→состав→start→приёмка; редактирование входов требует согласования заново; две вкладки показывают одинаковое состояние; устаревший autosave не возвращает active-card в backlog; нет сервера — start disabled без отложенного отправления; запуск открывает собственную историю, обсуждение — правильную ACP-сессию; старый внешний porch-прогон по-прежнему виден.
    
    ### U7 — Интеграционные проверки и включение
    
    **Covers:** R1–R8; KTD1–KTD7. **Зависимости:** U1–U6.
    
    Добавить проверки модулей с имитатором runtime и контролируемыми сбоями. Интеграционные fixtures запускаются через Compose; существующие e2e-harness с bare node/Python-серверами адаптировать перед использованием. Включать новый механизм только через явное enable; выполнить миграционную проверку старых данных. Документировать настройку состава, исправление авторизации, отмену и восстановление.
    
    **Сценарии:** полный запуск каждым CLI; stop и continue; падение между durable writes; перезапуск Node и пересоздание runner; legacy/managed карточки одновременно; регрессии board/claims/review/Workflow; ACP replay остаётся только в собственной вкладке, request-id разных сокетов независимы.
    
    **Порядок поставки:** U1 и U2 → U3 → U4 → U5 → U6 → U7. Backend и UI можно коммитить небольшими частями; пользовательский start доступен только после работающих stop/reconcile и гейтов. После этого отдельно уточнять планы Fusion и подготовки идеи.
    
    ## Verification Contract
    
    Проверки ниже выполняются при реализации; в ходе составления плана сервисы и CLI не запускались. Прочитанный контракт установленного porch ещё не доказывает совместимость контейнера runner.
    
    1. **Контракт runtime:** реальные launch/events/result/cancel для Devin, Codex, Pi через Compose; сохранение артефактов и наблюдение после рестарта. Это входной гейт U1.
    2. **Модули:** тесты сериализации CAS, идемпотентности, согласований, ownership, переходов, snapshots и reconcile на имитаторе; Node-тесты импортируют модули без запуска HTTP listener.
    3. **Интеграция:** Compose-backed API и browser-сценарии U2–U7 с имитатором; детерминированные сбои стартового handshake, lease, отмены и записи проекций. Затем короткий реальный solo-поток каждым CLI.
    4. **Frontend:** `npm run build:web` на хосте, проверка ошибок Vue/TypeScript и сборки; браузерная проверка пользовательского потока и двух вкладок.
    5. **Runtime-правила:** перед запуском `docker compose ps` и `ss -tlnp`; стек только Compose, штатные порты без дополнительных серверов. Не использовать legacy e2e-harness до его адаптации к этому правилу.
    6. **Регрессии:** старые карточки и внешние porch-прогоны; review/checker; session/load routing и namespace request-id. Tauri-ветки не менять. При необходимости bridge править в `deploy/acp-ws-bridge.mjs`.
    
    Результаты проверки фиксировать отдельно от плана: команды, exit codes, сценарии, CLI/модели и найденные ограничения. Не отмечать неподтверждённые сценарии успешными.
    
    ## Definition of Done
    
    - R1–R8 доступны для явно включённой карточки; сценарии U1–U7 пройдены с сохранёнными результатами.
    - Devin, Codex и Pi дают проверенный результат через один контракт acp-ui/porch; compose-авторизация и постоянные пути подтверждены.
    - Нет дубликатов после повторной команды, двух вкладок и частичного launch; stop и reconcile доказаны до включения start.
    - История, принятые документы, ветка и артефакты переживают перезапуск; managed-поля не откатываются legacy PUT.
    - Приёмка относится к проверенному снимку результата; merge/push автоматически не выполняются.
    - Старые карточки, claims, Workflow и ACP-инварианты сохранены; frontend собирается на хосте.

    // acp-runner.mjs — thin "board -> CLI" host service for the ACP UI panel.
    //
    // The runner is deliberately dumb: it knows no prompts and does no planning.
    // For every card whose stage is bound to a role (roles.json `stageRoles`)
    // and that holds no live claim, it:
    //   1. puts a rev-safe claim into `claims.json` (lease + pid + runnerPid +
    //      the stage the card was claimed from),
    //   2. writes a SHORT brief to <projectPath>/.acp/cards/<cardId>/00_brief.md
    //      (first deriving 03_checklist.md from 02_plan.md's list items when it
    //      is missing — an existing checklist is progress state and is never
    //      regenerated — and naming the first open item in the brief),
    //   3. spawns the role's CLI with cwd = projectPath (up to `maxRetries`
    //      attempts on a non-zero exit), stdout/stderr -> run-<N>.log,
    //   4. renews `leaseUntil` on a heartbeat while the child runs,
    //   5. on exit writes `kind: 'card'` events (with `role` + `sessionId` and,
    //      when the role carries `models`, the step's `model`) to
    //      activity.json, releases the claim, and NEVER moves the card.
    //
    // Modes:
    //   node server/acp-runner.mjs --once           # single pass, then exit
    //   node server/acp-runner.mjs --serve          # loop with the roles' poll interval
    //   node server/acp-runner.mjs stop-all         # SIGTERM own children, release own claims
    //   node server/acp-runner.mjs release-all      # release own claims, kill nothing
    //   node server/acp-runner.mjs cancel <cardId>  # kill that card's child + flag it blocked
    //
    // Env: STATE_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:25900), ROOT_DIR (directory the
    // project paths must live under; default $HOME/projects), DRY_RUN=1 (print
    // the command instead of spawning), RUNNER_ID (default `runner-<pid>`),
    // RUNNER_DEBUG=1 (heartbeat/sweep traces on stderr — renewals never hit the
    // ledger).
    //
    // Guards: timeoutMin -> SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 10 s; maxConcurrent per role
    // is strict; maxRetries (default 1 = no retry) caps attempts per card and the
    // exhausted card is flagged `blocked`; idleTimeoutMin (default 15, 0 =
    // watchdog off) -> a child silent for that long takes the same SIGTERM
    // path as the lease timeout, audited as `idle Nm — terminated` and counted
    // as a failed attempt; cards in done/backlog or flagged blocked/cancelled
    // are never taken; a sweep on every pass drops claims whose lease expired
    // while their pid is dead and returns those cards to the stage they were
    // claimed from, flagged `blocked`; an unreachable state server is reported
    // on stderr without exiting (in --serve); cards are never moved.
    // stop-all/cancel only ever signal pids that are still children of the
    // runner pid recorded in the claim (or spawned by this process) — a
    // foreign runner's process is never touched.
    //
    // Node only, zero dependencies.
    
    import { spawn, execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
    import { promises as fs, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
    import { homedir } from 'node:os';
    import { join, resolve, sep } from 'node:path';
    import { isManagedCard } from './execution/legacy-guard.mjs';
    
    const STATE_URL = (process.env.STATE_URL || 'http://127.0.0.1:25900').replace(/\/+$/, '');
    const ROOT_DIR = resolve(process.env.ROOT_DIR || join(homedir(), 'projects'));
    const DRY_RUN = process.env.DRY_RUN === '1';
    const RUNNER_ID = process.env.RUNNER_ID || `runner-${process.pid}`;
    const DEBUG = /^(1|true|yes|on)$/i.test(process.env.RUNNER_DEBUG || '');
    
    const RETRY_TRIES = 6;
    const RETRY_DELAY_MS = 300;
    const KILL_GRACE_MS = 10_000;
    const MAX_ENTRIES = 5000;
    const MIN_HEARTBEAT_MS = 5_000;
    
    // pid -> ChildProcess for runs started by this process (used by stop-all).
    const liveProcs = new Map();
    
    function debug(msg) {
      if (DEBUG) console.error(`[runner ${new Date().toISOString()}] ${msg}`);
    }
    
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // State-server HTTP client (same protocol as server/acp-state-server.mjs:
    // GET/PUT /api/state/:name with {data, rev}; rev mismatch -> 409).
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    async function req(method, path, body) {
      const res = await fetch(`${STATE_URL}${path}`, {
        method,
        headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
        body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
      });
      let payload = {};
      try {
        payload = JSON.parse((await res.text()) || '{}');
      } catch {
        payload = {};
      }
      return { status: res.status, payload };
    }
    
    async function readDoc(name, fallback) {
      const { status, payload } = await req('GET', `/api/state/${name}`);
      if (status === 404) return { data: structuredClone(fallback), rev: 0 };
      if (status !== 200) throw new Error(`GET ${name} -> ${status}`);
      return { data: payload.data ?? structuredClone(fallback), rev: Number(payload.rev) || 0 };
    }
    
    async function writeDoc(name, data, rev) {
      const { status, payload } = await req('PUT', `/api/state/${name}`, { data, rev });
      if (status === 409) {
        const err = new Error(`rev conflict on ${name}`);
        err.code = 'REV_CONFLICT';
        throw err;
      }
      if (status !== 200) throw new Error(`PUT ${name} -> ${status}`);
      return Number(payload.rev) || 0;
    }
    
    async function mutate(name, fallback, fn, tries = RETRY_TRIES) {
      let last = null;
      for (let i = 0; i < tries; i++) {
        const { data, rev } = await readDoc(name, fallback);
        const next = fn(structuredClone(data));
        try {
          await writeDoc(name, next, rev);
          return next;
        } catch (e) {
          if (e && e.code === 'REV_CONFLICT') {
            last = e;
            await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, RETRY_DELAY_MS));
            continue;
          }
          throw e;
        }
      }
      throw new Error(`${name}: lost ${tries} revision races (${last})`);
    }
    
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Model helpers (mirror scripts/boardctl: live claim = leaseUntil > now).
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    function liveClaims(claimsDoc, now = Date.now()) {
      const out = {};
      for (const [cid, claim] of Object.entries(claimsDoc.claims || {})) {
        if (Number(claim?.leaseUntil) > now) out[cid] = claim;
      }
      return out;
    }
    
    function emptyBoard() {
      return { version: 2, cards: [] };
    }
    function emptyProjects() {
      return { version: 1, projects: [], activeProjectId: 'all' };
    }
    function emptyRoles() {
      return { version: 1, roles: [], stageRoles: {} };
    }
    function emptyClaims() {
      // `attempts` is the dispatcher's per-card failure counter: it survives
      // claim release so a card cannot be retaken forever. A successful run
      // clears it; exhausting `maxRetries` flags the card blocked.
      return { version: 1, claims: {}, attempts: {} };
    }
    function emptyActivity() {
      return { entries: [], usage: [] };
    }

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    """boardctl — work with the ACP panel board from a terminal or an agent.
    
    Talks straight to the host state server (default http://127.0.0.1:25900), the
    same document the web panel reads, so a card added here shows up on every
    device, and a card claimed here is not taken twice.
    
        boardctl stages                      # stages + the statuses each one allows
        boardctl list --project acp-ui
        boardctl next --project acp-ui       # the card an agent should pick up
        boardctl show 3f2a                  # any unique id prefix works
        boardctl add --title "Fix X" --project acp-ui --stage spec --priority high
        boardctl move 3f2a dev review
        boardctl claim 3f2a --agent hermes --session sess-1 --lease 900
        boardctl release 3f2a --reason "handing over"
        boardctl note 3f2a "measured: panel writes 41 rows"
        boardctl review 3f2a                 # findings, round, the agent_tested gate
        boardctl review 3f2a --sync          # minor/nit -> backlog cards, round-limit flag
        boardctl review 3f2a --round 2 --close f-crit
        boardctl review-check 3f2a f-crit confirmed --reason "verified at auth.ts:88"
        boardctl events --limit 20 --card 3f2a
        boardctl delegate --session sess-1 --subagent explore --goal "map auth flow"
        boardctl delegate --session sess-1 --subagent explore --end --outcome done \
            --detail "mapped 3 entry points"
    
    Every command takes --json for machine-readable output. The acting agent name
    comes from --agent, else $BOARD_AGENT, else "boardctl".
    
    Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 usage/validation error, 2 not found, 3 conflict/transport.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import argparse
    import json
    import os
    import sys
    import time
    import urllib.error
    import urllib.request
    import uuid
    
    DEFAULT_URL = os.environ.get("BOARD_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:25900")
    DEFAULT_PROJECT = os.environ.get("BOARD_PROJECT", "")
    ACTOR = os.environ.get("BOARD_AGENT", "boardctl")
    
    # Mirrors BOARD_STAGE_IDS / STAGE_STATUSES in src/stores/board.ts. Kept here so
    # the CLI can refuse an invalid combination instead of writing a card the panel
    # would silently rewrite.
    STAGES: "list[str]" = ["backlog", "spec", "plan", "dev", "reviewtest", "done"]
    STAGE_LABELS = {
        "backlog": "Backlog",
        "spec": "Spec",
        "plan": "Plan",
        "dev": "Dev",
        "reviewtest": "Review/Test",
        "done": "Done",
    }
    STAGE_STATUSES: "dict[str, list[str]]" = {
        "backlog": [],
        "spec": ["in_progress", "review", "done"],
        "plan": ["in_progress", "review", "done"],
        "dev": ["in_progress", "review", "done"],
        "reviewtest": ["in_progress", "agent_tested", "accepted"],
        "done": [],
    }
    PRIORITIES = ["high", "medium", "low"]
    MAX_ENTRIES = 5000
    
    
    class CliError(Exception):
        def __init__(self, msg: str, code: int = 1) -> None:
            super().__init__(msg)
            self.code = code
    
    
    # --- state server -----------------------------------------------------------
    
    
    def _request(path: str, method: str = "GET", body: dict | None = None) -> dict:
        data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            f"{DEFAULT_URL}{path}",
            data=data,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            method=method,
        )
        try:

    async function passOnce() {
      await sweepExpiredClaims();
    
      const [{ data: board }, { data: projects }, { data: roles }, { data: claims }] =
        await Promise.all([

      const attempts = claims.attempts || {};
      const roleById = new Map((roles.roles || []).map((r) => [r?.id, r]));
      const running = new Map(); // roleId -> live claims held now
      for (const c of Object.values(live)) {
        const rid = c.roleId || String(c.agentName || '').split(':').slice(1).join(':');
        if (rid) running.set(rid, (running.get(rid) || 0) + 1);
      }
    
      const results = [];
      const taken = new Map(); // roleId -> cards started this pass
      for (const card of board.cards || []) {
        const stage = card?.stage;
        if (stage === 'done' || stage === 'backlog') continue;
        if (card?.blocked || card?.cancelled) continue;
        // Cards managed by the execution core (U2+) are dispatched through the
        // managed lifecycle — the legacy runner must never claim them, even if a
        // stale row somehow advertises a dispatchable stage.
        if (isManagedCard(card)) continue;
        const roleId = (roles.stageRoles || {})[stage];
        if (!roleId) continue;
        const role = roleById.get(roleId);
        if (!role || !role.cli) continue;
        if (live[card.id]) continue;

        if ((Number(attempts[card.id]) || 0) >= maxAttempts) {

          } catch (e) {
            console.error(`mark ${card.id}: ${e.message}`);
          }
          results.push({ card: card.id, skipped: 'retries-exhausted' });
          continue;
        }
        const maxC = Number(role.maxConcurrent) >= 1 ? Math.floor(Number(role.maxConcurrent)) : 1;
        if ((running.get(roleId) || 0) + (taken.get(roleId) || 0) >= maxC) continue;

      runner:
        <<: *node
        # U1: fixed uid matching the mounted host user — porch refuses control of
        # run dirs owned by a different uid, and root-owned files inside ~/.pi,
        # ~/.codex or ~/.local/share/devin would break the host CLIs.
        user: "1001:1001"
        command: ["node", "/repo/server/acp-runner.mjs", "--serve"]
        environment:
          HOME: /home/hermes
          PATH: /home/hermes/.local/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
          STATE_URL: http://127.0.0.1:25900
          ROOT_DIR: /home/hermes/projects
          RUNNER_ID: host-runner
          # U3 (prepared): must equal the state's ACP_WORKSPACE_DIR — the same
          # absolute path is visible in both namespaces via the projects mount.
          ACP_WORKSPACE_DIR: /home/hermes/projects/.acp-workspaces
          # Persistent execution root for porch registry/output/attempt dirs.
          ACP_EXEC_DIR: /home/hermes/.hermes/acp-ui-state/execution
        # Volumes REPLACE the anchor list, so repeat it and add runner-only mounts:
        # ~/.codex (Codex auth + session store) and ~/.gitconfig (commit identity).
        volumes:
          - .:/repo:ro
          - /home/hermes/projects:/home/hermes/projects:rw
          - /home/hermes/.local:/home/hermes/.local:rw
          - /home/hermes/.pi:/home/hermes/.pi:rw
          - /home/hermes/.hermes:/home/hermes/.hermes:rw

      async function tick() {
        await snapshotLoad();
        // Late predecessor deaths: a peer alive at first load is re-probed
        // every tick — when it dies, its tracked work + journal spool are
        // inherited for draining instead of orphaned.
        await scanPredecessors();
        try {
          await ensureRegistered();
        } catch (e) {
          // Registration's transport failure IS an API outage — supervise owned
          // work locally, launch nothing.
          if (isOutageError(e)) {
            if (!outage) { outage = true; outageSince = now(); }
            return outageTick();
          }
          throw e;
        }
        let listing;
        try {
          listing = await client.listCards();
        } catch (e) {
          if (isOutageError(e)) {
            if (!outage) { outage = true; outageSince = now(); }
            return outageTick();
          }
          throw e;
        }
        if (outage) {
          // API is back — replay before resuming normal scheduling.
          outage = false;
          await replayJournal();
          outageSince = null;
        } else if (journalEntries.length || inheritedSpools.size) {
          // Retained entries (unproven resolves, not-yet-adopted ownership) are
          // retried on EVERY tick until drained — retention is not expiry.
          await replayJournal();
        }
        const out = { cards: 0 };
        for (const c of listing?.cards || []) {
          let card = null;
          try {
            card = await client.getCard(c.cardId);
          } catch (e) {
            // A mid-loop API loss is still an outage — enter outage mode instead
            // of aborting the tick and dropping the owned-work supervision pass.
            if (isOutageError(e)) {
              outage = true;
              outageSince = outageSince ?? now();
              out.outage = true;
              break;
            }
            throw e;
          }
          if (!card) continue;
          out.cards += 1;
          for (const rs of card.runs || []) {
            // Dispatch reaches terminal runs that still hold live attempt/
            // validation reservations — driveRun drains those groups and never
            // issues new work for a terminal run.
            if (!runNeedsDrive(rs)) continue;
            try {
              await driveRun(card, rs, out);
            } catch (e) {
              if (isOutageError(e)) {
                outage = true;
                outageSince = outageSince ?? now();
                out.outage = true;
                break; // stop launching immediately; owned attempts keep local state
              }
              out.errors = out.errors || [];
              out.errors.push({ cardId: card.cardId, runId: rs.id, error: String(e?.message || e) });
            }
          }
        }
        await snapshotWrite();
        if (journalDegraded) {
          // Externally observable on EVERY tick — a degraded journal gates
          // launches and must be diagnosable even when nothing tried to launch.
          out.journal_degraded = true;
          if (lastJournalError) out.journal_error = lastJournalError;
        }
        return out;
      }

    // Managed execution driver (U5, default OFF).
    //
    // Gate: ACP_EXEC_START=1. When unset this file behaves exactly as before —
    // no client, no runtime, no timers are created. The pump is an INDEPENDENT
    // serial tick source that runs CONCURRENTLY with the legacy pass: passOnce()
    // may sit inside runCard for hours, and managed heartbeats / observation /
    // cancel / check settlement / journal replay still happen on every tick.
    //
    //   * Timer chaining (never setInterval) makes overlapping ticks impossible:
    //     the next tick is scheduled only after the in-flight one settles.
    //   * A tick failure is logged and retried at the next interval — it never
    //     kills legacy dispatch, and a legacy failure never stops the pump.
    //   * API outages are handled INSIDE the scheduler (snapshot + local
    //     supervision only); the pump needs no outage logic of its own.
    //   * stop() drops the pending timer and waits a bounded time for the
    //     in-flight tick. It NEVER marks managed work terminal — durable
    //     reservations live on the server and a successor adopts them after a
    //     positive death/environment proof (U4). SIGTERM is not a resolve.
    //   * stop-all / release-all / cancel act on claims.json + liveProcs only —
    //     managed runs hold no legacy claims, so legacy cranks can never
    //     impersonate a managed lifecycle stop.
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    const MANAGED_DEFAULT_TICK_MS = 5_000;
    const MANAGED_STOP_DRAIN_MS = 15_000;
    
    function truthyEnv(v) {
      return /^(1|true|yes|on)$/i.test(String(v ?? ''));
    }
    
    // Serial bounded tick pump. Exported + timer-injectable for tests.
    export function createManagedPump({
      tick,
      intervalMs = MANAGED_DEFAULT_TICK_MS,
      onError = (e) => console.error(`managed tick: ${e?.message || e}`),
      setTimeoutFn = setTimeout,
      clearTimeoutFn = clearTimeout,
    } = {}) {
      if (typeof tick !== 'function') throw new Error('managed pump requires a tick');
      let timer = null;
      let running = false;
      let inFlight = null;
      let ticks = 0;
      let errors = 0;
    
      function schedule() {
        if (!running || timer || inFlight) return;
        timer = setTimeoutFn(fire, intervalMs);
        // Never let the pump alone keep the process alive — the serve loop or an
        // in-flight legacy pass decides liveness.
        if (timer && typeof timer.unref === 'function') timer.unref();
      }
    
      function fire() {
        if (timer) { clearTimeoutFn(timer); timer = null; }
        if (inFlight) return inFlight; // serialization: no overlap, ever
        inFlight = (async () => {
          try {
            await tick();
          } catch (e) {
            errors++;
            try { onError(e); } catch { /* the pump's error path must itself survive */ }
          } finally {
            ticks++;
            inFlight = null;
            schedule();
          }
        })();
        return inFlight;
      }
    
      return {
        start() {
          if (running) return;
          running = true;
          fire(); // first tick now — later ones ride the timer chain
        },
        async stop({ drainMs = MANAGED_STOP_DRAIN_MS } = {}) {
          running = false;
          if (timer) { clearTimeoutFn(timer); timer = null; }
          if (!inFlight) return { ticks, errors, drained: true };
          // Bounded drain: a wedged tick must not hang shutdown. A dropped wait
          // is NOT a dropped reservation — the server's durable records outlive
          // the process either way.
          await Promise.race([
            inFlight.catch(() => {}),
            new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, Math.max(0, drainMs))),
          ]);
          return { ticks, errors, drained: !inFlight };
        },
        fire, // test seam: drive one serialized tick without a timer
        ticks: () => ticks,
        errors: () => errors,
        running: () => running,
        inFlight: () => !!inFlight,
      };
    }
    
    // Build the managed driver. Returns {enabled:false} when the gate is off —
    // callers can start()/stop() it unconditionally. Every production dependency
    // is injectable for tests (client/transport/runtime/scheduler/pump/timers).
    export async function createManagedDriver(deps = {}) {
      const env = deps.env ?? process.env;
      const enabled = deps.enabled ?? truthyEnv(env.ACP_EXEC_START);
      const runnerId = deps.runnerId ?? RUNNER_ID;
      const driver = {
        enabled,
        runnerId,
        scheduler: null,
        pump: null,
        async start() {},
        async stop() { return { ticks: 0, errors: 0, drained: true }; },
        async tickOnce() { return null; },
        stats: () => ({ ticks: 0, errors: 0 }),
        describe: () => ({ enabled, runnerId, state: 'disabled' }),
      };
      if (!enabled) return driver;
    
      const stateDir = deps.stateDir
        ?? resolve(env.STATE_DIR || join(homedir(), '.hermes', 'acp-ui-state'));
      const client = deps.client
        ?? (deps.clientFactory ?? createInternalClient)({
          baseUrl: deps.baseUrl ?? env.ACP_EXEC_API_URL ?? STATE_URL,
          stateDir,
          transport: deps.transport,
        });
      const runtime = deps.runtime
        ?? (deps.runtimeFactory ?? createPorchRuntime)({ env });
      const scheduler = deps.scheduler
        ?? (deps.schedulerFactory ?? createManagedScheduler)({
          client,
          runtime,
          runnerId,
          instanceId: deps.instanceId,
          leaseMs: deps.leaseMs,
          stateDir,
          env,
          validationEnabled: deps.validationEnabled ?? null,
          now: deps.now,
          hooks: deps.hooks,
        });
      const tickMs = deps.tickMs
        ?? Math.max(250, Number(env.ACP_EXEC_TICK_MS) || MANAGED_DEFAULT_TICK_MS);
      const pump = deps.pump ?? createManagedPump({
        tick: () => scheduler.tick(),
        intervalMs: tickMs,
        onError: deps.onTickError,
        setTimeoutFn: deps.setTimeoutFn,
        clearTimeoutFn: deps.clearTimeoutFn,
      });
      const validation = deps.validationEnabled ?? env.ACP_EXEC_VALIDATION === '1';
    
      driver.scheduler = scheduler;
      driver.pump = pump;
      driver.start = async () => {
        // Runtime-level startup evidence: who we are and what the gates are —
        // no secrets, no tokens.
        console.error(
          `managed execution: enabled runner=${runnerId} `
          + `instance=${scheduler.instanceId} tick=${tickMs}ms `
          + `validation=${validation ? 'on' : 'off'} stateDir=${stateDir}`,
        );
        pump.start();
      };
      driver.stop = (opts) => pump.stop(opts);
      driver.tickOnce = () => pump.fire();
      driver.stats = () => ({ ticks: pump.ticks(), errors: pump.errors() });
      driver.describe = () => ({
        enabled: true,
        runnerId,
        instanceId: scheduler.instanceId,
        validation: validation ? 'on' : 'off',
        tickMs,
        ticks: pump.ticks(),
        tickErrors: pump.errors(),
      });
      return driver;
    }
    
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Entry — runOnce/runServe are exported with injected seams so tests drive the
    // exact production path; importing this module runs nothing.
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    // --once: one legacy pass WITH the managed pump active beside it. On exit the
    // pump stops (bounded drain) — managed work launched or observed during the
    // pass stays durably reserved on the server, never silently terminalized.
    export async function runOnce({ passOnceImpl = passOnce, driver = null } = {}) {
      const d = driver ?? (await createManagedDriver());
      try {
        if (d.enabled) await d.start();
        const results = await passOnceImpl();
        console.log(JSON.stringify({ ok: true, runs: results, managed: d.describe() }, null, 2));
      } catch (e) {
        console.error(`runner: ${e.message}`);
        process.exitCode = 1;
      } finally {
        await d.stop();
      }
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Entry — runOnce/runServe are exported with injected seams so tests drive the
    // exact production path; importing this module runs nothing.
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    // --once is a LEGACY-ONLY bounded pass. With the managed gate on it refuses
    // outright (before any client/runtime/scheduler exists): a single pass would
    // launch managed work and then stop supervising it — observation, check
    // settlement and cancellation would be orphaned until another runner
    // appeared. Managed execution requires --serve, whose pump stays alive for
    // the whole process lifetime. With the gate off, --once is exactly the
    // historical single legacy pass.
    export async function runOnce({
      passOnceImpl = passOnce,
      driver = null,
      env = process.env,
    } = {}) {
      const managedWanted = driver ? driver.enabled
        : truthyEnv(env.ACP_EXEC_START);
      if (managedWanted) {
        console.error(
          'runner: --once is a bounded legacy-only pass — managed execution '
          + '(ACP_EXEC_START=1) requires --serve so launched work stays '
          + 'supervised; refusing instead of orphaning it');
        process.exitCode = 2;
        return;
      }
      const d = driver ?? (await createManagedDriver({ env }));
      try {
        const results = await passOnceImpl();
        console.log(JSON.stringify({ ok: true, runs: results, managed: d.describe() }, null, 2));
      } catch (e) {
        console.error(`runner: ${e.message}`);
        process.exitCode = 1;
      } finally {
        await d.stop();
      }
    }
    
    export async function runServe({
      passOnceImpl = passOnce,
      driver = null,
      pollImpl = pollIntervalMs,
      setTimeoutFn = setTimeout,
      registerSignals = null, // (onSig) -> unsubscribe; default installs SIGINT/SIGTERM
    } = {}) {
      const d = driver ?? (await createManagedDriver());
      let stopped = false;
      const onSig = (sig) => {
        if (stopped) process.exit(0);
        stopped = true;
        console.error(`runner: ${sig}, stopping after this pass…`);
      };
      let unsubscribe = () => {};
      if (registerSignals === null) {
        const handlers = ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM'].map((sig) => {
          const h = () => onSig(sig);
          process.on(sig, h);
          return [sig, h];
        });
        unsubscribe = () => { for (const [sig, h] of handlers) process.off(sig, h); };
      } else {
        unsubscribe = registerSignals(onSig) || (() => {});
      }
      try {
        if (d.enabled) await d.start();
        while (!stopped) {
          try {
            const results = await passOnceImpl();
            const ran = results.filter((r) => !r.skipped && !r.dryRun && !r.error).length;
            if (ran) console.log(JSON.stringify({ at: new Date().toISOString(), runs: results }));
          } catch (e) {
            console.error(`runner: ${e.message}`);
          }
          if (stopped) break;
          const waitMs = await pollImpl();
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeoutFn(r, waitMs));
        }
      } finally {
        unsubscribe();
        await d.stop();
      }

    // Deterministic timer wheel: setTimeout callbacks fire only when advance()
    // moves the clock. Handles mimic the unref'd Node Timeout interface.
    function fakeTimers() {
      let now = 0;
      let seq = 0;
      const queue = new Map();
      const setTimeoutFn = (fn, ms) => {
        const id = ++seq;
        queue.set(id, { at: now + (Number(ms) || 0), fn });
        return { id, unref() {} };
      };
      const clearTimeoutFn = (t) => { if (t) queue.delete(t.id); };
      const advance = (ms) => {
        const target = now + ms;
        for (;;) {
          let nid = null;
          let at = Infinity;
          for (const [id, t] of queue) {
            if (t.at <= target && t.at < at) { at = t.at; nid = id; }
          }
          if (nid === null) break;
          now = at;
          const f = queue.get(nid).fn;
          queue.delete(nid);
          f();
        }
        now = target;
      };
      return {
        now: () => now,
        setTimeoutFn,
        clearTimeoutFn,
        advance,
        pending: () => queue.size,
      };
    }
    
    // Let queued microtasks/async continuations settle between timer advances.
    const flush = () => new Promise((r) => setImmediate(r));

      return { kind: 'fake-client', calls: [] };
    }
    function fakeRuntime() {
      return { kind: 'fake-runtime' };
    }

    +    ({error, code, ...}) instead of raising so command paths can inspect the

    +            return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read() or b"{}")

    export const FINDINGS_FILE = 'review_findings.json';
    export const VERDICTS_FILE = 'review_verdict.json';
    
    export function buildReviewerPrompt({
      cardId, cardTitle, runId, attemptId, copyDir, round, resultSha256,
      requirementsText, planText,
    }) {
      const lines = [];
      lines.push('# Managed review pass');
      lines.push('');
      lines.push('You are the reviewer of a managed card run. You are looking at');
      lines.push('an ISOLATED COPY of the result — your edits here never reach the');
      lines.push('canonical workspace. Review, do not implement.');
      lines.push('');
      lines.push('## Identity');
      lines.push(`- card: ${cardId}${cardTitle ? ` — ${cardTitle}` : ''}`);
      lines.push(`- run: ${runId}`);
      lines.push(`- attempt: ${attemptId}`);
      lines.push(`- review copy: ${copyDir}`);
      lines.push(`- round: ${round}`);
      lines.push(`- result: ${resultSha256}`);
      lines.push('');
      lines.push('## Approved requirements (verbatim)');
      lines.push('');
      lines.push(requirementsText.trimEnd());
      lines.push('');
      lines.push('## Approved plan (verbatim)');
      lines.push('');
      lines.push(planText.trimEnd());
      lines.push('');
      lines.push('## Your output contract');
      lines.push('');
      lines.push(`Write \`.acp-out/${FINDINGS_FILE}\` in this copy — JSON:`);
      lines.push('```');
      lines.push(JSON.stringify({
        version: 1, round, resultSha256,
        findings: [{ id: 'f1', round, severity: 'critical|major|minor|nit', text: '…', where: 'path:line', status: 'open' }],
      }, null, 2));
      lines.push('```');
      lines.push('- severities: critical|major block; minor|nit are kept as notes.');
      lines.push('- An empty findings list is a valid "no findings" verdict.');
      lines.push('- Do not modify the reviewed sources — only write the doc.');
      lines.push('');
      return lines.join('\n');
    }
    
    export function buildCheckerPrompt({
      cardId, cardTitle, runId, attemptId, copyDir, round, resultSha256,
      findingsDoc,
    }) {
      const lines = [];
      lines.push('# Managed checker pass');
      lines.push('');
      lines.push('You are the checker of a managed card run. You see a SEPARATE');
      lines.push('pristine copy of the result plus the reviewer\'s findings — vet');
      lines.push('each finding against the actual code.');
      lines.push('');
      lines.push('## Identity');
      lines.push(`- card: ${cardId}${cardTitle ? ` — ${cardTitle}` : ''}`);
      lines.push(`- run: ${runId}`);
      lines.push(`- attempt: ${attemptId}`);
      lines.push(`- check copy: ${copyDir}`);
      lines.push(`- round: ${round}`);
      lines.push(`- result: ${resultSha256}`);
      lines.push('');
      lines.push('## Reviewer findings under review (verbatim, verified import)');
      lines.push('');
      lines.push(JSON.stringify(findingsDoc, null, 2));
      lines.push('');
      lines.push('## Your output contract');
      lines.push('');
      lines.push(`Write \`.acp-out/${VERDICTS_FILE}\` in this copy — JSON:`);
      lines.push('```');
      lines.push(JSON.stringify({
        version: 1, round, resultSha256,
        verdicts: [{ findingId: 'f1', verdict: 'confirmed|rejected|disputed', reason: '…' }],
      }, null, 2));
      lines.push('```');
      lines.push('- vet EVERY finding id — a finding you skip stays unvetted and');
      lines.push('  still gates the result.');
      lines.push('- rejected = the finding is wrong; confirmed/disputed = stands.');
      lines.push('');
      return lines.join('\n');
    }
    
    // The fix prompt is the implementer prompt PLUS the complete verified gate

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    """u5_boardctl_managed_selftest.py — U5 boardctl managed-surface tests.
    
    Imports the real `scripts/boardctl` module and drives `main(argv)` with the
    HTTP layer stubbed — `_request` serves board/claims docs, `_exec_request`
    records and answers the /api/execution routes. Asserts:
    
      * `review <managed>` reads the card view + run record through
        /api/execution and renders the run's verified evidence — never touches
        .acp/cards files;
      * every file-write review flag (--round/--close/--sync) and review-check
        are refused on managed cards BEFORE any request is made;
      * `accept` binds the exact recorded runId + resultSha256 through the
        user-channel command POST, retries revision_conflict with a fresh
        revision, and refuses a non-awaiting run without posting;
      * `stop` posts the never-gated stop command;
      * move/claim/rm/flag/set --stage are refused on managed rows;
      * legacy paths (review-check file write, move, set) still work —
        no managed card regressions;
      * no internal token / offline managed state: the module must not read
        BOARD_STATE_DIR/STATE_DIR nor send the internal token header.
    
    Run: python3 scripts/u5_boardctl_managed_selftest.py
    """

    class Transport:
        """Stubbed HTTP layer: serves /api/state docs + /api/execution views and
        records every call. `script` maps (method, path-prefix) → queue of
        (status, payload)."""
        def __init__(self, board_cards=None, script=None):
            self.calls = []          # (method, path, body)
            self.exec_calls = []     # (method, exec_path, body)
            self.board = {"version": 2, "cards": board_cards or []}
            self.script = dict(script or {})
            self.puts = []
    
        def request(self, path, method="GET", body=None):
            self.calls.append((method, path, body))
            if path == "/api/state/board.json" and method == "GET":
                return {"data": self.board, "rev": 1}
            if path == "/api/state/claims.json" and method == "GET":
                return {"data": {"version": 1, "claims": {}}, "rev": 1}
            if path == "/api/state/activity.json" and method == "GET":
                return {"data": {"entries": [], "usage": []}, "rev": 1}
            if path == "/api/state/roles.json" and method == "GET":
                return {"data": {"version": 1, "roles": [], "stageRoles": {}}, "rev": 1}
            if path == "/api/state/projects.json" and method == "GET":
                return {"data": {"version": 1, "projects": []}, "rev": 1}
            if method == "PUT":
                self.puts.append((path, body))
                if path == "/api/state/board.json":
                    self.board = body["data"]
                return {"rev": body["rev"] + 1}
            return {"data": {}, "rev": 0}
    
        def exec_request(self, path, method="GET", body=None):
            self.exec_calls.append((method, path, body))
            for key in list(self.script):
                m, prefix = key.split(" ", 1)
                if method == m and path.startswith(prefix):
                    q = self.script[key]
                    out = q.pop(0) if isinstance(q, list) else q

    await test('runServe: pump ticks during blocked pass; injected SIGTERM stops, never terminalizes', async () => {
      const t = fakeTimers();
      let ticks = 0;
      const calls = [];
      const scheduler = {
        instanceId: 'inst-serve',
        tick: async () => { ticks++; calls.push('tick'); },
      };
      const driver = await createManagedDriver({
        enabled: true,
        client: fakeClient(),
        runtime: fakeRuntime(),
        scheduler,
        tickMs: 250,
        setTimeoutFn: t.setTimeoutFn,
        clearTimeoutFn: t.clearTimeoutFn,
        onTickError: () => {},
      });
      let onSig = null;
      let passCount = 0;
      let releasePass = null;
      const p = runServe({
        passOnceImpl: async () => {
          passCount++;
          if (passCount === 1) {
            // First pass sits blocked like a long runCard — managed ticks must flow.
            await new Promise((r) => { releasePass = r; });
          }
          return [];
        },
        driver,
        pollImpl: async () => 1000,
        setTimeoutFn: t.setTimeoutFn,
        registerSignals: (fn) => { onSig = fn; return () => {}; },
      });
      await flush();
      await drive(t, 8, 250); // pump ticks while the legacy pass is blocked
      assert.ok(ticks >= 8, `ticks while legacy pass blocked: ${ticks}`);
      // SIGTERM lands while the legacy pass is STILL blocked — the pump must
      // quiesce immediately, not when the pass returns.
      onSig('SIGTERM');
      await flush();
      const atSignal = ticks;
      await drive(t, 6, 1000); // pass still blocked — zero new managed ticks
      assert.equal(ticks, atSignal,
        'pump kept ticking after the signal while the pass was blocked');
      releasePass();          // let the legacy pass finish → loop sees stopped
      await drive(t, 2, 1500);
      await p;
      assert.ok(passCount >= 1);
      assert.deepEqual([...new Set(calls)], ['tick'],
        'scheduler only ever saw tick() — shutdown never terminalized anything');
      await drive(t, 4, 1000);
      assert.equal(ticks, atSignal, 'no ticks after shutdown');
    });
    
    await test('stop before the deferred first tick runs zero work', async () => {
      // start() queues the first tick as a microtask — a stop landing before it
      // must drop it: nothing was ever launched, so nothing is owed.

    // The internal token lives at <stateDir>/execution/internal-token and the
    // porch exec store is ACP_EXEC_DIR (default <stateDir>/execution) — both must
    // resolve to the SAME root or the driver would read one store and hold auth
    // for another. Explicit STATE_DIR wins; ACP_EXEC_DIR alone implies its
    // parent; both set inconsistently is a config fault — fail closed.
    export function resolveManagedStateDir(env = process.env) {
      const stateDir = String(env.STATE_DIR || '').trim()
        ? resolve(env.STATE_DIR.trim()) : null;
      const execDir = String(env.ACP_EXEC_DIR || '').trim()
        ? resolve(env.ACP_EXEC_DIR.trim()) : null;
      if (stateDir && execDir && join(stateDir, 'execution') !== execDir) {
        throw new Error(
          `managed config inconsistent: STATE_DIR=${stateDir} vs ACP_EXEC_DIR=${execDir}`
          + ' (must equal <stateDir>/execution) — refusing a split store');
      }
      return stateDir ?? (execDir ? resolve(execDir, '..') : null)
        ?? resolve(join(homedir(), '.hermes', 'acp-ui-state'));
    }

    // is injectable for tests (client/transport/runtime/scheduler/pump/timers),
    // and every env value is read from the supplied env, not the module snapshot.
    export async function createManagedDriver(deps = {}) {
      const env = deps.env ?? process.env;

      const runnerId = deps.runnerId ?? env.RUNNER_ID ?? RUNNER_ID;
      const driver = {
        enabled,
        runnerId,
        scheduler: null,
        pump: null,
        async start() {},
        async stop() { return { ticks: 0, errors: 0, drained: true }; },
        async tickOnce() { return null; },
        stats: () => ({ ticks: 0, errors: 0 }),
        describe: () => ({ enabled, runnerId, state: 'disabled' }),
      };
      if (!enabled) return driver;

      const client = deps.client

      // Runner quiesce (process shutdown, not a user stop): forbids EVERY new
      // piece of work — begin_attempt, begin_validation, check spawns both
      // pre-intent and post-intent — and drains what we already own:
      //   - in-flight check groups are cancelled through the same kill path as
      //     a user stop (positive group-death proof still required);
      //   - recorded proc outcomes are still reported durably;
      //   - the validation RESERVATION is retained for successor adoption —
      //     a dying runner never marks it terminal on its own say-so.
      // Nothing is resolved by the flag itself; durable duties keep replaying.
      let quiesced = false;
      function quiesce() { quiesced = true; }
      // Bounded wait for in-flight validation tasks after quiesce — returns
      // honestly about what is still pending; never resolves or drops duties.
      async function drain(ms = 15000) {
        const inflight = [...valTasks.values()];
        if (!inflight.length) return { drained: 0, pending: 0 };
        let timer = null;
        await Promise.race([
          Promise.allSettled(inflight),
          new Promise((res) => { timer = setTimeout(res, ms); timer.unref?.(); }),
        ]).finally(() => clearTimeout(timer));
        return { drained: inflight.length - valTasks.size, pending: valTasks.size };
      }

        try {
          return await send(card, 'end_validation', {
            runId: run.id, validationId: valId, outcome,
            ...(reason ? { reason: String(reason).slice(0, 300) } : {}),
            ...self(),
          }, `ev-${valId}-${outcome}`);

            }, `ev-${valId}-unproven`);

    // reservation is RETAINED 'active' for successor adoption — never resolved
    // by a dying runner.
    // ============================================================================
    
    test('U5 quiesce: runServe SIGTERM drains the owned check group, spawns nothing new', async () => {
      const env = await mkEnv();
      const { svc, projectDir, stateDir } = env;
      await seedBase(svc, projectDir, [cardFixture('card-a')]);
      const gate = join(stateDir, 'gate-a');
      const marker2 = join(stateDir, 'check2-ran');
      const runId = await mkValidationRun(svc, 'card-a', [
        { run: `until [ -f '${gate}' ]; do sleep 0.1; done; echo done`, timeoutSec: 60 },
        { run: `echo ran > '${marker2}'`, timeoutSec: 30 },
      ]);
      const { sched, runtime } = mkSched(env);
      // The REAL production driver — injected with the real scheduler+client so
      // d.stop() exercises quiesce → pump stop → bounded task drain.
      const driver = await createManagedDriver({
        enabled: true,
        env: { RUNNER_ID: 'host-runner' },
        stateDir,
        client: mkClient(svc, stateDir),
        runtime,
        scheduler: sched,
        tickMs: 60,
      });
      let releasePass;
      const passGate = new Promise((res) => { releasePass = res; });
      let sigFn = null;
      const serve = runServe({
        driver,
        passOnceImpl: async () => { await passGate; return []; },
        registerSignals: (onSig) => { sigFn = onSig; return () => {}; },
        pollImpl: async () => 50,
      });
      // The production pump drives the run — poll until check-0's real group is
      // durably recorded (spawn already happened at that point).
      let rec = null;
      for (let i = 0; i < 300 && !rec; i += 1) {
        const rv = await runView(svc, runId);
        for (const p of Object.values(rv.validation?.procs || {})) {
          if (p?.leader?.pgid) livePgroups.add(p);
        }
        const p0 = rv.validation?.procs?.['0'];
        if (p0?.state === 'recorded') rec = p0;
        if (!rec) await sleep(60);
      }
      assert.ok(rec?.leader?.pgid, 'check-0 group durably recorded before the signal');
      try {
        sigFn('SIGTERM'); // legacy pass still blocked — quiesce must not wait for it
        // Drain is async inside driver.stop; poll the authoritative record until
        // the owned group is reported settled with a positive kill proof.
        let v = null;
        for (let i = 0; i < 250; i += 1) {
          v = (await runView(svc, runId)).validation;
          if (v?.procs?.['0']?.state === 'settled') break;
          await sleep(60);
        }
        const p0 = v?.procs?.['0'];
        assert.equal(p0?.state, 'settled', `check-0 must settle: ${J(v?.procs)}`);
        assert.equal(p0?.proof?.groupDead, true, 'positive group-death proof required');
        // Direct OS proof — no member of the recorded pgid survives.
        assert.deepEqual(procGroupMembers(p0.leader.pgid) || [], [],
          'recorded process group is verifiably empty');
        livePgroups.delete(rec);
        assert.equal(v.status, 'active',
          'reservation retained for successor adoption — a dying runner never resolves it');
        assert.equal(v.owner.instanceId, sched.instanceId, 'recorded owner unchanged');
        // Check-1 NEVER spawned: no proc, no report, no side-effect marker.
        assert.ok(!v.procs?.['1'], 'check-1 intent/spawn never issued');
        assert.equal((v.checks?.reports || []).length, 1, 'only the cancelled check reported');
        assert.equal(v.checks.reports[0].status, 'cancelled');
        await assert.rejects(fs.access(marker2), /ENOENT/, 'check-2 marker absent');
        // No reviewer/checker/fix attempt ever launched — implementer only.
        const starts = runtime._calls.filter((c) => c.m === 'start');
        assert.equal(starts.length, 1, `only the implementer launched: ${J(starts.map((s) => s.a?.profileId))}`);
        // Pump stopped + quiesced: real time passes, ZERO further launches.
        assert.equal(sched.quiesced(), true);
        await sleep(400);
        assert.equal(runtime._calls.filter((c) => c.m === 'start').length, 1,
          'no fresh launch after quiesce');
      } finally {
        await fs.writeFile(gate, 'x').catch(() => {});
        releasePass();
        await serve;
        if (rec) { await killRecordedGroup(rec); livePgroups.delete(rec); }
      }
    });
    
    // The same fence proven from the other side: quiesce landing BETWEEN the
    // durable begin_attempt row and runtime.start must still never launch —
    // the attempt reconciles through the never-entered contract.
    test('U5 quiesce: fence between begin_attempt and runtime.start never launches', async () => {
      const env = await mkEnv();
      const { svc, projectDir } = env;
      await seedBase(svc, projectDir);
      const runId = await mkValidationRun(svc, 'card-a', [{ run: 'echo ok', timeoutSec: 30 }]);
      const box = {};
      const { sched, runtime } = mkSched(env, {
        hooks: {
          // Deterministic signal point: the durable attempt row exists, the
          // runtime has NOT been invoked — exactly the race window.
          onAttemptDurable: async () => { box.sched.quiesce(); },
        },
      });
      box.sched = sched;
      const r = await drive(svc, sched, runId, (x) => (x.attempts || []).length > 0);
      assert.equal(r.attempts[0].status, 'active', 'attempt row landed durable');
      // Let the resolve settle — then prove nothing ever reached the runtime.
      await drive(svc, sched, runId, (x) => (x.attempts?.[0]?.status ?? '') !== 'active');
      const r2 = await runView(svc, runId);
      assert.equal(runtime._calls.filter((c) => c.m === 'start').length, 0,
        'runtime.start NEVER invoked');
      assert.notEqual(r2.attempts[0].status, 'active',
        `never-entered attempt reconciled: ${r2.attempts[0].status}`);
      assert.match(String(r2.attempts[0].reason ?? ''), /never entered|cancel/);
      // Post-quiesce ticks issue zero further work.
      const out = await sched.tick();
      assert.equal(runtime._calls.filter((c) => c.m === 'start').length, 0,
        `still zero launches: ${J(out)}`);
    });

      await seedBase(svc, projectDir, [
        cardFixture('card-b', { order: 5 }), cardFixture('card-a', { order: 10 }),
      ]);
      await saveSchedulerLimits(stateDir, {
        global: 1, roles: { implementer: 1, reviewer: 1, checker: 1 },
      });
      const runA = await mkValidationRun(svc, 'card-a', [{ run: 'echo ok', timeoutSec: 30 }]);
      const { sched, runtime } = mkSched(env, {
        behaviors: { byProfile: { 'acp-reviewer': { outcome: 'failed', delayMs: 3 } } },
      });

          console.error(`runner: managed quiesce failed: ${e?.message || e}`);

        let taskDrain = null;
        try {
          taskDrain = await scheduler.drain?.(drainMs);

    // ============================================================================
    // Stop during a running check: user stop lands mid-execution, the scheduler
    // cancels only its proven group, the run finishes cancelled.
    // ============================================================================
    
    test('U5 stop during a running check drains the proven group', async () => {
      const env = await mkEnv();
      const { svc, projectDir } = env;
      await seedBase(svc, projectDir);
      const runId = await mkValidationRun(svc, 'card-a', [
        { run: 'echo start && sleep 60', timeoutSec: 90 },
      ]);
      const { sched } = mkSched(env);
      let proc = null;
      try {
        const run = await drive(svc, sched, runId,
          (r) => r.validation?.phase === 'verify'
            && Object.values(r.validation?.procs || {}).some((p) => p?.leader?.pgid > 0));
        proc = Object.values(run.validation.procs)[0];
        assert.equal(proc.state, 'recorded');
        livePgroups.add(proc);
    
        const c = await getCard(svc, 'card-a');
        const st = await cmd(svc, 'card-a', {
          commandId: `stop-${randomUUID().slice(0, 6)}`, type: 'stop',
          expectedControlRevision: c.json.controlRevision,
          payload: { reason: 'test stop' },
        });
        assert.equal(st.status, 200, J(st.json));
    
        const after = await drive(svc, sched, runId, (r) => r.status === 'cancelled', { maxTicks: 120 });
        assert.equal(after.validation.status, 'cancelled');
        // Positive group death: the recorded pgid is verifiably gone.
        let dead = false;
        try { process.kill(-proc.leader.pgid, 0); } catch (e) { dead = e.code === 'ESRCH'; }
        assert.ok(dead, 'check process group is verifiably dead');
        livePgroups.delete(proc);
      } finally {
        if (proc) { await killRecordedGroup(proc); livePgroups.delete(proc); }
        await stopAndDrain(svc, sched, runId, 'card-a').catch(() => {});
      }
    });
    
    // ============================================================================
    // Domain barriers through the REAL authenticated internal path — each call
    // carries a fresh expectedInternalRevision so the refusal observed is the
    // ownership/evidence gate, not a revision rejection.
    // ============================================================================

          if (doc.instanceId !== srcInst) {

          // Same container, different instance: inherit ONLY when the recorded

          const probe = Number.isInteger(doc.pid)

          const dead = probe && probe.exists === true

              || (probe.readable && probe.starttime && doc.pidStarttime && probe.starttime !== doc.pidStarttime))
            : probe && probe.exists === false;
          if (!dead) continue;                                   // live/unknown — hands off
          // Two distinct one-shot consumptions per dead predecessor:
          //   consumedTracked — the tracked-work merge runs once (a retried
          //     scan must not resurrect entries already drained or adopted);
          //   seenPredecessors — marked only when the journal spool's state is
          //     KNOWN (read, or provably absent). An unreadable spool degrades
          //     and retries next tick — a transient EACCES can never orphan a
          //     pending duty.
          if (!consumedTracked.has(srcInst)) {
            consumedTracked.add(srcInst);
            for (const t of doc.tracked || []) {

                tracked.set(t.attemptId, {
                  ...t, owned: false, inheritedFrom: srcInst,
                });
              }
            }
          }
          // Recover the predecessor's own journal spool — durably drained
          // events/observations it recorded must not die with its instance.
          const spoolFile = join(journalDir, `u4-journal-${runnerId}-${srcInst}.jsonl`);
          let raw = null;

            if (e && e.code !== 'ENOENT') {

              }
              entry.srcInstance = srcInst;
              entries.push(entry);
            }
