    # A running container may predate the current spec's `user:` — the RUNNING
    # uid and the SPEC uid are recorded separately; they are different objects.
    state_uid=$(xstate 'id -u' 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
    echo "info  running state container uid=$state_uid (live identity, whatever it is)"
    runner_live_uid=$(dc exec -T runner id -u 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
    echo "info  running runner container uid=${runner_live_uid:-unavailable} (container start-time identity)"
    runner_spec_uid=$(xrun 'id -u' | tr -d '[:space:]')

        || bad "prepared spec missing ACP_EXEC_TOKEN_UID=1001"
    fi
    
    echo "== $PASS pass / $FAIL fail / $GAP expected-gap"
    [ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]

    ### Key Technical Decisions
    
    - **KTD1 — контейнерный backend.** Расширить интерфейс среды ядра, сохранив start/events/result/cancel/reconcile и публичные идентификаторы. Porch запускается и наблюдается в namespace своего worker-контейнера под одним UID. При недоступности контейнера нельзя читать одноимённый процесс из namespace runner. Использовать неизменяемые образы с зафиксированными CLI и зависимостями.
    - **KTD2 — доверенный контроллер среды.** Отдельный Compose-сервис владеет Docker socket; принимает от runner аутентифицированные команды по внутреннему каналу. Разрешены только зарегистрированные ресурсы и фиксированные профили ролей; никаких произвольных mounts/образов/команд Docker из пользовательского payload. Ни участники, ни process-backend solo не получают Docker socket или административный токен.
    - **KTD3 — отдельные материалы.** Worker получает собственный HOME, scoped credentials/config без общей истории CLI, собственные артефакты, проект и ролевые входы. Снимок панели — экспорт Git-дерева без ссылок на общий git-dir и execution-хранилище. Панель/судья имеют проект ro. Интегратор работает в приватном репозитории worker, подготовленном доверенным контроллером из выбранного снимка; git-dir автономный, без alternates, hardlinks и ссылок на общий repository. Каноническая ветка/worktree задачи остаётся у контроллера; перед проверками он импортирует полный результат, включая незакоммиченные, новые и удалённые файлы, и привязывает доказательства к этому снимку. Restart восстанавливает сопоставление private repository и канонической ветки без повторного импорта. Rootfs ro, рабочие tmp-каталоги отдельные, non-root, без privileged/host PID/host network, capabilities сняты.
    - **KTD4 — сеть и API.** Каждый участник изолирован от остальных и внутренних API. Egress — через шлюз с перечнем разрешённых провайдеров и поисковых сервисов; обращения к loopback/локальным/private адресам через DNS, IP или редирект блокируются. Сеть участников не даёт прямого обхода шлюза. Зависимости проекта готовит отдельная setup/validation-среда по принятым setup-командам и lockfiles, с явно разрешёнными package registries через шлюз. Контроллер только запускает этот scoped профиль; команды проекта не выполняются в доверенном сервисе с Docker socket. Материализованный набор/кеш привязывается к hash lockfiles и передаётся рабочим/validation-средам без доступа к чужим данным. Изменение lockfile требует новой подготовки. Failure setup не маскировать как успешный ответ Pi; участникам не выдавать произвольный egress. Доступ к Docker и API артефактов панели отсутствует у интегратора. Обновление credentials не должно открывать общую историю.
    - **KTD5 — результаты и фазы.** Добавить Run.mode=fusion, resultKind=document|implementation, фазы panel/judge/integrate плюс гейты ядра. Хранить структурированный ответ с Markdown-представлением и ссылками на доказательства. Сервер валидирует полноту; изменение области наряда требует явного вердикта судьи, при сомнении ожидание пользователя. LLM-вердикт не считать доказательством изоляции.
    - **KTD6 — состояние и UI.** Расширять server/execution и API ядра. retry_participant, exclude_panelist и approve_work_order проходят команды карточки с commandId/expectedControlRevision; устаревшее согласование наряда отклоняется. Детали managed-запуска отделены от ACP-чата и внешнего reader porch.
    
    Основание границы Docker: [Docker Engine security](https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/). Контроль daemon предоставляет возможности изменения файлов хоста; доступ принадлежит только доверенному сервису. Реальная совместимость CLI с этой средой проверяется F1, а не предполагается из наличия Docker.
    
    ### Assumptions и Defaults
    
    Два панелиста по умолчанию; модели выбираются явно из настроенного состава. Две попытки на роль, максимум три цикла исправления; лимиты и таймауты наследуют настройки ядра и фиксируются до запуска. scheduler соблюдает глобальный лимит. Новая функция включается только явно, legacy остаётся прежним.
    
    ## Implementation Units
    
    ### F1 — Среда и границы доступа
    
    **Covers:** R1, R2, R4, R9; KTD1–KTD4. **Зависимости:** ядро U1–U7.
    **Files:** server/execution/environment/, deploy/execution/, compose.yaml; scripts/test_execution_environment.mjs, scripts/execution_environment_smoke.mjs (новые).
    
    Добавить контроллер среды, worker-профили, сетевой шлюз, scoped credentials и container-runtime. По digest полного эффективного AgentProfile (Pi/образ/provider/model, skills, extensions, tools allowlist, параметры поиска и launch config) фиксировать capability веб-поиска, поддержанный способ его включения и результат probe с реальным обращением к публичному источнику; одна доступность egress не подтверждает наличие инструмента модели. Непроверенная комбинация не допускается при включённом поиске. Конфигурация resource roots задаётся deployment; внутренние пути контейнеров отображаются на зарегистрированные host roots без клиентских абсолютных путей. Сохранять worker identity и артефакты до старта, отменять только принадлежащую попытку.
    
    **Сценарии:** shell не пишет ro-проект и не читает чужие артефакты; общий HOME/git-dir/socket/API недоступны; конфигурация mount не принимается от участника; блокируются внутренние адреса и обход egress; модель запускается и возвращает полный результат каждым участвующим Pi-профилем; поиск включается и фактически используется каждым поддержанным сочетанием; удаление search tool при прежних образе/модели инвалидирует probe; approved setup подготавливает зависимости и реальный dependency-backed check выполняется в ограниченной среде; изменение lockfile требует нового набора зависимостей; интегратор выполняет git status/diff/commit в приватном repository, не видит чужие refs, полный результат попадает в каноническую ветку и сохраняется после рестарта; timeout наблюдения не отменяет работу; рестарт контроллера восстанавливает живого worker, исчезновение worker не создаёт дубликат.
    **Гейт:** реальные launch/events/result/cancel для выбранных Pi-профилей и подтверждённые ограничения до включения Fusion.
    
    ### F2 — Панель и частичный сбой
    
    **Covers:** R1, R3–R5, R9; KTD5–KTD6. **Зависимости:** F1.
    **Files:** server/execution/fusion/; scripts/test_fusion_controller.mjs (новый).

До первой попытки проверять сохранённые capabilities поиска и digest полного эффективного AgentProfile; любое изменение digest, включая tools/extensions/allowlist при прежних образе/модели, требует нового probe.     ### F3 — Судья и два результата
    
    # Task-relative review and acceptance
    
    The caller owns acceptance of delegated work and self/external review findings,
    including LLM judge verdicts. Give workers and reviewers the same intended use,
    acceptance criteria, required checks, constraints, and non-goals. Keep that
    contract stable: neither optional improvements nor pressure to finish authorizes
    changing the user's requirements.
    
    ## Decide by evidence and task impact
    
    Judge each distinct finding by its evidence, realistic consequences in intended
    use, and effect on the agreed outcome. Severity labels, reviewer confidence, and
    model agreement are inputs to judgment, not proof or automatic priorities.
    
    - **Fix** verified violations of requirements or material risks in intended use.
    - **Verify** plausible concerns that could change acceptance but lack sufficient
      evidence. Use a targeted check rather than a speculative rewrite.
    - **Accept or defer** real limitations tolerable within the task's requirements;
      weigh the consequence of deferring against the cost and regression risk of fixing.
    - **Dismiss** disproven or duplicate claims, unsupported speculation after
      proportionate investigation, and preferences without meaningful task impact.
    
    An expensive fix does not make a blocker acceptable. MVP scope does not excuse
    material security/privacy exposure, data loss, or broken required behavior.
    A concrete code-path trace can establish a defect without a reproduction; lack
    of a reproduction alone does not justify dismissal. If credible material risk
    cannot be resolved, report the blocker instead of claiming acceptance. Request
    user input when resolution requires changing the agreed scope or a material
    decision the available evidence cannot settle.
    
    For example, an optimization for hypothetical large-scale use can be deferred
    when a prototype meets its actual workload requirements. The same performance
    issue needs fixing when it violates the task's latency target. A demonstrated
    cross-user data leak remains a blocker in an internet-facing MVP.
    
    ## Verify and finish
    
    Review the actual result and relevant surrounding behavior against the contract.
    Send the worker necessary corrections with focused checks, preserving accepted
    tradeoffs. After correction, verify the fixes and plausible regressions; broaden
    or repeat review only for a concrete unresolved risk, new evidence, or a required
    check. Optional suggestions alone do not justify another round.
    
    Keep brief reasons for dispositions in existing task notes or a required journal,
    and carry them into follow-ups. Reopen a decision when changed evidence, code,
    requirements, or a demonstrated mistake invalidates its rationale. New material
    defects still require handling, even late in review. If correction repeats without
    progress, change the approach or report the specific blocker; a round limit does
    not authorize accepting unresolved defects.
    
    Finish when the criteria and required checks are satisfied and no material
    blockers or acceptance-critical uncertainties remain. Zero suggestions and
    unanimous reviewer approval are not prerequisites. In the final response, disclose
    real limitations consciously accepted or deferred: why they are acceptable for
    this task, their practical consequences, and when to revisit them. Omit dismissed
    nits and distinguish unresolved uncertainty from a confirmed limitation.

    // State-server porch client — the Workflow view's only data source.
    //
    // The browser cannot read ~/.cache/pragmatic-orchestration/steer; the state
    // server (server/acp-state-server.mjs) bridges it read-only:
    //   GET /api/porch/runs      → { runs: PorchRunSummary[] } (startedAt desc)
    //   GET /api/porch/runs/:id  → { meta, state, audit, final }
    // `porchBase()` replicates storage.ts's stateServerBase() convention:
    // VITE_STATE_URL wins (inside the function — the node test runner imports
    // this module), else http://<location.hostname>:25900 passed through
    // toSecureUrl() so an https page lands on the TLS twin :25910.
    //
    // Erasable TS only; nothing reads import.meta.env or location at module
    // top level — scripts/test_workflow_porch.mjs imports the lib directly.
    
    import { toSecureUrl } from '../host/secure.ts';
    import type { PorchAudit, PorchRunDetail, PorchRunSummary } from './types.ts';
    
    const STATE_SERVER_PORT = 25900;
    const HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS = 1500;
    const REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000;
    
    export function porchBase(): string {
      const env = import.meta.env?.VITE_STATE_URL as string | undefined;
      if (env) return env.replace(/\/+$/, '');
      const hostname =
        (typeof location !== 'undefined' && location.hostname) || '127.0.0.1';
      return toSecureUrl(`http://${hostname}:${STATE_SERVER_PORT}`);
    }
    
    async function fetchWithTimeout(url: string, ms: number): Promise<Response> {
      const ctrl = new AbortController();
      const timer = setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), ms);
      try {
        return await fetch(url, { signal: ctrl.signal });
      } finally {
        clearTimeout(timer);
      }
    }
    
    // Session-scoped like storage.ts's probe — concurrent callers share one
    // in-flight probe and a `true` verdict is cached for the page's life. A
    // `false` verdict is NOT cached: the next call re-probes, so a state
    // server that comes up after first mount heals the view on its own
    // instead of pinning it at "unreachable" until reload.
    let healthProbe: Promise<boolean> | null = null;
    
    export async function probePorch(): Promise<boolean> {
      if (!healthProbe) {
        healthProbe = (async () => {
          try {
            const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`${porchBase()}/health`, HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS);
            if (!res.ok) return false;
            const body = (await res.json().catch(() => null)) as { ok?: boolean } | null;
            return body?.ok === true;
          } catch {
            return false;
          }
        })();
      }
      const probe = healthProbe;
      if (await probe) return true;
      // Clear only if nobody started a newer probe while we awaited.
      if (healthProbe === probe) healthProbe = null;
      return false;
    }
    
    export async function listRuns(): Promise<PorchRunSummary[]> {
      const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`${porchBase()}/api/porch/runs`, REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS);
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`porch runs: HTTP ${res.status}`);
      const body = (await res.json().catch(() => null)) as {
        runs?: PorchRunSummary[];
      } | null;
      return Array.isArray(body?.runs) ? body.runs : [];
    }
    
    /** One run's raw payload; null on 404 (the run vanished or never existed). */
    export async function getRun(runId: string): Promise<PorchRunDetail | null> {
      const res = await fetchWithTimeout(
        `${porchBase()}/api/porch/runs/${encodeURIComponent(runId)}`,
        REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS,
      );
      if (res.status === 404) return null;
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`porch run ${runId}: HTTP ${res.status}`);
      const body = (await res.json().catch(() => null)) as {
        meta?: PorchRunDetail['meta'];
        state?: Record<string, unknown> | null;
        audit?: PorchAudit | null;
        final?: string | null;
      } | null;
      if (body === null || body.meta === undefined) return null;
      return {
        meta: body.meta,
        state: body.state ?? null,
        audit: body.audit ?? null,
        final: body.final ?? null,
      };
    }

    ## U5 contract (concrete, no new approvals)
    
    **Result snapshot/hash**: `computeResultManifest(ws, baseCommit)` enumerates `git ls-files -s` (tracked, incl. dirty worktree bytes), `--others --exclude-standard` (new non-ignored), `--deleted`; per entry records `{path, type: file|link|gitlink|excluded, sha256|linkTargetHash, size, mode}`. Symlinks recorded by target hash, never followed; non-regular files (fifo/socket) abort the capture — nothing silently omitted. Credential-pattern files (`.env`, `.npmrc`, `.netrc`, key/cert material) and any `.git` path are recorded as `excluded` entries with content hash but never materialized. `resultSha256` = sha256 over the canonical manifest. Manifest itself is committed as a run artifact through the authenticated import path (stage → `commit_artifact`, hash-verified).
    
    **Validation copies**: pristine `base/` materialized per validation under `<wsRoot>/.validation/<runId>/<validationId>/` — files copied verbatim (dirty bytes, untracked, deletions absent), then `git init` + one commit → self-contained repo, own `.git`, never linked to the source. Checks run in a `verify/` reflink/full copy; reviewer+checker run in a `review/` copy; source workspace is read-only for the whole pipeline. Copy is not a sandbox — no isolation claim; same-UID worktree caveat documented.
    
    **Checks**: approved `plan.setup[]` + `plan.checks[]` run verbatim via `bash -c` single-argv (no concatenation), cwd confined under the verify copy, `detached` own process group, bounded timeout, stdout/stderr capped tails + truncation flags, cancel = `kill(-pgid)` only when the recorded leader's `{pid,starttime}` proves ours; otherwise unresolved → blocked diagnostic, never a foreign signal. Durable proc record per check enables crash-replay proof.
    
    **Reviewer/checker**: porch attempts (`acp-reviewer`/`acp-checker` profiles from preset members, snapshotted config pre-launch, durable `begin_attempt` before spawn) with `cwd` = review copy. Contract: reviewer writes `.acp-out/review_findings.json` `{version:1,round,findings:[{id,round,severity,text,where,status}]}`; checker receives the exact findings doc + `resultSha256` and writes `.acp-out/review_verdict.json`. Both imported as artifacts and submitted via `record_report` (internal token + attempt-role binding — implementer/external cannot write verdicts). Gate mirrors boardctl exactly: open critical/major with latest verdict `confirmed`|`disputed`|unvetted block; `rejected` doesn't; minor/nit retained non-blocking; missing/corrupt/stale verdict fails closed. Exit-0 without a valid report = durable failure, never acceptance.
    
    **Phases**: `prepare → implement → awaiting_validation → verify → review → check_review → {awaiting_acceptance | implement(fix) | blocked | failed}`. `run.rounds[]` records each completed cycle bound to `resultSha256`; fix = implementer attempt in canonical workspace with prior result hash + open findings; round ≥ `maxRounds` (preset limits) with open blockers or failing checks → `blocked`.
    
    **Acceptance**: `accept_result{runId, resultSha256}` — same commandId+payload replays; stale hash → 409. Re-hashes the live workspace and compares to the recorded `acceptance.resultSha256`; any post-review edit/commit invalidates → refusal, no success. On match → `succeeded`, card → reviewtest/accepted.
    
    **Stop/req-change**: stop sets `validation.cancel` + attempt cancels; the check-exec task polls durable cancel and kills only its proven group; run stays `stopping` until all reservations (attempts + validation procs) are proven terminal. Requirements change inherits the same path.

    export const useBoardStore = defineStore('board', () => {
      const cards = ref<BoardCard[]>([]);
      const filters = ref<BoardFilters>(emptyFilters());
      const ready = ref(false);
      let store: KVStore | null = null;
      let saveTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    
      // ---- persistence --------------------------------------------------------
    
      function scheduleSave(): void {
        if (!store || saveTimer) return;
        saveTimer = setTimeout(() => {
          saveTimer = null;
          void persist();
        }, 600);
      }
    
      async function persist(): Promise<void> {
        if (!store) return;
        await store.set('version', STORE_VERSION);
        await store.set('cards', cards.value);
        await store.save();
      }
    
      async function initBoardStore(): Promise<void> {
        if (ready.value) return;
        store = await loadKvStore(STORE_PATH);
        const version = await store.get<number>('version');
        const saved = await store.get<unknown[]>('cards');
        if (Array.isArray(saved)) {
          cards.value = saved
            .map(sanitizeCard)
            .filter((c): c is BoardCard => c !== null);
        }
        ready.value = true;
        // v1 (or version-less) board → write the migrated v2 document back so
        // the next load takes the fast path and `version` reflects reality.
        if (version !== STORE_VERSION) void persist();
    
        // Flush a pending debounced write on unload — otherwise a card edited
        // <600ms before a reload would be lost.
        if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
          window.addEventListener('pagehide', () => {
            if (saveTimer) {
              clearTimeout(saveTimer);
              saveTimer = null;
              void persist();
            }
          });
        }
      }
    
      // ---- ledger mirror ------------------------------------------------------
    
      function logCardEvent(card: BoardCard, detail: string): void {
        useActivityStore().recordEntry({
          // A dedicated kind, so the Events tab and its filters can tell card
          // lifecycle apart from agent syncs.
          kind: 'card',
          agentName: card.agent || 'board',
          title: card.title,
          detail,
        });
      }
    
      // ---- queries ------------------------------------------------------------
    
      /**
       * Resolve which registered project a card belongs to. `card.project` is a
       * free-text label (usually seeded from a cwd's last segment), so it matches
       * either the project name or the project path's basename — case-insensitive.
       * Unmatched/empty labels are unassigned (`null`).
       */
      function projectIdForCard(card: BoardCard): string | null {
        const label = card.project.trim().toLowerCase();
        if (!label) return null;
        const projects = useProjectsStore().projects;
        const byName = projects.find((p) => p.name.trim().toLowerCase() === label);
        if (byName) return byName.id;
        const byBase = projects.find(
          (p) => p.path.split(/[\\/]/).filter(Boolean).pop()?.toLowerCase() === label
        );
        return byBase?.id ?? null;
      }
    
      /** All cards — the board is scoped by its own filter row (f.project), not
       * by the sidebar's project-scope selector, which is a session-list filter
       * and is not reachable from the board view. */
      const scopedCards = computed(() => cards.value);
    
      function matchesFilters(card: BoardCard): boolean {
        const f = filters.value;
        if (f.project && card.project !== f.project) return false;
        if (f.agent && card.agent !== f.agent) return false;
        if (f.priority && card.priority !== f.priority) return false;
        if (f.search) {
          const q = f.search.trim().toLowerCase();
          const hay = `${card.title} ${card.description} ${card.project} ${card.agent}`.toLowerCase();
          if (!hay.includes(q)) return false;
        }
        return true;
      }
    
      const filteredCards = computed(() => scopedCards.value.filter(matchesFilters));
    
      const isFiltering = computed(
        () =>
          !!filters.value.project ||
          !!filters.value.agent ||
          !!filters.value.priority ||
          !!filters.value.search.trim()
      );
    
      /** Filtered, ordered cards of one stage — drives both the column body and
       * its header count so the counters always reflect the active filter. */
      function cardsInStage(stage: BoardStageId): BoardCard[] {
        return filteredCards.value
          .filter((c) => c.stage === stage)
          .sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order || a.createdAt - b.createdAt);
      }
    
      const projectOptions = computed(() =>
        [...new Set(cards.value.map((c) => c.project).filter(Boolean))].sort()
      );
    
      // ---- mutations ----------------------------------------------------------
    
      function nextOrder(stage: BoardStageId): number {
        const inStage = cards.value.filter((c) => c.stage === stage);
        return inStage.length ? Math.max(...inStage.map((c) => c.order)) + ORDER_STEP : ORDER_STEP;
      }
    
      function makeCard(partial: Partial<BoardCard> = {}): BoardCard {
        const now = Date.now();
        const stage =
          partial.stage && BOARD_STAGE_IDS.includes(partial.stage) ? partial.stage : 'backlog';
        return {
          id: uuid(),
          title: partial.title ?? '',
          description: partial.description ?? '',
          project: partial.project ?? '',
          agent: partial.agent ?? '',
          priority: partial.priority ?? 'medium',
          acceptance: partial.acceptance ?? '',
          verification: partial.verification ?? '',
          links: partial.links ? partial.links.map((l) => ({ ...l })) : [],
        return card;
      }
    
      function updateCard(id: string, patch: Partial<BoardCard>): MutationResult {
        const card = cards.value.find((c) => c.id === id);
        if (!card) return { ok: false };
        const { status: _status, stage: _stage, ...rest } = patch;
        Object.assign(card, rest, { id: card.id, updatedAt: Date.now() });
        // Status/stage move through their own paths (setCardStatus / moveCard)
        // so the per-stage status rules always hold — but a direct patch that
        // carries a valid status still applies, gated like setCardStatus.
        let refusal: string | null = null;
        if (_status !== undefined && STAGE_STATUSES[card.stage].includes(_status as CardStatus)) {
          refusal = reviewGateRefusal(card.id, card.stage, _status as CardStatus, card.status);
          if (!refusal) card.status = _status as CardStatus;
        }
        scheduleSave();
        if (refusal) {
          logCardEvent(card, `status → ${_status} refused: ${refusal}`);
          return { ok: false, reason: refusal };
        }
        return { ok: true };
      }
    
      function removeCard(id: string): void {
        const card = cards.value.find((c) => c.id === id);
        if (!card) return;
        cards.value = cards.value.filter((c) => c.id !== id);
        scheduleSave();
        logCardEvent(card, `card deleted from ${card.stage}`);
      }
    
      function duplicateCard(id: string): BoardCard | null {
        const src = cards.value.find((c) => c.id === id);
        if (!src) return null;
        const copy = makeCard({
          ...src,
          title: `${src.title} (copy)`,
          stage: src.stage,
          status: src.status,

        cards.value.push(copy);

        logCardEvent(copy, `duplicated from "${src.title}" in ${src.stage}`);

    /**
     * Rev-safe read-modify-write on a shared state document — the same
     * GET -> mutate -> PUT-with-rev -> retry-on-409 protocol the runner's
     * `mutate()` and boardctl use (server/acp-runner.mjs, scripts/boardctl).
     * `fn` receives the current document and returns the next one, or `null`
     * to abort the write. Returns false when no state server is reachable —
     * callers then fall back to the KV store path (Tauri / offline web).
     */
    export async function mutateRemoteDoc(
      name: string,
      fn: (data: Record<string, unknown>) => Record<string, unknown> | null,
      tries = 6,
    ): Promise<boolean> {
      if (isTauriHost() || !(await probeStateServer())) return false;
      const base = stateServerBase();
      const url = `${base}/api/state/${encodeURIComponent(name)}`;
      for (let i = 0; i < tries; i++) {
        let data: Record<string, unknown> = {};
        let rev = 0;
        try {
          const res = await fetchWithTimeout(url, {}, REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS);
          if (res.status === 404) {
            data = {};
            rev = 0;
          } else if (res.ok) {
            const body = (await res.json().catch(() => null)) as {
              data?: Record<string, unknown>;
              rev?: number;
            } | null;
            if (!body || typeof body !== 'object') return false;
            data = body.data && typeof body.data === 'object' ? body.data : {};
            rev = typeof body.rev === 'number' ? body.rev : 0;
          } else {
            return false;
          }
        } catch {
          return false;
        }
        const next = fn(structuredClone(data));
        if (next === null) return true;
        try {
          const put = await fetchWithTimeout(
            url,
            {
              method: 'PUT',
              headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
              body: JSON.stringify({ data: next, rev }),
            },
            REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS,
          );
          if (put.ok) return true;
          if (put.status === 409) {
            await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 300));
            continue;
          }
          return false;
        } catch {
          return false;
        }
      }
      return false;
    }

    <script setup lang="ts">
    // One render block inside an expanded workflow node — assistant text,
    // collapsible reasoning, a tool card, or a muted lifecycle line (meta).
    //
    // Text renders via marked+v-html the same way ChatView renders message
    // bodies (same trust level: agent output). Everything here is a porch
    // preview — data_preview caps at 200 chars, so blocks flagged `truncated`
    // carry a "preview truncated" marker instead of pretending to be whole.
    import { ref } from 'vue';
    import { marked } from 'marked';
    import type { EventBlock } from '../../lib/porch/types';
    
    const props = defineProps<{ block: EventBlock }>();
    const open = ref(false);
    
    function renderMarkdown(content: string): string {
      return marked.parse(content, { async: false }) as string;
    }
    
    // Tool input/output are JSON-ish preview strings; mono pre keeps them
    // readable without pretending they are full payloads.
    </script>
    
    <template>
      <div v-if="props.block.kind === 'text'" class="wf-block wf-text">
        <div class="wf-md" v-html="renderMarkdown(props.block.markdown)" />
        <span v-if="props.block.truncated" class="wf-trunc" title="Preview truncated by porch (200-char cap)">…</span>
      </div>
    
      <div v-else-if="props.block.kind === 'reasoning'" class="wf-block">
        <button class="wf-reason-toggle" type="button" @click="open = !open">
          {{ open ? '▾' : '▸' }} reasoning
        </button>
        <div v-if="open" class="wf-reasoning">
          {{ props.block.text }}<span v-if="props.block.truncated" class="wf-trunc" title="Preview truncated by porch (200-char cap)">…</span>
        </div>
      </div>
    
      <div v-else-if="props.block.kind === 'tool'" class="wf-block wf-tool">
        <div class="wf-tool-head">
          <span class="wf-tool-name">{{ props.block.name }}</span>
          <span class="wf-tool-status" :class="props.block.status">{{ props.block.status }}</span>
        </div>
        <pre v-if="props.block.input !== undefined" class="wf-tool-io">{{ props.block.input }}</pre>
        <pre v-if="props.block.output !== undefined" class="wf-tool-io out">{{ props.block.output }}</pre>
        <span v-if="props.block.truncated" class="wf-trunc" title="Preview truncated by porch (200-char cap)">…</span>
      </div>
    
      <div v-else class="wf-block wf-meta">
        {{ props.block.text }}<span v-if="props.block.truncated" class="wf-trunc" title="Preview truncated by porch (200-char cap)">…</span>
      </div>
    </template>

    <script setup lang="ts">
    import { ref, computed } from 'vue';
    import type { BoardCard, BoardStageId, CardStatus } from '../../stores/board';
    import { useRolesStore } from '../../stores/roles';
    import { statusBreakdown, type BoardStageDef } from './columns';
    import BoardCardItem from './BoardCardItem.vue';
    
    const props = defineProps<{
      col: BoardStageDef;
      cards: BoardCard[];
    }>();
    
    const emit = defineEmits<{
      add: [];
      open: [card: BoardCard];
      move: [cardId: string, to: BoardStageId, beforeId?: string | null];
      'set-status': [cardId: string, status: CardStatus];
      'set-flag': [cardId: string, flag: 'blocked' | 'cancelled', on: boolean];
      duplicate: [cardId: string];
      remove: [cardId: string];
      reorder: [cardId: string, delta: -1 | 1];
    }>();
    
    // HTML5 drag & drop state. `depth` tracks nested dragenter/leave so the
    // highlight doesn't flicker when crossing card boundaries.
    const depth = ref(0);
    const dropBeforeId = ref<string | null>(null);
    const dragActive = computed(() => depth.value > 0);
    
    /** Per-status tally inside this stage, e.g. `in_progress 1 / review 1`. */
    const breakdown = computed(() => statusBreakdown(props.col.id, props.cards));
    
    /** Cards in this stage carrying the `blocked` flag — counted separately
     * from the status split (the flag can sit on a card in any status). */
    const blockedCount = computed(() => props.cards.filter((c) => c.blocked).length);
    
    // Stage-role selector: the role bound to this stage in roles.json. Empty
    // means "as now — any runner picks up the stage's cards".
    const rolesStore = useRolesStore();
    const stageRole = computed(() => rolesStore.roleForStage(props.col.id));
    const stageRoleNoRunner = computed(
      () => !!stageRole.value && !rolesStore.roleHasRunner(stageRole.value)
    );
    
    function onStageRole(event: Event) {
      const value = (event.target as HTMLSelectElement).value;
      try {
        rolesStore.setStageRole(props.col.id, value || null);
      } catch (e) {
        // The select lists real roles only, so a throw here means a stale
        // option raced a delete — log it; the next render resyncs the value.
        console.error('setStageRole failed:', e);
      }
    }
    
    function cardIdFromDrag(event: DragEvent): string | null {
      return event.dataTransfer?.getData('application/x-board-card') || null;
    }
    
    function onDragEnter(event: DragEvent) {
      if (!event.dataTransfer?.types.includes('application/x-board-card')) return;
      event.preventDefault();
      depth.value += 1;
    }
    
    function onDragOver(event: DragEvent) {
      if (!event.dataTransfer?.types.includes('application/x-board-card')) return;
      event.preventDefault();
      event.dataTransfer.dropEffect = 'move';
      const el = (event.target as HTMLElement | null)?.closest?.('.board-card');
      dropBeforeId.value = el ? el.getAttribute('data-card-id') : null;
    }
    
    function onDragLeave(event: DragEvent) {
      if (!event.dataTransfer?.types.includes('application/x-board-card')) return;
      depth.value = Math.max(0, depth.value - 1);
      if (depth.value === 0) dropBeforeId.value = null;
    }
    
    function onDrop(event: DragEvent) {
      const id = cardIdFromDrag(event);
      depth.value = 0;
      if (!id) return;
      event.preventDefault();
      const beforeId = dropBeforeId.value;
      dropBeforeId.value = null;
      if (id === beforeId) return;
      emit('move', id, props.col.id, beforeId);
    }
    
    function onDragEnd() {
      depth.value = 0;
      dropBeforeId.value = null;
    }
    </script>

        const ids = new Set(cardIds);
        const released: [string, CardClaim][] = [];
        // Preferred path: CAS on the shared document (web + state server).

    // Managed execution API client (U6) — the typed user-channel surface of
    // server/execution/state-service.mjs. Erasable-TS only so node:test can run
    // it directly (same convention as src/lib/porch/api.ts).
    //
    // Wire contract (all under the state server base, e.g. http://host:25900):
    //   GET    /api/execution/cards                              → {cards: [summary]}
    //   GET    /api/execution/cards/:cardId                      → ExecCardView
    //   GET    /api/execution/cards/:cardId/documents/:versionId → ExecDocVersion & {content}
    //   POST   /api/execution/cards/:cardId/commands             → {ok,cardId,controlRevision,result}
    //   GET    /api/execution/presets                            → {presets,rev,compatibility,compatError}
    //   POST   /api/execution/presets                            → {ok,preset,rev}
    //   PUT    /api/execution/presets/:presetId                  → {ok,preset,rev}
    //   DELETE /api/execution/presets/:presetId                  → {ok,deleted,rev}
    //   GET    /api/execution/runs/:runId                        → ExecRun
    //   GET    /api/execution/runs/:runId/events?cursor&limit    → {runId,events,nextCursor,remaining,total,corrupt}
    //   GET    /api/execution/runs/:runId/artifacts/:artifactId  → {artifactId,kind,bytes,sha256,content,contentBase64}
    //
    // Every card mutation is a command envelope {commandId, type, payload,
    // expectedControlRevision}; the server dedups commandId BEFORE the revision
    // check, so replaying an id returns the recorded result and reusing an id
    // with a different payload answers 409 command_conflict. Lifecycle commands
    // are never queued or retried automatically — one deliberate user action
    // generates one commandId.

      private async req<T>(method: string, path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T> {
        const ctrl = new AbortController();
        const timer = setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), this.timeoutMs);
        let res: Response;
        try {
          res = await this.fetchFn(`${this.base}${path}`, {
            method,
            headers: body === undefined ? undefined : { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
            body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
            signal: ctrl.signal,
          });
        } catch (e) {
          const err = new ExecApiError(0, null, `state server unreachable: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`);
          err.details.cause = 'network';
          throw err;
        } finally {
          clearTimeout(timer);
        }
        const parsed = (await res.json().catch(() => null)) as unknown;
        if (!res.ok) {
          throw new ExecApiError(res.status, parsed, `HTTP ${res.status}`);
        }
        return parsed as T;
      }

    // Pure presentation + gating helpers for the managed execution UI (U6).
    // No Vue/Pinia/DOM imports — node:test exercises this module directly, and
    // CardDrawer/ExecutionPanel render from its verdicts.
    //
    // Every gate here mirrors a REAL server rule from
    // server/execution/execution-domain.mjs — the server remains authoritative;
    // these produce the disabled-reason text the user sees instead of a dead
    // click, and they never invent permissions the server does not enforce.
    
    import type {
      ExecCardView,
      ExecCheck,
      ExecDocKind,
      ExecDocState,
      ExecDocVersion,
      ExecPresetInput,
      ExecRun,
      ExecRunSummary,
    } from './api';
    
    // Run statuses that still own a reservation window (mirrors
    // RUN_NONTERMINAL / ATTEMPT_NONTERMINAL in execution-domain.mjs — kept here
    // as the UI's cheap first-pass gate; the card view's `reserved` flag is the
    // authoritative one when present).
    export const RUN_LIVE_STATUSES = new Set([
      'queued',
      'active',
      'stopping',
      'awaiting_acceptance',
    ]);
    export const ATTEMPT_LIVE_STATUSES = new Set(['launching', 'running', 'cancelling']);
    
    export interface GateResult {
      ok: boolean;
      /** Human-readable reason the action is unavailable; empty when ok. */
      reason: string;
    }
    
    const ok: GateResult = { ok: true, reason: '' };
    const no = (reason: string): GateResult => ({ ok: false, reason });
    
    /** Live reservations across all runs of the card, from the card view's
     * authoritative summaries (`reserved` covers live attempts AND active/
     * unproven validations — a terminal run can still hold one). */
    export function liveReservations(view: ExecCardView): ExecRunSummary[] {
      return (view.runs ?? []).filter((r) => {
        if (r.reserved) return true;
        return typeof r.status === 'string' && RUN_LIVE_STATUSES.has(r.status);
      });
    }
    
    /** The run summary the card currently points at, if any. */
    export function currentRunSummary(view: ExecCardView): ExecRunSummary | null {
      if (!view.currentRunId) return null;
      return (view.runs ?? []).find((r) => r.id === view.currentRunId) ?? null;
    }
    
    export function docState(view: ExecCardView, kind: ExecDocKind): ExecDocState {
      return view.documents?.[kind] ?? { current: null, versions: [] };
    }
    
    export function currentVersion(view: ExecCardView, kind: ExecDocKind): ExecDocVersion | null {
      const docs = docState(view, kind);
      if (!docs.current) return null;
      return docs.versions.find((v) => v.versionId === docs.current) ?? null;
    }
    
    // -- action gates --------------------------------------------------------------
    
    /** `start`: server requires approved requirements + approved plan + a bound
     * composition, and no live reservation anywhere on the card. */
    export function canStart(view: ExecCardView): GateResult {
      if (!view.approvals?.requirements) return no('approve the current requirements first');
      if (!view.approvals?.plan) return no('approve the current plan first');
      if (!view.composition?.preset) return no('save an execution team (preset) for this card first');
      const live = liveReservations(view);
      if (live.length) {
        return no(`run ${live[0].id} is still live — stop it and let it settle first`);
      }
      return ok;
    }
    
    /** `stop`: reachable whenever anything is still live — the backend never
     * gates stop; without live runs there is nothing to stop. */
    export function canStop(view: ExecCardView): GateResult {
      if (!(view.runs ?? []).length) return no('no run yet');
      const live = liveReservations(view);
      if (!live.length) return no('nothing live — every run has finished or is awaiting a decision');
      return ok;
    }
    
    /** `continue`: a previous run must exist, nothing may be live, and the
     * latest run must be parked (active + awaiting_validation /
     * awaiting_acceptance) or terminal. Mirrors cmdContinue's admission. */
    export function canContinue(view: ExecCardView, run: ExecRun | null): GateResult {
      const cur = currentRunSummary(view);
      if (!cur) return no('no run to continue from');
      const live = liveReservations(view);
      if (live.length) {
        return no(`run ${live[0].id} still holds a live reservation`);
      }
      if (cur.status === 'queued' || cur.status === 'stopping') {
        return no(`run ${cur.id} is ${cur.status} — wait for it to settle`);
      }
      const status = run && run.id === cur.id ? run.status : cur.status;
      const phase = run && run.id === cur.id ? run.phase : null;
      if (status === 'active' && phase !== 'awaiting_validation' && phase !== 'awaiting_acceptance') {
        return no('the current run is still in flight');
      }
      return ok;
    }
    
    /** `accept_result`: only the parked awaiting_acceptance run with its
     * recorded result hash may be accepted. */
    export function canAccept(view: ExecCardView, run: ExecRun | null): GateResult {
      if (!run || run.id !== view.currentRunId) {
        return no('open the current run to review its verified result');
      }
      if (run.status !== 'awaiting_acceptance' || !run.acceptance) {
        return no('the run has not passed its checks/review gate yet');
      }
      return ok;
    }
    
    /** `change_requirements`: always reachable on a managed card — it revokes
     * both approvals and halts live work in one commit. */
    export function canChangeRequirements(_view: ExecCardView): GateResult {
      return ok;
    }
    
    // -- enable eligibility (client-side pre-check; the server decides) ------------
    
    export interface EnableEligibility {
      ok: boolean;
      reasons: string[];
    }
    
    /** Pre-flight reasons an unmanaged card cannot be enabled. The server is
     * authoritative (it also checks git root + legacy claims); this only spares
     * the user a guaranteed refusal. `projectResolvable` comes from the board
     * store's projectIdForCard. */
    export function enableEligibility(opts: {
      cancelled: boolean;
      projectResolvable: boolean;
      projectLabel: string;
    }): EnableEligibility {
      const reasons: string[] = [];
      if (opts.cancelled) reasons.push('a cancelled card cannot be managed');
      if (!opts.projectResolvable) {
        reasons.push(
          opts.projectLabel.trim()
            ? `project "${opts.projectLabel}" is not a registered project`
            : 'set the card project to a registered project first',
        );
      }
      return { ok: reasons.length === 0, reasons };
    }
    
    // -- payload builders ------------------------------------------------------------
    
    export type DocSourceInput =
      | { type: 'text'; text: string }
      | { type: 'import'; path: string; projectId?: string };
    
    export function attachDocPayload(
      kind: ExecDocKind,
      source: DocSourceInput,
      opts: { requirementsVersionId?: string; checks?: ExecCheck[] } = {},
    ): Record<string, unknown> {
      const payload: Record<string, unknown> = { kind, source };
      if (opts.requirementsVersionId) payload.requirementsVersionId = opts.requirementsVersionId;
      if (opts.checks) payload.checks = opts.checks;
      return payload;
    }
    
    export function approvePayload(
      version: ExecDocVersion,
      extra: Record<string, unknown> = {},
    ): Record<string, unknown> {
      return { versionId: version.versionId, sha256: version.sha256, ...extra };
    }
    
    export function presetCommandPayload(preset: ExecPresetInput): Record<string, unknown> {
      return { preset };
    }
    
    export function startPayload(opts: { baseRef?: string; freshWorkspace?: boolean } = {}): Record<string, unknown> {
      const payload: Record<string, unknown> = {};
      if (opts.baseRef?.trim()) payload.baseRef = opts.baseRef.trim();
      if (opts.freshWorkspace) payload.freshWorkspace = true;
      return payload;
    }
    
    export function stopPayload(reason?: string): Record<string, unknown> {
      return reason?.trim() ? { reason: reason.trim().slice(0, 500) } : {};
    }
    
    export function continuePayload(note?: string): Record<string, unknown> {
      return note?.trim() ? { note: note.trim().slice(0, 2000) } : {};
    }
    
    export function acceptPayload(run: ExecRun): Record<string, unknown> | null {
      const hash = run.acceptance?.resultSha256;
      if (!hash) return null;
      return { runId: run.id, resultSha256: hash };
    }
    
    // -- check rows (structured plan checks editor) -----------------------------------
    
    export interface CheckRow {
      run: string;
      cwd: string;
      timeoutSec: string;
      setup: boolean;
    }
    
    export function checksToRows(checks: ExecCheck[] | undefined | null): CheckRow[] {
      return (checks ?? []).map((c) => ({
        run: c.run ?? '',
        cwd: c.cwd ?? '',
        timeoutSec: c.timeoutSec === undefined ? '' : String(c.timeoutSec),
        setup: c.setup === true,
      }));
    }
    
    /** Convert editor rows to a validated checks array (mirrors

    export function rowsToChecks(rows: CheckRow[]): { ok: boolean; problems: string[]; checks: ExecCheck[] } {
      const problems: string[] = [];

        const at = `check ${i + 1}`;
        const run = r.run.trim();
        if (!run) {

          if (!Number.isFinite(t) || t <= 0 || t > 24 * 3600) {
            problems.push(`${at}: timeout must be a number of seconds up to ${24 * 3600}`);
            return;
          }
          timeoutSec = t;
        }
        const check: ExecCheck = { run };
        if (cwd) check.cwd = cwd;
        if (timeoutSec !== undefined) check.timeoutSec = timeoutSec;
        if (r.setup) check.setup = true;
        checks.push(check);
      });
      return { ok: problems.length === 0, problems, checks };
    }

      /** Injectable fetch for tests. */
      fetchFn?: typeof fetch;
      /** Per-request timeout (ms). */
      timeoutMs?: number;
    }
    
    const REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000;
    
    /** Base URL of the state server that hosts the execution API — the same
     * convention as src/lib/host/storage.ts's stateServerBase(). */
    export function execBase(): string {
      const env = import.meta.env?.VITE_STATE_URL as string | undefined;
      if (env) return env.replace(/\/+$/, '');
      const hostname =
        (typeof location !== 'undefined' && location.hostname) || '127.0.0.1';
      return toSecureUrl(`http://${hostname}:25900`);
    }
    
    export class ExecClient {
      private readonly base: string;
      private readonly fetchFn: typeof fetch;
      private readonly timeoutMs: number;
    
      constructor(opts: ExecClientOptions = {}) {
        this.base = (opts.baseUrl ?? execBase()).replace(/\/+$/, '');
        this.fetchFn = opts.fetchFn ?? fetch;
        this.timeoutMs = opts.timeoutMs ?? REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS;
      }
    
      private async req<T>(method: string, path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T> {
        const ctrl = new AbortController();
        // The timeout bounds the WHOLE request — headers AND body — so a stalled
        // or half-delivered response can never wedge the caller's polling.
        const timer = setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), this.timeoutMs);
        let res: Response;
        let parsed: unknown;
        try {
          res = await this.fetchFn(`${this.base}${path}`, {
            method,
            headers: body === undefined ? undefined : { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
            body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
            signal: ctrl.signal,
          });
          parsed = await res.json().catch(() => null);
        } catch (e) {
          const aborted = e instanceof Error && e.name === 'AbortError';
          const err = new ExecApiError(
            0,
            null,
            aborted
              ? `state server did not answer within ${this.timeoutMs}ms`
              : `state server unreachable: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`,
          );
          err.details.cause = aborted ? 'timeout' : 'network';
          throw err;
        } finally {
          clearTimeout(timer);
        }
        if (!res.ok) {
          throw new ExecApiError(res.status, parsed, `HTTP ${res.status}`);
        }
        return parsed as T;
      }
    
      // -- reads -------------------------------------------------------------------
    
      async probe(): Promise<boolean> {
        const ctrl = new AbortController();
        const timer = setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS);
        try {
          const res = await this.fetchFn(`${this.base}/health`, { signal: ctrl.signal });
          if (!res.ok) return false;
          const body = (await res.json().catch(() => null)) as { ok?: boolean } | null;
          return body?.ok === true;
        } catch {
          return false;
        } finally {
          clearTimeout(timer);
        }
      }
    
      listCards(): Promise<{ cards: ExecCardSummary[] }> {
        return this.req('GET', '/api/execution/cards');
      }
    
      getCard(cardId: string): Promise<ExecCardView> {
        return this.req('GET', `/api/execution/cards/${encodeURIComponent(cardId)}`);
      }
    
      getDocument(cardId: string, versionId: string): Promise<ExecDocVersionContent> {
        return this.req(
          'GET',
          `/api/execution/cards/${encodeURIComponent(cardId)}/documents/${encodeURIComponent(versionId)}`,
        );
      }
    
    
    // -- action gates --------------------------------------------------------------
    
    /** `start` (cmdStart): approved inputs + bound composition + zero live
     * reservations or in-flight runs anywhere on the card. */
    export function canStart(view: ExecCardView): GateResult {
      const inputs = inputsApproved(view);
      if (!inputs.ok) return inputs;
      if (!view.composition?.preset) return no('save an execution team (preset) for this card first');
      const live = inflightRuns(view);
      if (live.length) {
        return no(`run ${live[0].id} is still live — stop it and let it settle first`);
      }
      return ok;
    }
    
    /** `stop`: reachable whenever anything is still live — the backend never
     * gates stop; without live runs there is nothing to stop. */
    export function canStop(view: ExecCardView): GateResult {
      if (!(view.runs ?? []).length) return no('no run yet');
      const live = inflightRuns(view);
      if (!live.length) return no('nothing live — every run has finished or is awaiting a decision');
      return ok;
    }
    
    /** `continue` (cmdContinue): the card must have a previous run, no run may
     * hold a live reservation (`reserved` — live attempt or active/unproven
     * validation), no run may be queued/stopping/in-flight active, and the
     * CURRENT run must be parked (active + awaiting_validation /
     * awaiting_acceptance) or terminal. The same approved-inputs and
     * composition gates as `start` apply — continue never bypasses them.
     * `run` is the loaded detail of the current run (its phase proves the
     * parked state summaries cannot express); without it an active-status
     * current run is conservatively inadmissible. */
    export function canContinue(view: ExecCardView, run: ExecRun | null): GateResult {
      const cur = currentRunSummary(view);
      if (!cur) return no('no run to continue from');
      const inputs = inputsApproved(view);
      if (!inputs.ok) return no(`continue requires freshly approved inputs — ${inputs.reason}`);
      if (!view.composition?.preset) return no('save an execution team (preset) for this card first');
      for (const r of view.runs ?? []) {
        if (r.reserved === true) {
          return no(`run ${r.id} still holds a live reservation — it must drain first`);
        }
        if (r.status === 'queued' || r.status === 'stopping') {
          return no(`run ${r.id} is ${r.status} — wait for it to settle`);
        }
        if (r.status === 'active') {
          const phase = run && run.id === r.id ? run.phase : null;
          if (phase === null || !PARKED_PHASES.has(phase)) {
            return no(`run ${r.id} is still in flight — only a parked or terminal run may precede a continuation`);
          }
        }
      }
      return ok;
    }

      private async req<T>(method: string, path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T> {
        const ctrl = new AbortController();
        // The timeout bounds the WHOLE request — headers AND body — so a stalled
        // or half-delivered response can never wedge the caller's polling.
        const timer = setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), this.timeoutMs);
        let res: Response;
        try {
          res = await this.fetchFn(`${this.base}${path}`, {
            method,
            headers: body === undefined ? undefined : { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
            body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
            signal: ctrl.signal,
          });
        } catch (e) {
          clearTimeout(timer);
          const aborted = e instanceof Error && e.name === 'AbortError';
          const err = new ExecApiError(
            0,
            null,
            aborted
              ? `state server did not answer within ${this.timeoutMs}ms`
              : `state server unreachable: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`,
          );
          err.details.cause = aborted ? 'timeout' : 'network';
          throw err;
        }

          // aborted or malformed 200 is a transport failure, never a typed
          // result the caller could adopt as authoritative state.

    export function canAccept(view: ExecCardView, run: ExecRun | null): GateResult {

    // Managed execution store (U6): the typed user-channel view of
    // server/execution/state-service.mjs. Polling is ref-counted per card —
    // CardDrawer watches the open card, WorkflowPanel watches the focused
    // card; unwatching stops fetches for that card.
    //
    // Invariants:
    //  - commands are NEVER queued for later and NEVER retried automatically:
    //    one deliberate user action = one commandId = one POST. A stale
    //    controlRevision answers revision_conflict → we refresh and surface;
    //    the user decides whether to click again.
    //  - every managed-card command carries expectedControlRevision taken from
    //    a refresh performed immediately before the POST — never a cached
    //    revision from an earlier poll.
    //  - a transport failure marks the store offline and disables actions
    //    until a successful read re-establishes the state server.
    //  - per-card `seq` is bumped on unwatch/reset; responses from a previous
    //    generation are dropped (card switch / unmount race).
    //  - run detail/events come from the run's own endpoints; the card view's
    //    `reserved` flag is authoritative for live-work gating (a terminal

      const saveError = ref<{ code: string; error: string; at: number } | null>(null);
      let store: KVStore | null = null;
      let saveTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    
      // Pending user-field deltas — per card, per FIELD, stamped with a
      // monotonic mutation generation. The managed save path merges ONLY these
      // fields onto a fresh remote row, so an untouched field of an edited
      // card (or an untouched card) is never rewritten from a stale local
      // copy, and an edit that lands mid-flight keeps its newer generation so
      // it is never cleared unshipped.
      const dirtyFields = new Map<string, Map<string, number>>();
      /** Cards created locally that the remote doc has never seen — the only
       * local-only rows a merge may add (never resurrect remote deletions). */
      const newCardIds = new Set<string>();
      const deletedCardIds = new Set<string>();
      let mutGen = 0;
      let managedSaveRunning = false;
      let managedSaveAgain = false;
      let managedSyncSeq = 0;
    
      function markFields(id: string, fields: string[]): void {
        let m = dirtyFields.get(id);
        if (!m) {
          m = new Map();
          dirtyFields.set(id, m);
        }
        const g = ++mutGen;
        for (const f of fields) m.set(f, g);
      }
    
      function markNew(id: string): void {
        newCardIds.add(id);
      }
    
      const hasManagedCards = computed(() =>
        cards.value.some((c) => c.execution?.managed === true)
      );
    
      // ---- persistence --------------------------------------------------------
    
      function scheduleSave(): void {
        if (!store || saveTimer) return;
        saveTimer = setTimeout(() => {
          saveTimer = null;
          void persist();
        }, 600);
      }
    
      async function persist(): Promise<void> {
        if (!store) return;
        if (!hasManagedCards.value) {
          dirtyFields.clear();
          newCardIds.clear();
          deletedCardIds.clear();
          await store.set('version', STORE_VERSION);
          await store.set('cards', cards.value);
          await store.save();
          return;
        }
        await persistManagedBoard();
      }
    
      /** Managed-board save: NEVER takes the KV last-write-wins/force path.
       * GET the fresh remote doc, merge only pending user-field deltas onto
       * fresh rows (managed-owned fields always come from remote), PUT with
       * the fresh rev, retry only on `rev_conflict`. Serialized: while a save
       * is in flight a further schedule just marks `managedSaveAgain`, and a
       * field's dirty mark is cleared only when the generation actually sent
       * still equals the current one — an edit that lands mid-PUT is never
       * lost. A protection refusal surfaces `saveError` + authoritative
       * reload; an unreachable server keeps the local mirror and dirty marks. */
      async function persistManagedBoard(): Promise<void> {
        if (managedSaveRunning) {
          managedSaveAgain = true;
          return;
        }
        managedSaveRunning = true;

    <script setup lang="ts">
    // Managed execution section of the card drawer (U6): the user-channel UI
    // over the execution state service. Everything rendered here comes from
    // the execution store's polled card view — never from cached board state.
    //
    // Lifecycle commands are deliberate user actions only: one click = one
    // commandId = one POST through execStore.sendCommand (busy-guarded).
    // Nothing is queued offline — while the state server is unreachable every
    // action is disabled with its reason visible.
    import { computed, onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, ref, watch } from 'vue';
    import { useBoardStore } from '../../stores/board';
    import { useExecutionStore } from '../../stores/execution';
    import { useUiStore } from '../../stores/ui';
    import { useWorkflowStore } from '../../stores/workflow';
    import {
      acceptPayload,
      attachDocPayload,
      canAccept,
      canContinue,
      canStart,
      canStop,
      checksToRows,
      currentVersion,
      docKindLabel,
      docState,
      effectivePlanChecks,
      enableEligibility,
      fmtSha,
      fmtTs,
      phaseLabel,
      planBindingNote,
      presetCommandPayload,
      reservedRuns,
      rowsToChecks,
      runStatusLabel,
      shortId,
      startPayload,
      stopPayload,
      continuePayload,
      type CheckRow,
      type DocSourceInput,
    } from '../../lib/execution/ui-model';
    import type { ExecDocKind, ExecDocVersion, ExecPresetInput, ExecRole } from '../../lib/execution/api';
    
    const props = defineProps<{ cardId: string }>();
    
    const board = useBoardStore();
    const exec = useExecutionStore();
    const uiStore = useUiStore();
    const wfStore = useWorkflowStore();
    
    // This panel owns one watch on its card — mounted/unmounted with the
    // drawer, and re-balanced on card switch.
    watch(
      () => props.cardId,
      (id, prev) => {
        if (prev && prev !== id) exec.unwatchCard(prev);
        if (id) exec.watchCard(id);
      },
    );
    
    const st = computed(() => exec.stateFor(props.cardId));
    const view = computed(() => st.value.view);
    const boardCard = computed(() => board.cards.find((c) => c.id === props.cardId) ?? null);
    const offline = computed(() => exec.online === false);
    const busy = computed(() => st.value.busy !== null);
    
    // A command is disabled while offline, while another command is in flight,
    // or while its own gate says no — the reason is always shown, never a dead
    // click.
    function gated(gate: { ok: boolean; reason: string }): { disabled: boolean; title: string } {
      if (offline.value) return { disabled: true, title: 'state server unreachable — actions are disabled' };
      if (busy.value) return { disabled: true, title: `a ${st.value.busy} command is still in flight` };
      return { disabled: !gate.ok, title: gate.ok ? '' : gate.reason };
    }
    
    async function send(
      type: Parameters<typeof exec.sendCommand>[1],
      payload: Record<string, unknown> = {},
    ): Promise<boolean> {
      const r = await exec.sendCommand(props.cardId, type, payload);
      if (!r.ok && r.error) {
        alert(r.status === 409 ? `${r.error}\n\nState was reloaded from the server.` : r.error);
      }
      return r.ok;
    }
    
    // ---- enable -----------------------------------------------------------------
    
    const eligibility = computed(() => {
      const c = boardCard.value;
      if (!c) return { ok: false, reasons: ['card not found'] };
      return enableEligibility({
        cancelled: c.cancelled,
        projectResolvable: !!board.projectIdForCard(c),
        projectLabel: c.project,
      });
    });
    
    function onEnable() {
      if (!confirm(
        'Enable managed execution for this card?\n\n' +
          'The execution engine takes over the card\'s stage, status, flags, ' +
          'project and session — the board fields become read-only.',
      )) return;
      void send('enable');
    }
    
    // ---- documents ---------------------------------------------------------------
    
    const DOC_KINDS: ExecDocKind[] = ['requirements', 'plan', 'design'];
    const docTab = ref<ExecDocKind>('requirements');
    const docVersions = computed(() => docState.value ? [] : []); // placeholder (replaced below)
    </script>

    function presetToInput(): { ok: boolean; input?: ExecPresetInput; problems: string[] } {
      const problems: string[] = [];
      const members = {} as Record<ExecRole, { cli: string; model: string; effort?: string; params?: Record<string, unknown> }>;
      for (const role of ROLES) {
        const m = presetDraft.value.members[role];
        if (!m.cli) { problems.push(`${role}: cli is required`); continue; }
        if (!m.model.trim()) { problems.push(`${role}: model is required`); continue; }
        const member: { cli: string; model: string; effort?: string; params?: Record<string, unknown> } = {
          cli: m.cli,
          model: m.model.trim(),
        };
        if (m.effort.trim()) member.effort = m.effort.trim();
        if (m.params.trim()) {
          let parsed: unknown;
          try {
            parsed = JSON.parse(m.params);
          } catch (e) {
            problems.push(`${role}: params is not valid JSON — ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : e}`);
            continue;
          }
          if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object' || Array.isArray(parsed)) {
            problems.push(`${role}: params must be a JSON object like {"key": "value"}`);
            continue;
          }
          member.params = parsed as Record<string, unknown>;
        }
        members[role] = member;
      }
      const limits: Record<string, number> = {};
      for (const [key, raw] of Object.entries(presetDraft.value.limits)) {
        const n = Number(raw);
        if (!raw.trim() || !Number.isFinite(n) || n <= 0) {
          problems.push(`limit ${key} must be a positive number`);
          continue;
        }
        limits[key] = n;
      }
      if (!presetDraft.value.name.trim()) problems.push('preset name is required');
      if (problems.length) return { ok: false, problems };
      return {
        ok: true,
        problems,
        input: {
          ...(presetDraft.value.id ? { id: presetDraft.value.id } : {}),
          name: presetDraft.value.name.trim(),
          members: members as ExecPresetInput['members'],
          limits: limits as ExecPresetInput['limits'],
        },
      };
    }
    
    function loadPresetIntoEditor(id: string) {
      const p = exec.presets.find((x) => x.id === id);
      if (!p) return;
      presetDraft.value = {
        id: p.id,
        name: p.name,
        members: {
          implementer: {
            cli: p.members.implementer?.cli ?? 'pi',
            model: p.members.implementer?.model ?? '',
            effort: p.members.implementer?.effort ?? '',
            params: p.members.implementer?.params ? JSON.stringify(p.members.implementer.params) : '',
          },
          reviewer: {
            cli: p.members.reviewer?.cli ?? 'pi',
            model: p.members.reviewer?.model ?? '',
            effort: p.members.reviewer?.effort ?? '',
            params: p.members.reviewer?.params ? JSON.stringify(p.members.reviewer.params) : '',
          },
          checker: {
            cli: p.members.checker?.cli ?? 'pi',
            model: p.members.checker?.model ?? '',
            effort: p.members.checker?.effort ?? '',
            params: p.members.checker?.params ? JSON.stringify(p.members.checker.params) : '',
          },
        },
        limits: {
          maxAttemptsPerRole: String(p.limits?.maxAttemptsPerRole ?? 1),
          timeoutMin: String(p.limits?.timeoutMin ?? 60),
          maxReviewRounds: String(p.limits?.maxReviewRounds ?? 3),
        },
      };
      presetEditorOpen.value = true;
    }
    
    async function onSavePreset() {
      const built = presetToInput();
      if (!built.ok || !built.input) {
        alert(`preset is not valid:\n${built.problems.join('\n')}`);
        return;
      }
      // save_preset upserts the registry AND binds a snapshot to this card in

      const ok = await send('save_preset', presetCommandPayload(built.input));
      if (ok) presetEditorOpen.value = false;
    }

    }
    
    async function onDeletePreset(id: string) {

      const r = await exec.removePreset(id);

    }
    
    const compositionLine = computed(() => {

    async function onStart() {

    }
    
    async function onContinue() {

      if (ok) continueNote.value = '';
    }

      if (!confirm(

    }
    
    async function onAccept() {

      if (!r) return;
      const payload = acceptPayload(r);
      if (!payload) {

              <div class="exec-btnrow">
                <button
                  class="btn primary"
                  data-testid="doc-attach"
                  :disabled="offline || busy || (!docDraft.trim() && !docImportPath.trim())"
                  @click="onAttachDoc"
                >Attach new version</button>
                <button class="btn" @click="docEditorOpen = false">Close</button>
              </div>
            </div>
            <button v-else class="link-add" data-testid="doc-new" @click="docEditorOpen = true">
              + New {{ docKindLabel(docTab).toLowerCase() }} version
                    :value="e"
                  >{{ e }}</option>
                </select>
                <input
                  v-model="presetDraft.members[role].params"
                  class="f-input mono"
                  placeholder='params {"key":"value"}'
                  :aria-label="`${role} params`"
                />
              </div>
              <div class="exec-limits">
                <label>attempts/role <input v-model="presetDraft.limits.maxAttemptsPerRole" class="f-input exec-num" /></label>
                <label>timeout min <input v-model="presetDraft.limits.timeoutMin" class="f-input exec-num" /></label>
                <label>review rounds <input v-model="presetDraft.limits.maxReviewRounds" class="f-input exec-num" /></label>
              </div>
              <div class="exec-btnrow">
                <button
                  class="btn primary"
                  data-testid="preset-save"
                  :disabled="offline || busy"
                  @click="onSavePreset"
                >Save preset + bind to card</button>
                <button class="btn" @click="presetEditorOpen = false">Close</button>
              </div>
              <p v-if="exec.presetsError" class="art-error">{{ exec.presetsError }}</p>
              <p v-if="exec.compatError" class="exec-warn" data-testid="compat-error">{{ exec.compatError }}</p>
            </div>
            <p v-if="exec.compatError && !presetEditorOpen" class="exec-warn" data-testid="compat-error">{{ exec.compatError }}</p>
          </div>
    
          <!-- run control -->
          <div class="exec-block" data-testid="exec-runcontrol">
            <div class="exec-blockhead">
              <span class="exec-blocktitle">Run</span>
              <span v-if="run" class="exec-line mono" data-testid="run-status">
                {{ shortId(run.id) }} · {{ runStatusLabel(run.status) }}<template v-if="run.phase"> · {{ phaseLabel(run.phase) }}</template>
              </span>
            </div>
    
            <div class="exec-btnrow" data-testid="run-actions">
              <button
                class="btn primary"
                data-testid="exec-start"
                :disabled="gated(startGate).disabled"
                :title="gated(startGate).title || 'Start a new run from the approved inputs'"
                @click="onStart"
              >Start</button>
              <button
                class="btn"
                data-testid="exec-stop"
                :disabled="gated(stopGate).disabled"
                :title="gated(stopGate).title || 'Record a durable stop — live attempts are cancelled'"
                @click="onStop"
              >Stop</button>
              <button
                class="btn"
                data-testid="exec-continue"
                :disabled="gated(continueGate).disabled"
                :title="gated(continueGate).title || 'Continue with a new run carrying the workspace forward'"
                @click="onContinue"
              >Continue</button>
              <button
                class="btn"
                data-testid="exec-changereq"
                :disabled="offline || busy"
                title="Revoke the requirements+plan approvals and stop live work"
                @click="onChangeRequirements"
              >Change requirements</button>
              <button
                class="btn primary"
                data-testid="exec-accept"
                :disabled="gated(acceptGate).disabled"
                :title="gated(acceptGate).title || 'Accept the reviewed workspace result'"
                @click="onAccept"
              >Accept result</button>
            </div>
            <p v-if="!startGate.ok || !continueGate.ok || !acceptGate.ok" class="art-note" data-testid="gate-hints">
              {{ [startGate, continueGate, acceptGate].map((g) => g.reason).filter(Boolean).join(' · ') }}
            </p>
    
            <div class="exec-startrow">
              <input v-model="startBaseRef" class="f-input mono" placeholder="base ref (default HEAD)" data-testid="start-baseref" />
              <label class="check-setup">
                <input v-model="startFreshWorkspace" type="checkbox" /> fresh workspace
              </label>
            </div>
            <input
              v-model="continueNote"
              class="f-input"
              placeholder="note for the continuation run (optional)"
              data-testid="continue-note"
            />
    
            <!-- selected run detail -->
            <template v-if="run">
              <p v-if="run.error" class="art-error" data-testid="run-error">{{ run.error }}</p>
              <p v-if="run.diagnostic?.detail" class="exec-warn" data-testid="run-diagnostic">{{ run.diagnostic.detail }}</p>
              <p v-if="run.acceptance" class="exec-line mono" data-testid="run-acceptance">
                verified result {{ fmtSha(run.acceptance.resultSha256, 16) }}… · round {{ run.acceptance.round }}
              </p>
              <p v-if="run.validation" class="exec-line mono" data-testid="run-validation">
                validation {{ run.validation.status }}<template v-if="run.validation.checks?.verdict"> · checks {{ run.validation.checks.verdict }}</template>
                <template v-if="run.validation.cancel"> · cancel requested</template>
              </p>
              <div v-if="run.attempts?.length" class="exec-attempts" data-testid="run-attempts">
                <div v-for="a in run.attempts" :key="a.id" class="exec-attempt mono">
                  {{ a.role }}#{{ a.n }} · {{ a.status }}<template v-if="a.phase"> · {{ a.phase }}</template>
                  <template v-if="a.finishedAt"> · {{ fmtTs(a.finishedAt) }}</template>
                  <span v-if="a.cancel" class="exec-warn"> · cancelling</span>
                  <p v-if="a.error" class="art-error">{{ a.error }}</p>
                </div>
              </div>
              <div v-if="runArtifacts.length" class="exec-artifacts" data-testid="run-artifacts">
                <button
                  v-for="a in runArtifacts"
                  :key="a.id"
                  class="art-row mono"
                  :title="a.file ?? a.id"
                  @click="onOpenArtifact(a.id)"
                >
                  <span class="art-name">{{ a.kind ?? 'artifact' }} · {{ a.file ?? shortId(a.id) }}</span>
                </button>
                <pre v-if="openedArtifact" class="exec-docview mono" data-testid="artifact-content">{{ openedArtifact.content }}</pre>
              </div>
              <div class="exec-btnrow">
                <button class="btn" data-testid="open-in-workflow" :disabled="!run" @click="onOpenInWorkflow">
                  Show in Workflow panel
                </button>
              </div>
              <div v-if="eventsTail.length" class="exec-events" data-testid="run-events">
                <div v-for="e in eventsTail" :key="e.seq" class="exec-event mono">
                  <span class="exec-eventseq">#{{ e.seq }}</span> {{ e.type }}
                </div>
                <p v-if="st.eventsPending || st.eventsCorrupt" class="art-note">
                  {{ st.eventsPending ? 'loading earlier events…' : '' }}
                  {{ st.eventsCorrupt ? `${st.eventsCorrupt} malformed event lines skipped` : '' }}
                </p>
              </div>
            </template>
            <p v-else-if="st.runError" class="art-error">{{ st.runError }}</p>
    
            <!-- run history -->
            <div v-if="view.runs.length" class="exec-history" data-testid="run-history">
              <div
                v-for="r in [...view.runs].reverse()"
                :key="r.id"
                class="exec-histrow mono"
                :class="{ sel: st.selectedRunId === r.id }"
                @click="exec.selectRun(props.cardId, r.id)"
              >
                {{ shortId(r.id) }} · {{ runStatusLabel(r.status) }}

                <span v-if="r.id === view.currentRunId" class="exec-current">current</span>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </template>
      </div>
    </template>

    async function onEnable() {
      if (!confirm(
        'Enable managed execution for this card?\n\n' +
          'The execution engine takes over the card\u2019s stage, status, flags, ' +
          'project and session — those fields become read-only on the board.',
      )) return;

      if (!view.value) return [];
      return [...docState(view.value, docTab.value).versions].sort(
        (a, b) => b.createdAt - a.createdAt,
      );
    });
    const docSelectedId = ref<string | null>(null);
    const selectedVersion = computed(() => {
      if (!view.value) return null;
      const d = docState(view.value, docTab.value);
      const want = docSelectedId.value ?? d.current;
      return d.versions.find((v) => v.versionId === want) ?? null;
    });
    
    // Viewed document content vs load failure are SEPARATE — an error text is
    // never a seed for a new document version.
    const docViewText = ref<string | null>(null);
    const docViewError = ref<string | null>(null);
    const docViewFor = ref<string | null>(null);
    const docViewLoading = ref(false);
    let docViewSeq = 0;
    
    const docDraft = ref('');
    const docImportPath = ref('');
    const docEditorOpen = ref(false);
    /** Which version the draft was seeded from + a token guarding the async

    const docDraftSeed = ref<string | null>(null);
    let docSeedSeq = 0;
