    watch([docTab, () => props.cardId], () => {
      docViewSeq += 1;
      docSeedSeq += 1;
      uiSeq += 1;
      docSelectedId.value = null;
      docViewText.value = null;
      docViewError.value = null;
      docViewFor.value = null;
      docDraft.value = '';
      docDraftSeed.value = null;
      docImportPath.value = '';
      docEditorOpen.value = false;
      planCheckRows.value = null;
    });
    onBeforeUnmount(() => {
      uiSeq += 1;
      docViewSeq += 1;
      docSeedSeq += 1;
    });
    
    const docApproval = computed(() => {
      const a = view.value?.approvals;
      if (!a) return null;
      return docTab.value === 'requirements' ? a.requirements : docTab.value === 'plan' ? a.plan : null;
    });
    const selectedApproved = computed(

        !!selectedVersion.value &&

        docApproval.value.sha256 === selectedVersion.value.sha256,
    );
    
    async function onViewDoc() {
      const v = selectedVersion.value;
      if (!v) return;
      const cardId = props.cardId;
      const seq = ++docViewSeq;
      docViewLoading.value = true;
      docViewError.value = null;
      try {
        const d = await exec.getDocument(cardId, v.versionId);
        if (seq !== docViewSeq || cardId !== props.cardId) return;
        docViewText.value = d.content;
        docViewError.value = null;
        docViewFor.value = v.versionId;
      } catch (e) {
        if (seq !== docViewSeq || cardId !== props.cardId) return;
        docViewText.value = null;
        docViewError.value = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
        docViewFor.value = v.versionId;
      } finally {
        if (seq === docViewSeq && cardId === props.cardId) docViewLoading.value = false;
      }
    }
    
    function onEditDoc() {
      const v = selectedVersion.value;
      if (!v || !view.value) return;
      if (docTab.value === 'design') return; // design is informational, not approved
      const extra: Record<string, unknown> = {};
      if (docTab.value === 'plan') {
        // The approval binds the exact check set shown — editor rows override
        // attach-time/document checks, mirroring the server's precedence. A
        // malformed editor row aborts instead of silently approving a derived
        // set the user never saw.
        if (planCheckRows.value !== null) {
          const v2 = rowsToChecks(planCheckRows.value);
          if (!v2.ok) {
            alert(`check list is not valid — nothing is approved:\n${v2.problems.join('\n')}`);
            return;
          }
        }
        const eff = effectivePlanChecks(v, planCheckRows.value);
        if (!eff.checks.length) {

        }
        if (!confirm(
          `Approve plan ${shortId(v.versionId)} (${fmtSha(v.sha256)}) with these checks ` +

            eff.checks.map((c, i) => checkLine(c, i)).join('\n'),
        )) return;
        extra.checks = eff.checks;
      } else if (!confirm(
        `Approve requirements ${shortId(v.versionId)} (${fmtSha(v.sha256)})?\n\n` +
          'Approvals bind to this exact version — attaching a new version requires a new approval.',
      )) return;
      await send(docTab.value === 'requirements' ? 'approve_requirements' : 'approve_plan', {

        sha256: v.sha256,
        ...extra,

    $ sed -n '1,235p' src/features/board/useCardDraft.ts
    // Card-drawer draft machine (extracted for behavioral tests): the local
    // editable copy of a board card, debounced back into the board store.
    //
    // Correctness rules this encodes:
    //  - `editedFields` is the set of fields the USER touched since the draft
    //    was loaded — flush() sends only those, so a stale untouched draft
    //    field can never overwrite another writer's newer value.
    //  - A pending debounced write belongs to the card it was made on. A card
    //    switch flushes the OLD card first (with its old draft + edited set);
    //    the timer is cancelled so it can never fire against the new card.
    //  - Unmount flushes whatever is pending; the timer can never outlive the
    //    component.
    //  - Managed cards: lifecycle mutations (stage/status/blocked/cancelled)
    //    are never issued from the draft — the board store refuses them too.

        if (edited.has('title')) patch.title = d.title.trim() || 'Untitled card';
        if (edited.has('description')) patch.description = d.description;
        if (edited.has('project')) patch.project = d.project.trim();
        if (edited.has('agent')) patch.agent = d.agent;
        if (edited.has('priority')) patch.priority = d.priority;
        if (edited.has('acceptance')) patch.acceptance = d.acceptance;
        if (edited.has('verification')) patch.verification = d.verification;

      watch(

        if (saveTimer) {
          clearTimeout(saveTimer);
          saveTimer = null;
        }
        flush();
      };

    // ---- release / stop -----------------------------------------------------
    // The controls mutate the same state documents the runner and boardctl
    // use: claims.json drops the claim (rev-checked), activity.json gets a
    // `card` audit row. Killing the child process belongs to the runner that
    // owns it — the panel says so plainly in the note under the executor.
    
    const notes = ref<Record<string, string>>({});
    const pending = ref(false);
    
    function audit(
      released: [string, CardClaim][],
      detail: (cardId: string, c: CardClaim) => string,
    ): void {
      for (const [cid, c] of released) {
        activity.recordEntry({
          kind: 'card',
          agentName: 'panel',
          title: titleOf(cid),
          detail: detail(cid, c),
          role: c.roleId || '',
          sessionId: c.sessionId || '',
        });
      }
    }
    
    function pidText(released: [string, CardClaim][]): string {
      const pids = released.map(([, c]) => c.pid).filter((p): p is number => !!p);
      return pids.length ? `pids ${pids.join(', ')}` : 'any live process';
    }
    
    async function releaseHeld(ex: ExecRow, held: HeldCard): Promise<void> {
      if (pending.value) return;
      pending.value = true;
      try {
        const released = await claimsStore.releaseClaims([held.cardId]);
        audit(released, (cid) =>
          `claim released by panel (Agents tab) card=${cid} — child pid not signalled`
        );
        notes.value = {
          ...notes.value,
          [ex.key]: released.length
            ? `Released "${held.title}" — the claim is gone from claims.json. ` +
              `The panel cannot signal its process: ${pidText(released)} keeps ` +
              `running until the runner that owns it exits.`
            : `"${held.title}" — the claim was already gone.`,
        };
      } finally {
        pending.value = false;
      }
    }
    
    async function stopExecutor(ex: ExecRow): Promise<void> {
      if (pending.value) return;
      const all = [...ex.roles.flatMap((r) => r.held), ...ex.orphanHeld];
      if (!all.length) return;
      pending.value = true;
      try {
        const cardIds = all.map((h) => h.cardId);
        const released = await claimsStore.releaseClaims(cardIds);
        audit(released, (cid, c) =>
          `stop-all card=${cid} released by panel; pid ${c.pid ?? '-'} not ` +
          `signalled (panel cannot kill) role=${c.roleId || '-'}`
        );
        notes.value = {
          ...notes.value,
          [ex.key]: released.length
            ? `Released ${released.length} claim(s) — slots are free and the ` +
              `cards can be picked up again. The panel cannot signal ` +
              `processes it does not own: ${pidText(released)} keep running ` +
              `until their runner exits them; run \`node server/acp-runner.mjs ` +
              `stop-all\` on the runner host to kill now.`
            : 'No live claims to release.',
        };
              :data-busy="ex.busy"
              :data-max="ex.max"
              :title="`${ex.busy} of ${ex.max} slot(s) busy (live claims vs maxConcurrent)`"
            >{{ ex.busy }}/{{ ex.max }}</span>
            <span
              v-for="rn in ex.runnerNames"
              :key="rn"
              class="chip mono runner"
              :title="`Configured agent running '${ex.cli}'`"
            >{{ rn }}</span>
            <span

    // Card-drawer draft machine (extracted for behavioral tests): the local
    // editable copy of a board card, debounced back into the board store.
    //
    // Correctness rules this encodes:
    //  - `editedFields` is the set of fields the USER touched since the draft
    //    was loaded — flush() sends only those, so a stale untouched draft
    //    field can never overwrite another writer's newer value.
    //  - A pending debounced write belongs to the card it was made on. A card
    //    switch flushes the OLD card first (with its old draft + edited set);
    //    the timer is cancelled so it can never fire against the new card.
    //  - Unmount flushes whatever is pending; the timer can never outlive the
    //    component.
    //  - Managed cards: lifecycle mutations (stage/status/blocked/cancelled)
    //    are never issued from the draft — the board store refuses them too.
    //
    // The composable takes minimal seams (saveMs for tests, an alert sink, and
    // a narrow board interface) so the whole state machine runs in node.
    
    import { computed, onBeforeUnmount, ref, watch, type ComputedRef, type Ref } from 'vue';
    import type { BoardCard, BoardStageId, CardStatus, MutationResult } from '../../stores/board';
    import { statusesForStage } from './columns';
    
    export interface CardDraftDeps {
      /** The card the draft currently mirrors (reactive). */
      card: ComputedRef<BoardCard | null>;
      /** The bound card id (reactive). */
      cardId: ComputedRef<string>;
      /** Resolve a card by id — used to flush the OLD card on a switch. */
      findCard: (id: string) => BoardCard | null;
      moveCard: (id: string, stage: BoardStageId) => MutationResult;
      setCardStatus: (id: string, status: CardStatus) => MutationResult;
      setCardFlag: (id: string, flag: 'blocked' | 'cancelled', value: boolean, reason?: string) => MutationResult;
      updateCard: (id: string, patch: Partial<BoardCard>) => MutationResult;
      /** Refusal surface — alert() in the component, captured in tests. */
      onRefused: (reason: string) => void;
      /** Debounce delay — 400ms in the UI, tiny in tests. */
      saveMs?: number;
      /** Registration seam for unmount cleanup — onBeforeUnmount in the SFC,
       * scope-stop in tests. When omitted, callers own the lifecycle. */
      onDispose?: (fn: () => void) => void;
    }
    
    export interface CardDraft {
      title: string;
      description: string;
      project: string;
      agent: string;
      priority: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low';
      acceptance: string;
      verification: string;
      blocked: boolean;
      blockedReason: string;
      cancelled: boolean;
      stage: BoardStageId;
      status: CardStatus | null;
      links: { label: string; url: string }[];
      sessionKey: string;
    }
    
    export function draftFromCard(c: BoardCard): CardDraft {
      return {
        title: c.title,
        description: c.description,
        project: c.project,
        agent: c.agent,
        priority: c.priority,
        acceptance: c.acceptance,
        verification: c.verification,
        blocked: c.blocked,
        blockedReason: c.blockedReason,
        cancelled: c.cancelled,
        stage: c.stage,
        status: c.status,
        links: c.links.map((l) => ({ ...l })),
        sessionKey: c.session ? `${c.session.agentName}::${c.session.sessionId}` : '',
      };
    }
    
    const emptyDraft: CardDraft = {
      title: '',
      description: '',
      project: '',
      agent: '',
      priority: 'medium',
      acceptance: '',
      verification: '',
      blocked: false,
      blockedReason: '',
      cancelled: false,
      stage: 'backlog',
      status: null,
      links: [],
      sessionKey: '',
    };
    
    export function useCardDraft(deps: CardDraftDeps) {
      const saveMs = deps.saveMs ?? 400;
    
      const draft: Ref<CardDraft> = ref({ ...emptyDraft, links: [] });
      const lastSavedAt = ref<number | null>(null);
      let saveTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    
      // Declared before the card watcher: an { immediate: true } callback runs
      // synchronously at registration — a let-declaration after it would be a
      // temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError on every mount.
      let editedFields = new Set<string>();
    
      /** Server-owned lifecycle on a managed card — the draft's stage/status/
       * flags never reach the board store for these. */
      function isManagedCard(c: BoardCard | null): boolean {
        return c?.execution?.managed === true;
      }
    
      /** Write pending draft edits. `targetId` pins the card the edits belong
       * to (a card switch flushes the old card before the draft is swapped). */
      function flush(targetId?: string) {
        saveTimer = null;
        const c = targetId ? deps.findCard(targetId) : deps.card.value;
        if (!c) return;
        const d = draft.value;
        const edited = editedFields;
        editedFields = new Set();
        const managed = isManagedCard(c);
        // Stage first (a stage change may reset the status), then the in-stage
        // status, then the flags — each through its own mutation so the
        // stage's status rules and the ledger entries stay intact. Managed
        // cards skip this whole block: these controls are disabled and the
        // board would refuse anyway.
        if (!managed) {
          if (edited.has('stage') && d.stage !== c.stage) {
            const r = deps.moveCard(c.id, d.stage);
            if (!r.ok && r.reason) deps.onRefused(r.reason);
          }
          if (edited.has('status') && d.status && d.status !== c.status) {
            const r = deps.setCardStatus(c.id, d.status);
            // The review-cycle gate refuses `agent_tested` while blocking
            // findings are open — surface the reason and snap the draft back.
            if (!r.ok && r.reason) {
              deps.onRefused(r.reason);
              draft.value.status = c.status;
            }
          }
          if (
            (edited.has('blocked') || edited.has('blockedReason')) &&
            (d.blocked !== c.blocked || d.blockedReason.trim() !== c.blockedReason)
          ) {
            const r = deps.setCardFlag(c.id, 'blocked', d.blocked, d.blocked ? d.blockedReason.trim() : '');
            if (!r.ok && r.reason) deps.onRefused(r.reason);
          }
          if (edited.has('cancelled') && d.cancelled !== c.cancelled) {
            const r = deps.setCardFlag(c.id, 'cancelled', d.cancelled);
            if (!r.ok && r.reason) deps.onRefused(r.reason);
          }
        }
        const patch: Partial<BoardCard> = {};
        if (edited.has('title')) patch.title = d.title.trim() || 'Untitled card';
        if (edited.has('description')) patch.description = d.description;
        if (edited.has('project')) patch.project = d.project.trim();
        if (edited.has('agent')) patch.agent = d.agent;
        if (edited.has('priority')) patch.priority = d.priority;
        if (edited.has('acceptance')) patch.acceptance = d.acceptance;
        if (edited.has('verification')) patch.verification = d.verification;
        if (edited.has('links')) {
          patch.links = d.links
            .filter((l) => l.label.trim() || l.url.trim())
            .map((l) => ({ label: l.label.trim(), url: l.url.trim() }));
        }
        if (edited.has('sessionKey')) {
          const sessionKey = d.sessionKey;
          patch.session = sessionKey
            ? { agentName: sessionKey.split('::')[0], sessionId: sessionKey.split('::').slice(1).join('::') }
            : null;
        }
        if (Object.keys(patch).length) {
          const r = deps.updateCard(c.id, patch);
          if (!r.ok && r.reason) deps.onRefused(r.reason);
        }
        lastSavedAt.value = Date.now();
      }
    
      /** Explicit one-shot write — duplicate/remove paths. */
      function flushNow() {
        if (saveTimer) {
          clearTimeout(saveTimer);
          saveTimer = null;
        }
        flush();
      }
    
      function markDirty(field: string) {
        editedFields.add(field);
        if (saveTimer) clearTimeout(saveTimer);
        saveTimer = setTimeout(() => flush(), saveMs);
      }
    
      /** A managed card picked a stage/status in the UI — unreachable while
       * the control is disabled, but keep the semantics honest: the draft's
       * status follows the stage's own rules. */
      function onStagePicked() {
        const allowed = statusesForStage(draft.value.stage);
        if (!draft.value.status || !allowed.includes(draft.value.status)) {
          draft.value.status = allowed[0] ?? null;
        }
        markDirty('stage');
        markDirty('status');
      }
    
      function resetToCard() {
        if (deps.card.value) draft.value = draftFromCard(deps.card.value);
        editedFields = new Set();
      }
    
      // Card switch: cancel the pending write first, then flush it against the
      // OLD card id — the timer must never deliver old edits to the new card.
      watch(
        deps.cardId,
        (_id, prevId) => {
          if (saveTimer) {
            clearTimeout(saveTimer);
            saveTimer = null;
            if (prevId) flush(prevId);
          }
          resetToCard();
        },
        { immediate: true },
      );
    
      const dispose = () => {
        if (saveTimer) {
          clearTimeout(saveTimer);
          saveTimer = null;
        }
        flush();
      };
      if (deps.onDispose) deps.onDispose(dispose);
      else onBeforeUnmount(dispose);
    
      const hasPending = computed(() => editedFields.size > 0 || saveTimer !== null);
    
      return {

    // Managed execution store (U6): the typed user-channel view of
    // server/execution/state-service.mjs. Polling is ref-counted per card —
    // CardDrawer watches the open card, the Workflow panel watches the focused
    // card; unwatching stops fetches for that card.
    //
    // Concurrency rules:
    //  - every request carries a monotonic issue stamp; a response may only
    //    adopt state or flip `online` when no NEWER request was issued since —
    //    an old slow GET can never roll state or connectivity backwards.
    //  - `seq` is the per-card watch generation (bumped on unwatch). `reqSeq`
    //    orders refreshCard calls; `runReqSeq` orders run-detail/event calls
    //    (also bumped by selectRun). A response checks all applicable guards
    //    before touching state.
    //  - commands are NEVER queued for later and NEVER retried automatically:
    //    one deliberate click = one commandId = one POST. The per-card `busy`
    //    flag is acquired before the first await, so two clicks cannot issue
    //    two different commandIds.
    //  - every managed-card command carries expectedControlRevision from a
    //    refresh performed while the busy flag is held; a failed refresh
    //    refuses the POST — a cached "ready" view is never command authority.
    //  - unwatching a card drops its entry entirely; a response arriving for
    //    the dropped object is discarded (`cards[cardId] !== st`).
    //  - run detail/events come from the run's own endpoints; the card view's
    //    `reserved` flag is authoritative for live-work gating.

      type ExecRunEvent,
      type ExecArtifactContent,

    import { RUN_LIVE_STATUSES } from '../lib/execution/ui-model.ts';
    import { useBoardStore } from './board';
    import { uuid } from '../lib/uuid';
    
    const POLL_MS = 2000;
    const EVENTS_PAGE = 200;
    /** Max event pages drained per refreshRun — a terminal run with a long

    const EVENTS_MAX_PAGES = 10;
    
    export type CardPhase = 'idle' | 'loading' | 'ready' | 'unmanaged' | 'error';

      ok: boolean;
      code?: string;
      error?: string;

      result?: unknown;
      details?: Record<string, unknown>;
    }
    
    export interface CardExecState {
      cardId: string;
      phase: CardPhase;
      view: ExecCardView | null;
      /** Last user-facing fetch/command error for this card. */
      error: string | null;
      lastFetchedAt: number | null;

      /** Watch generation — bumped when the entry is dropped. */
      seq: number;
      /** Latest refreshCard request id — newest issued wins. */
      reqSeq: number;
      /** Latest run request id — bumped by selectRun and each refreshRun. */
      runReqSeq: number;
      /** internalRevision at the last successful board.json managed-row sync. */
      syncedInternalRev: number;
      /** Run the detail pane shows (defaults to the card's current run). */
      selectedRunId: string | null;
      /** currentRunId seen on the previous adopt — auto-follows continue. */
      lastCurrentRunId: string | null;
      run: ExecRun | null;
      runError: string | null;
      events: ExecRunEvent[];
      eventsCursor: number;
      eventsTotal: number;
      eventsCorrupt: number;

      /** Command type currently in flight (busy-guard for double clicks). */
      busy: ExecCommandType | null;
      commandError: { code: string; error: string; at: number } | null;
      /** Single-flight refreshCard promise — later callers coalesce. Stored

      cardInflight: Promise<boolean> | null;

      runInflight: { runId: string } | null;
    }

          posts.push(env);

        exec.watchCard('card_1');

        const p1 = exec.sendCommand('card_1', 'stop'); // acquires busy, refreshes, POSTs

        const p2 = exec.sendCommand('card_1', 'stop'); // must refuse 'busy'
        postD.res({ ok: true, result: {} });
        const [r1, r2] = await Promise.all([p1, p2]);
        assert.equal(posts.length, 1);
        assert.equal(posts[0].type, 'stop');
        const results = [r1, r2];
        assert.ok(results.some((r) => r?.ok === true));

        exec.unwatchCard('card_1');

      async function selectRun(cardId: string, runId: string | null): Promise<void> {
        const st = stateFor(cardId);
        if (st.selectedRunId === runId && st.run) return;
        st.selectedRunId = runId;
        st.run = null;
        st.runError = null;
        st.events = [];
        st.eventsCursor = 0;
        st.eventsTotal = 0;
        st.eventsCorrupt = 0;
        st.eventsPending = false;
        st.runReqSeq += 1; // invalidate any in-flight detail/events response
        if (runId) await refreshRun(cardId);
      }

    $ sed -n '1,220p' src/components/WorkflowPanel.vue
    <script setup lang="ts">
    // Workflow side panel — the porch-run stepper docked next to the chat feed
    // (composer's run-mode = "workflow"). Same store and stepper as the former
    // top-level Workflow view, minus the run-list strip: in a narrow column the
    // panel just follows the latest run ("auto-trigger"); pinning a run stays
    // possible via the store, this surface doesn't need the list.
    //
    // Data path: state server's read-only porch endpoints (GET /api/porch/runs,
    // GET /api/porch/runs/:id) polled by src/stores/workflow.ts every 2s while
    // this panel is mounted.
    import { computed, onMounted, onBeforeUnmount } from 'vue';
    import { useWorkflowStore } from '../stores/workflow';
    import { useExecutionStore } from '../stores/execution';
    import { useBoardStore } from '../stores/board';
    import { DIRECTIONS } from '../lib/porch/graph';
    import type { Direction } from '../lib/porch/types';
    import WorkflowStepper from '../features/workflow/WorkflowStepper.vue';
    import { runStatusLabel, phaseLabel, shortId as execShortId, fmtTs } from '../lib/execution/ui-model';
    
    const wf = useWorkflowStore();
    const exec = useExecutionStore();
    const board = useBoardStore();
    
    // initWorkflowStore() can resolve after unmount (loadKvStore waits on the
    // state server). Without this guard the .then below would start a 2s
    // interval the Pinia store then keeps for the rest of the session.
    let disposed = false;
    
    let indexTimer: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;
    
    onMounted(() => {
      void wf.initWorkflowStore().then(() => {
        if (!disposed) wf.startPolling();
      });
      void exec.refreshIndex();
      void exec.loadPresets();
      // The managed index refreshes while this panel is mounted — the store's
      // own poll only covers watched/focused cards.
      indexTimer = setInterval(() => void exec.refreshIndex(), 2000);
    });
    onBeforeUnmount(() => {
      disposed = true;
      wf.stopPolling();
      exec.clearFocus();
      if (indexTimer !== null) {
        clearInterval(indexTimer);
        indexTimer = null;
      }
    });
    
    // ---- managed runs (U6) -----------------------------------------------------
    // The managed section reads ONLY the execution API — porch state stays
    // untouched. `exec.focused` pins one managed run's detail below the list;
    // the board's drawer routes here via execStore.openManagedRun().
    
    const focusedState = computed(() =>
      exec.focused ? exec.stateFor(exec.focused.cardId) : null,
    );
    const focusedRun = computed(() => focusedState.value?.run ?? null);
    const focusedCardTitle = computed(() => {
      const id = exec.focused?.cardId;
      if (!id) return '';
      return board.cards.find((c) => c.id === id)?.title ?? id;
    });
    
    function cardLabel(cardId: string): string {
      return board.cards.find((c) => c.id === cardId)?.title || cardId.slice(0, 8);
    }
    
    const DIR_LABELS: Record<Direction, string> = {
      run: 'Run',
      delegate: 'Delegate',
      ask: 'Ask',
      code: 'Code',
      pipeline: 'Pipeline',
    };
    
    function shortId(runId: string): string {
      return runId.replace(/^run_/, '');
    }
    
    /** "<runId-tail> · <agent>@<backend> · <model> · <status> · <elapsed>". */
    const summaryLine = computed(() => {
      const meta = wf.detail?.meta;
      const sum = wf.selectedSummary;
      if (!meta && !sum) return '';
      const parts: string[] = [];
      const runId = meta?.run_id ?? sum?.runId;
      if (runId) parts.push(shortId(runId));
      const agent = meta?.agent_id ?? sum?.agentId;
      const backend = meta?.backend ?? sum?.backend;
      if (agent || backend) parts.push(`${agent ?? '?'}@${backend ?? '?'}`);
      const status = meta?.status ?? sum?.status;
      if (status) parts.push(status);
      const started = meta?.started_at ?? sum?.startedAt;
      const finished = meta?.finished_at ?? sum?.finishedAt;
      const startMs = started ? Date.parse(started) : NaN;
      const endMs = finished ? Date.parse(finished) : wf.now;
      if (Number.isFinite(startMs) && Number.isFinite(endMs) && endMs >= startMs) {
        const s = Math.round((endMs - startMs) / 1000);
        if (s < 60) parts.push(`${s}s`);
        else if (s < 3600) parts.push(`${Math.floor(s / 60)}m ${s % 60}s`);
        else parts.push(`${Math.floor(s / 3600)}h ${Math.floor((s % 3600) / 60)}m`);
      }
      return parts.join(' · ');
    });
    
    const nodeCounts = computed<Record<string, number>>(() => {
      const out: Record<string, number> = {};
      for (const n of wf.nodes) {
        const c = wf.eventsFor(n.id).length;
        if (c > 0) out[n.id] = c;
      }
      return out;
    });
    </script>
    
    <template>
      <aside class="wf-panel" :aria-busy="!wf.ready">
        <header class="panel-head">
          <h2>Workflow</h2>
          <span class="panel-note" aria-live="polite" :title="summaryLine">{{ summaryLine }}</span>
        </header>
    
        <nav class="tab-bar" aria-label="Workflow direction">
          <button
            v-for="d in DIRECTIONS"
            :key="d"
            class="tab-btn"
            :class="{ active: wf.direction === d }"
            role="tab"
            :aria-selected="wf.direction === d"
            :title="wf.manualDirection === d ? 'Manual pick — click again to follow the run\'s direction' : undefined"
            @click="wf.setDirection(d)"
          >
            {{ DIR_LABELS[d] }}
          </button>
        </nav>
    
        <div v-if="wf.staleText" class="wf-banner" role="status">{{ wf.staleText }}</div>
        <div v-if="wf.errorText || wf.errorMessage" class="wf-banner error" role="alert">
          {{ wf.errorText ?? wf.errorMessage }}
        </div>
    
        <div class="panel-body">
          <!-- Managed card runs (execution API) — separate source/events,
               porch display below is untouched. -->
          <section v-if="exec.managedIndex.length || exec.focused" class="managed" data-testid="managed-section">
            <div class="managed-head">
              <span class="managed-title">Managed runs</span>
              <span v-if="exec.indexError" class="managed-err">{{ exec.indexError }}</span>
            </div>
            <div
              v-for="mc in exec.managedIndex"
              :key="mc.cardId"
              class="managed-row mono"
              :class="{ sel: exec.focused?.cardId === mc.cardId }"
              @click="exec.openManagedRun(mc.cardId, mc.currentRunId)"
            >
              <span class="managed-card" :title="cardLabel(mc.cardId)">{{ cardLabel(mc.cardId) }}</span>
              <span class="managed-run">{{ mc.currentRunId ? execShortId(mc.currentRunId) : 'no run' }}</span>
            </div>
    
            <div v-if="exec.focused && focusedRun" class="managed-detail" data-testid="managed-detail">
              <div class="managed-detailhead mono">
                {{ execShortId(focusedRun.id) }} · {{ runStatusLabel(focusedRun.status) }}<template v-if="focusedRun.phase"> · {{ phaseLabel(focusedRun.phase) }}</template>
              </div>
              <p class="managed-sub mono">{{ focusedCardTitle }}<template v-if="focusedRun.error"> · {{ focusedRun.error }}</template></p>
              <div v-if="focusedState?.events.length" class="managed-events">
                <div v-for="e in focusedState.events.slice(-12)" :key="e.seq" class="managed-event mono">
                  #{{ e.seq }} {{ e.type }}
                </div>
              </div>
              <p v-if="focusedRun.finishedAt" class="managed-sub mono">finished {{ fmtTs(focusedRun.finishedAt) }}</p>
            </div>
            <p v-else-if="exec.focused" class="managed-sub mono">loading run detail…</p>
          </section>
    
          <template v-if="wf.porchUp === false">
            <div class="wf-empty">
              <p>Porch endpoint unreachable.</p>
              <p class="wf-hint">The state server (port 25900) is not answering — start the stack with <code>docker compose up -d</code>.</p>
            </div>
          </template>
          <template v-else-if="wf.porchUp && wf.runs.length === 0">
            <div class="wf-empty">
              <p>No porch runs yet.</p>
              <p class="wf-hint">Dispatch one from a shell: <code>scripts/porch-dispatch -a &lt;agent&gt; --cwd &lt;dir&gt; "&lt;task&gt;"</code></p>
            </div>
          </template>
          <template v-else>
            <WorkflowStepper
              :nodes="wf.nodes"
              :active-index="wf.activeNodeIndex"
              :terminal="wf.terminal"
              :expanded-node-id="wf.expandedNodeId"
              :expanded-blocks="wf.expandedBlocks"
              :counts="nodeCounts"
              @toggle="wf.toggleNode"
            />
            <div v-if="wf.auditTruncated" class="wf-tail-note">showing last 512 KiB of audit.jsonl</div>
          </template>
        </div>
      </aside>
    </template>
    
    <style scoped>
    .wf-panel {
      display: flex;
      flex-direction: column;
      height: 100%;
      min-height: 0;
      overflow: hidden;
    }
    
    .panel-head {
      display: flex;
      align-items: baseline;
      justify-content: space-between;
      gap: 0.75rem;

    // Test-only ESM hooks: resolve the repo's bundler-style imports
    // (extensionless + .vue SFCs) so node can run real components.
    //
    // - extensionless relative specifier → tries .ts / .vue / .mjs / .js / /index.ts
    // - *.vue → @vue/compiler-sfc compile (script setup + inlineTemplate) so the
    //   emitted module is self-contained erasable TS.
    // - .ts → node's built-in type stripping handles it (erasable only).
    //
    // Registered from the test file via module.register(); nothing here runs in
    // the product build.
    
    import { readFileSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs';
    import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
    import { dirname, resolve as resolvePath, extname } from 'node:path';
    import { parse, compileScript } from '@vue/compiler-sfc';
    
    const EXTENSIONS = ['.ts', '.vue', '.mjs', '.js'];
    const INDEXES = ['/index.ts', '/index.mjs', '/index.js'];
    
    export async function resolve(specifier, context, next) {
      try {
        return await next(specifier, context);
      } catch (e) {
        if (
          (specifier.startsWith('./') || specifier.startsWith('../')) &&
          (e.code === 'ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND' ||
            e.code === 'ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION' ||
            e.code === 'ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT')
        ) {
          const parentDir = dirname(fileURLToPath(context.parentURL));
          if (!extname(specifier)) {
            for (const ext of EXTENSIONS) {
              const candidate = resolvePath(parentDir, specifier + ext);
              if (existsSync(candidate)) {
                return { url: pathToFileURL(candidate).href, shortCircuit: true };
              }
            }
          }
          // Bundler-style directory import → index.*
          for (const idx of INDEXES) {
            const candidate = resolvePath(parentDir, specifier + idx);
            if (existsSync(candidate)) {
              return { url: pathToFileURL(candidate).href, shortCircuit: true };
            }
          }
        }
        throw e;
      }
    }
    
    let sfcSeq = 0;
    
    export async function load(url, context, next) {
      if (!url.endsWith('.vue')) return next(url, context);
      const filename = fileURLToPath(url);
      const source = readFileSync(filename, 'utf8');
      const { descriptor, errors } = parse(source, { filename });
      if (errors.length) {
        throw new Error(`SFC parse errors in ${filename}: ${errors.map((e) => e.message).join('; ')}`);
      }
      const id = `test_sfc_${sfcSeq++}`;
      const compiled = compileScript(descriptor, { id, inlineTemplate: true });
      // inlineTemplate embeds the render function — the module is plain JS/TS
      // importing only 'vue' plus whatever the script imported.
      return { format: 'module', source: compiled.content, shortCircuit: true };
    }

      async function sendCommand(
        cardId: string,
        type: ExecCommandType,
        payload: Record<string, unknown> = {},
      ): Promise<CommandOutcome> {
        const st = stateFor(cardId);
        if (st.busy) {
          return { ok: false, code: 'busy', error: 'a command is still in flight — wait a moment' };
        }
        st.busy = type;
        st.commandError = null;
        const gen = st.seq;
        const stillMine = () => cards.value[cardId] === st && st.seq === gen;
        let net = 0; // request issue stamp — set immediately before the POST
        try {
          // Every command — including enable — is grounded in a fresh read
          // while the busy flag is held. `refreshCard` returns false both on
          // transport failure AND on a fresh "not managed" (404) answer; the
          // phase tells them apart below.
          const fresh = await refreshCard(cardId);
          if (!stillMine()) {
            return { ok: false, code: 'stale', error: 'the card view changed while checking state' };
          }
          if (type === 'enable') {
            if (st.phase === 'ready' && st.view?.managed) {
              return { ok: false, code: 'already_managed', error: 'this card is already managed' };
            }
            if (st.phase !== 'unmanaged') {
              return {
                ok: false,
                code: 'offline',
                error: st.error ?? 'the state server is unreachable — actions are disabled',
              };
            }
          } else if (!fresh || st.phase !== 'ready' || !st.view) {

    export function mirrorLocalDoc(name: string, data: Record<string, unknown>): void {
      writeLocalData(localKey(name), data);
    }
    
    // Web stores are cached per document name so every call site shares one
    // in-memory view (and one poll timer) for e.g. `preferences.json`.
    const webStores = new Map<string, Promise<KVStore>>();
    
    /** Test-only seam: tear down the cached stores (their poll timers included)
     * and the session health probe so each case makes a clean backend decision
     * and no interval outlives the harness. Production code never calls it. */
    export async function __resetWebKvForTests(): Promise<void> {
      const pending = [...webStores.values()];
      webStores.clear();
      healthProbe = null;
      for (const p of pending) {
        const store = await p.catch(() => null);
        if (store && typeof (store as { dispose?: unknown }).dispose === 'function') {
          (store as { dispose(): void }).dispose();
        }
      }

    # Pragmatic Orchestration
    
    Resolve the entrypoint below, then use only `"$PORCH"`. Select the mode from the user's intent and load only the linked reference needed for that mode.
    
    ## Platforms
    
    Linux/macOS use the full offline suite. Windows 11 + Git Bash/MSYS2 + native
    Python 3.11+ is experimental and community-supported; native supervisor and
    platform regressions run in CI. `sessions`/`quota` also run natively via the
    `porch.cmd` sibling launcher — no bash needed for session history. Use Git Bash for
    the `review`/`delegate` shell entrypoint and a private per-user registry. See
    [README.md](README.md#platform-support) for the verified scope and launcher
    limitations.
    
    ## Entrypoint resolution
    
    Set `PORCH` to the `porch` executable in the `scripts` subdirectory of the exact
    `SKILL.md` loaded by skill discovery. Verify it before the first call:
    
    ```bash
    test -x "$PORCH" || { echo "pragmatic-orchestration entrypoint not found: $PORCH" >&2; exit 1; }
    ```
    
    Resolve this from the loaded skill path, never from the caller's working directory, repository
    root, or `PATH`. Do not execute the entrypoint as a relative path. Keep the shell in the
    repository the external agent should inspect or change.
    
    ## Prompt transport is part of the launch
    
    Every `review ask` invocation must visibly transport a non-empty prompt in the
    same shell command: as the positional argument, through an explicit stdin pipe
    or heredoc, or with `--prompt-file FILE`. Never run a bare `review ask` command
    with only options and assume that prompt text from commentary, planning, or the
    surrounding agent context becomes stdin; shell execution has no such implicit
    connection. For a generated multiline repository review, prefer an explicit
    heredoc or prompt file so the complete problem statement and context seed are
    delivered atomically.
    
    ## Recommended review defaults
    
    Use these unless the user asks for a different tradeoff:
    
    - Independent architecture, design, debugging, or planning opinions: `review ask --progress compact` with all enabled profiles.
    - Routine file or diff review: `review code --progress compact` (`basic`: security + correctness).
    - High-risk or release-blocking review: `review code --depth super --progress compact`.
    - Use `specialists` only for a broader mid-cost review without an LLM judge. Use `ultra` only when the user explicitly prioritizes maximum coverage over cost and latency.
    - Repository research: `delegate -a grok` from the target repository root. Tell the worker whether the task is read-only, keep the default steerable session, and use `steer`/`wait` to continue incomplete work.
    - The `grok` profile is Grok 4.6 and is the default native Grok Build worker. Use the disabled-by-default `grok-fast` profile explicitly for fast context research with Grok 4.5.
    - GPT-6 Astra is an explicit Codex second opinion for difficult specification verification or optimization planning. Select it with `-a codex`; do not add it to routine research or the default review pool.
    - The default Claude Code profile is `claude-opus`: Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) at `medium` effort. The `claude-code` profile is a disabled alias for the same model and effort.
    - The opt-in `claude-fable` profile runs Claude Fable 5.1 for demanding long-horizon review or delegation. Its default `low` effort is cost-conscious; override it with `CLAUDE_EFFORT=high`, `xhigh`, or `max` when capability matters more than latency and cost.
    - The `devin` profile runs Devin CLI SWE-2-high (`devin` on PATH, `devin auth login`) for review and delegate over `devin acp`. It is disabled by default and never joins the default review pool: select it with `-a devin` or enable the profile. Effort is versioned into the model id, so there is no effort override; `auto`/`queue` steer merges into the running turn and `interrupt` cancels and sends.

    // scripts/u1_live_smoke.mjs — U1 live verification: real porch runs of one
    // CLI profile in an isolated execution root, driven through the runtime
    // adapter. No listeners; writes only under --root (default $U1_SMOKE_ROOT).
    //
    //   node scripts/u1_live_smoke.mjs --agent pi --mode run    [--timeout 420]
    //   node scripts/u1_live_smoke.mjs --agent pi --mode cancel [--timeout 180]
    //
    // run    — short task, full lifecycle: start -> status -> events -> wait ->
    //          reconcile. PASS requires terminal 'completed' AND the expected
    //          U1-SMOKE-OK marker in the full final result.
    // cancel — long task, cancel while running -> wait. PASS only on 'cancelled';
    //          a run that reached terminal before the cancel landed is reported
    //          as evidence, not a pass.
    // All exits run bounded cleanup: any run we started is cancelled and
    // waited to terminal before exiting. Only runs matched to THIS attempt's
    // selectors are ever touched.
    
    import { promises as fs } from 'node:fs';
    import os from 'node:os';
    import path from 'node:path';
    import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
    import { createPorchRuntime } from '../server/execution/porch-runtime.mjs';
    
    function arg(name, dflt) {
      const i = process.argv.indexOf(`--${name}`);
      return i >= 0 && i + 1 < process.argv.length ? process.argv[i + 1] : dflt;
    }
    const AGENT = arg('agent', '');
    const MODE = arg('mode', 'run');
    const TIMEOUT = Number(arg('timeout', MODE === 'cancel' ? 180 : 420));
    const PORCH = arg('porch', process.env.ACP_PORCH_CLI
      || path.join(os.homedir(), '.pi/agent/skills/pragmatic-orchestration/scripts/porch'));
    const ROOT = arg('root', process.env.U1_SMOKE_ROOT
      || path.join(os.tmpdir(), `u1-smoke-${process.pid}`));
    const MARKER = `U1-SMOKE-OK-${AGENT.toUpperCase()}`;
    
    if (!AGENT) {
      console.error('usage: u1_live_smoke.mjs --agent <porch-profile-id> [--mode run|cancel] [--timeout SEC] [--root DIR] [--porch PATH]');
      process.exit(2);
    }
    
    const emit = (kind, obj = {}) =>
      console.log('SMOKE ' + JSON.stringify({ kind, agent: AGENT, mode: MODE, ...obj }));
    
    const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
    
    // Explicit profile snapshot from the *installed* porch config — the runtime
    // requires one; we take the profile verbatim rather than inventing models.
    // scripts/porch -> skill root is one level up.
    const skillRoot = path.resolve(path.dirname(PORCH), '..');
    const installedCfg = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(path.join(skillRoot, 'config.json'), 'utf8'));
    const profile = installedCfg.agents?.[AGENT];
    if (!profile) {
      emit('FAIL', { msg: `profile '${AGENT}' not in installed porch config`, skillRoot });
      process.exit(1);
    }
    const snapshotConfig = { agents: { [AGENT]: { ...profile, enabled: true } } };
    emit('profile', { backend: profile.backend, model: profile.model,
      effort: profile.effort ?? null, porch: PORCH });
    
    const rt = createPorchRuntime({ rootDir: path.join(ROOT, 'exec'), porchPath: PORCH });
    emit('environment', rt.environment());
    
    // Tiny isolated git repo (standalone, not a git worktree — U3 owns real
    // worktree lifecycle). Proves cwd handling + git presence for commit-capable
    // agents.
    const ws = path.join(ROOT, 'ws', AGENT);
    await fs.mkdir(ws, { recursive: true });
    try {
      execFileSync('git', ['init', '-q', '-b', 'u1-smoke'], { cwd: ws });
      await fs.writeFile(path.join(ws, 'README.md'), `# u1 smoke repo (${AGENT})\n`);
      execFileSync('git', ['-c', 'user.email=u1@smoke', '-c', 'user.name=u1-smoke',
        'add', 'README.md'], { cwd: ws });
      execFileSync('git', ['-c', 'user.email=u1@smoke', '-c', 'user.name=u1-smoke',
        'commit', '-qm', 'init'], { cwd: ws });
      emit('repo', { ws, git: true });
    } catch (e) {
      emit('repo', { ws, git: false, error: String(e.message || e) });
    }
    
    const PROMPTS = {
      run: `Reply with exactly this marker and nothing else: ${MARKER}.
    Do not create, modify, or delete any files. Do not run tests. Just answer.`,
      // Cheap-but-slow task: one shell call keeps the turn alive long enough

      cancel: `Use your shell/terminal tool to run exactly this command and wait for it:
    sleep 120 && echo done
    Then reply DONE. Do nothing else — no other tools, no file changes.`,
    };

    # Delegate mode
    
    Delegate assigns one task to one explicitly selected external coding-agent
    profile in the caller's working directory. The parent owns scope, supervision,
    and acceptance. Use the workflow below; command choices depend on the situation.
    For built-in workers, apply the same task-design, supervision, and acceptance
    rules through their native tools.
    
    ## Contents
    
    - [Prepare the task](#context-and-intent)
    - [Launch](#steerable-and-detached-runs)
    - [Supervise](#first-minute-check-and-adaptive-parent-supervision)
    - [Observe and steer](#observation-and-steering)
    - [Wait and collect](#keeping-the-parent-active)
    - [Change approach](#changing-approach-and-preserving-work)
    - [Accept the result](#result-review-and-acceptance)
    - [Less capable workers](#delegating-to-a-less-capable-model)
    - [Read-only research](#stateful-grok-research)
    - [Handoffs](#handoffs)
    
    Read [delegate-runtime.md](delegate-runtime.md) for group waiting, durable Codex
    follow-ups, delivery states, backend differences, exits, or recovery. Read
    [delegate-vcs.md](delegate-vcs.md) when inspecting a worker through Git/JJ.
    
    ## Context and intent
    
    Before launch, inspect relevant code and record repository status. Give the
    worker the user's overall goal, relevant situation, and how this assignment
    contributes. Then specify the exact working root, bounded deliverable, scope and
    non-goals, compatibility constraints, acceptance criteria, and required checks.
    Use relevant file hints without treating them as the entire investigation scope.
    Explain task-specific pitfalls; prescribe implementation steps only where they
    prevent a concrete mistake. Assess the capability gap and apply the
    [additional protocol](#delegating-to-a-less-capable-model) when required.
    
    State whether the deliverable is an assessment or an implementation. Authorized
    work should continue to completion within scope; unresolved dependencies or
    necessary scope changes go to the parent with evidence while independent work
    continues. Keep localized edits and tests proportional to the task. Ask for
    findings, evidence, and a concise rationale, not hidden reasoning.
    
    ```text
    Context and intent: We are preparing the MCP server for reliable Windows use.
    This task should ensure client disconnects do not leave shutdown hanging.
    Working root: /exact/assigned/repository
    Task: Fix SSE shutdown and verify disconnect scenarios. Preserve the public API;
    another worker owns cursor behavior. Use the goal to choose an in-scope solution.
    Report any necessary scope change with evidence and a proposed adjustment.
    Return changed files, verification results, and remaining limitations or blockers.
    ```
    
    ## Steerable and detached runs
    
    - Select exactly one `-a <agent-id>`; no default, globs, or multi-select.
    - Codex CLI, Claude Code, OpenCode, Grok Build, and Devin CLI support delegation.
      Gemini is review-only and is rejected by delegate.
    - Delegate uses a full-access runtime, even for a read-only task. It provides no
      sandbox or interactive approval flow; task scope does not expand user authority.
      Backend permission failures remain explicit blockers.
    - Steerable is the default (`--steerable` is a compatibility alias). Use
      `--one-shot` only when explicitly choosing direct execution without steering.
    - Use `--detach` to return immediately with a run id on stdout, or keep a
      foreground call resumable through the harness. Either must permit supervision.
      `--detach` and `--one-shot` are mutually exclusive.
    - When later Codex follow-ups are likely, read
      [durable continuation](delegate-runtime.md#durable-codex-follow-ups) and opt
      into `--persist-session` at launch.
    
    ```bash
    # task.md contains the contract above; run from the assigned repository root.
    RUN_ID=$("$PORCH" delegate -a grok --detach --prompt-file task.md)
    # Inspect within the first minute, then follow the supervision guidance below.
    "$PORCH" delegate events "$RUN_ID" --max-events 50
    ```
    
    Record the run id and launch time. A foreground steerable run prints `run_id=…`
    early on stderr; retrieve its final answer from stdout or `wait`. Recover a lost
    id with `delegate list --active`, identifying the task before acting on it. If
    `PORCH_STEER_DIR` was overridden, preserve it for every control/observation command.
    Parallel writers need separate user-authorized workspaces; do not create them
    implicitly. Read-only workers may share a root. Batch independent tool calls
    and keep useful parent work moving while workers run.
    
    ## First-minute check and adaptive parent supervision

    # U6: managed execution UI — документы, одобрения, состав, запуск, наблюдение — отчёт
    
    Дата: 2026-10-01. Ветка `feat/agent-modes`.
    План: [agent-core-implementation-plan.md](../plans/agent-core-implementation-plan.md).
    Журнал отклонений: [2026.10.01_agent-core-u6_deviations.md](../tmp/2026.10.01_agent-core-u6_deviations.md).
    
    Отчёт покрывает **U6**: фронтенд managed-исполнения — execution API
    client + Pinia-store, секция документов/одобрений/состава/run-контроля в
    карточке, managed-aware персистентность доски, managed-история и детали в
    Workflow-панели. U7 (реальные CLI, Compose, браузерные пути/навигация)
    не реализован и не заявлен готовым. Модуль ждёт родительского
    независимого прогона и приёмки.
    
    ## Реализовано
    
    | Файл | Содержание |
    |---|---|
    | `src/lib/execution/api.ts` | Типизированный `ExecClient`: `getCard`/`getRun`/`getRunEvents`/`getDocument`/`getArtifact`, команды `sendCommand`, реестр пресетов `listPresets`/`createPreset`/`updatePreset`/`deletePreset`, `refreshIndex`. Типы приведены к реальным полям домена: `checkReport.exitCode`/`logOutArtifactId`/`logErrArtifactId`, `validation.reports.findings.doc`/`verdicts.doc`, `fixContext`, `rounds`, `artifacts`, `result`, `diagnostic`. `ExecApiError` с `status`/`code`/`details`; 409 → `revision_conflict`/`workspace_drift`/`command_conflict`. |
    | `src/lib/execution/ui-model.ts` | UI-гейты над реальными wire-фикстурами: `canStart`/`canStop`/`canContinue`/`canAccept`, `continuePayload`, сборка документов (`buildDocSource`), строки checks (`CheckRow`), `presetPayload`, лейблы стадий/фаз/статусов. |
    | `src/stores/execution.ts` | Per-card состояние с generations/single-flight: `watchCard`/`unwatchCard`, `refreshCard` (coalesce, reqSeq-guard, 404 → unmanaged + `clearManagedProjection`), `refreshRun` (per-selection in-flight токен — A→B→A безопасен; event-history drain по страницам с `eventsCursor`/`eventsPending`/`eventsCorrupt`), `selectRun` (pin исторического run, auto-follow current), `sendCommand` (свежий read → `expectedControlRevision`; net-stamp до POST — поздняя ошибка команды не гасит более новое здоровое состояние), `openManagedRun`/`clearFocus` (focus владеет ровно одним watch'ем), `managedIndex`, `loadPresets`. Отказ refresh = отказ команды без POST. Все poll-таймеры освобождаются `unwatch`/`clearFocus`/`stopPolling`. |
    | `src/features/board/useCardDraft.ts` | Автосейв-машина drawer'а: per-field dirty-tracking относительно baseline загрузки (а не текущего полла), flush старой карточки при смене `cardId`/dispose (не протекает в новую), отказы managed-мутаций. Watcher на тот же `cardId`: серверные managed-поля (stage/status/project/blocked/blockedReason/cancelled/session) обновляются из авторитетного projection при сохранении локальных пользовательских правок — поллинг НЕ помечает dirty и НЕ вызывает записей. |
    | `src/features/board/CardDrawer.vue` | Секция managed-исполнения через `ExecutionPanel`; managed-owned контролы (статус/стадия/проект/флаги/сессия) отключены с правдивой причиной; flush обращается к явному cardId. |
    | `src/features/board/ExecutionPanel.vue` | Документы (attach text/import-path, viewer, approve requirements/plan с выводом реальных checks: run/cwd/timeoutSec/setup), пресет-состав (save/bind, reload реестра после сохранения), run-контроль (start/stop/continue/accept_result по hash), disabled-реasons, `commandError` 409 → подсказка обновить. Отчётность по реальным полям домена: checks-отчёты (exitCode, отдельные stdout/stderr-артефакты, сопоставление по `report.index`), findings (severity/status/текст), verdicts-doc (blocking/nonblocking/disputed/unvetted семантика), rounds, result/diagnostic. Ownership/generation-гварды: чтение артефактов и открытие документов привязаны к card+run+seq; редактор документов заморожен на время in-flight attach; состояние run-control/preset сбрасывается при смене карточки. |
    | `src/features/board/ManagedRunEvents.vue` | Общий компонент полной managed-истории событий — все страницы, drained стором (без tail-cutoff); каждое событие раскрывается в записанный payload (`<details>` + verbatim JSON). Используется и в ExecutionPanel, и в WorkflowPanel — одна реализация. |
    | `src/stores/board.ts` | Per-field delta persistence: `updateCard` помечает только реально изменённые поля; `persistManagedBoard` сериализован (`managedSaveChain`), каждая попытка мержит из ЖИВЫХ `cards` + CAS-rev по `mutateRemoteDocChecked`; clear только отгруженных поколений (редактирование во время PUT сохраняется и доставляется следующим циклом). `adoptRemoteBoard`: remote — база, локальные только явно-новые/unsaved строки, удалённые remote-карты не воскрешаются, managed-поля всегда из авторитетной строки. `syncManagedRows` — read-only оверлей серверных managed-полей, seq-ordered, boolean = успех чтения (не «changed»). `applyManagedProjection`/`clearManagedProjection` — projection-синк без пользовательских записей, backstop против отката controlRevision. Lifecycle-мутации (move/status/flag/remove/drag) отказывают managed-картам с правдивыми причинами через `MutationResult`. Новые `fetchRemoteDoc`/`mutateRemoteDocChecked` — scoped, bounded whole-request JSON (тело читается под тем же дедлайном). |
    | `src/components/WorkflowPanel.vue` | Managed-секция рядом с porch (porch reader не изменён, `porchRunId` ≠ ACP session): список managed-карт (`managedIndex`), focus-деталь — селектор исторических run'ов карточки, статус/фаза/current-run принадлежность, `ManagedRunEvents` (полная drained-история с payload'ами), явные состояния: `runError` + retry-кнопка вместо вечного «loading…», loading только пока `runInflight`. Managed-индекс опрашивается пока панель смонтирована. |
    | `src/lib/host/storage.ts` | `fetchRemoteDoc`/`mutateRemoteDocChecked` для managed-персистентности; `KVStore.dispose` + `__resetWebKvForTests` — тестовый teardown poll-таймера RemoteKVStore и кэша probe (production интервал намеренно живёт всю сессию). |
    
    ## Плановые требования → доказательства
    
    | Требование | Доказательство |
    |---|---|
    | enable только из карточки с авторитетных входов | `enable` через `sendCommand`: свежий read → `phase==='unmanaged'` → POST без CAS; уже managed → `already_managed` до POST (execution-store тесты + real-handler suite) |
    | документы версионируются и одобряются раздельно | attach/approve requirements+plan через production-стор против реального handler; `approve_plan` bound к requirements (`requirementsSha256`, `checksSource: document_block`); набор checks показывается с run/cwd/timeoutSec/setup |
    | состав валидируется по server-compatibility | `save_preset` + `loadPresets` → `compatibility` из реального реестра; `canStart(view)` над стор-adopted view |
    | ревизии/409 без потери данных | deferred-command тест: ошибка не опускает свежее online-состояние; stale `expectedControlRevision` → реальный `409 revision_conflict` (классификация `ExecApiError`), повтор по live-rev через `sendCommand` успешен и store принимает свежий view |
    | observability/остановка/продолжение/приёмка | `selectRun` pin + auto-follow current; `refreshRun` drain'ит ВСЕ страницы событий (`eventsCursor`/`eventsPending`, out-of-order не откатывает курсор); terminal-переход триггерит добор деталей; acceptance bound к `resultSha256` (approve-gate `canAccept`) |
    | смена карточки без утечек/перетираний | focus владеет одним watch'ем; `unwatch` во время in-flight GET отменяет эффект ответа; A→B→A: старый A не гасит новый flight-токен; все таймеры/годы освобождаются — сьюта завершается сама |
    | managed persistence не затирает соседние правки | per-field дельта merge на remote-базе; delayed-PUT + правка во время полёта — обе сохраняются; remote-удаление не воскрешается; managed lifecycle-мутации отказывают |
    | run-детали правдивые | рендер только по полям реального run-рекорда: check-отчёты по `report.index` с exitCode/stdout/stderr-артефактами, findings/verdicts docs с семантикой гейта, artifacts читаются с run-генерационным гвардом |
    | события доступны целиком | `ManagedRunEvents` выводит ВСЕ drained-события с раскрытием payload — SSR-тест доказывает seq 1 и seq 30 с разными payload'ами одновременно в DOM (старый `slice(-12)` seq 1 скрыл бы) |
    | Workflow: исторический выбор + ошибка/повтор | селектор run'ов карточки (`st.view.runs`), `runError`+retry, loading только пока реальный flight; SSR-кейс: обе секции (managed+porch) рендерятся вместе |
    
    ## Реальный клиент/сервис-контракт (listener-free)
    
    `real state-service handler — user flow contract`: временные state/git
    каталоги, `createStateService`, посев `projects.json`/`board.json` через
    реальные PUT-маршруты, `ExecClient` над `svc.request` (без HTTP-listener).
    Весь flow идёт через **production Pinia-store**: `watchCard` + свежий
    read доказывает `unmanaged`, далее `exec.sendCommand` для
    enable → attach/approve requirements → attach/approve plan
    (`acp-checks` fence) → `save_preset`. Проверки: `canStart(st.view)` ok,
    server-projection `{stage:'plan',status:'done'}`, approved-bindings,
    `loadPresets` compatibility, re-attach инвалидирует ОБА approval,
    прямой stale-envelope → `ExecApiError 409 revision_conflict`,
    production-ритрай через свежий rev → успех + store-adoption,
    `st.commandError` чист.

    ## Чем доказано (честные слои)
    
    - **Реально:** запросный движок `ExecClient` против реального
      `svc.request`; production `sendCommand`/`refreshCard`/`refreshRun`/
      `selectRun`/`openManagedRun`; реальные CAS/dedup/aggregate/approval/
      invalidation семантики домена; board remote merge против реальных
      GET/PUT с ревизиями; SFC setup+render скомпилированных компонентов.
    - **Контролируемый транспорт:** гонки доказаны deferred-фикстурами
      (`FakeExec`/`wireFetch`) — порядок ответов управляем, без сети.
    - **SSR setup/render — НЕ браузер.** `createSSRApp`+`renderToString`
      выполняет setup и шаблон (включая immediate-watchers — TDZ-класс
      регрессий), но `onMounted`/`onBeforeUnmount`, навигация и реальные
      жизненные циклы не исполняются. Это setup/render-доказательство,
      не mount/unmount.
    - **НЕ доказано (U7):** браузерная навигация/жизненный цикл, живой
      HTTP-стек Compose, реальные Pi/Codex/Devin процессы, интеграция
      Tauri-хоста (Tauri-ветки не трогались).

    # Ревью четырёх агентских планов
    
    Дата: 2026-10-01. По одному read-only субагенту на план. Проверены документы, связи с ядром и релевантные исходники/установленные навыки. Реальные CLI/контейнерные прогоны не выполнялись. Внесённые ниже исправления проверены ведущим по тексту и связям документов; повторного независимого ревью исправленных версий не было.
    
    ## Результат
    
    Десять actionable замечаний: Fusion — 2, оркестратор — 3, Swarm — 3, подготовка идеи — 2. Все внесены в планы как уточнения согласованного поведения. Обязательных новых продуктовых вопросов не выявлено. Реальная совместимость среды и навыков остаётся входным гейтом реализации, а не доказанным результатом этого ревью.
    
    | План | Замечание | Исправление |
    |---|---|---|
    | Fusion | Git linked worktree не работает без общего git-dir | Приватный Git worker, доверенный импорт полного результата в каноническую ветку, тест рестарта |
    | Fusion | Egress не доказывает наличие поиска у модели | Capability и реальный search probe для CLI/образа/модели, preflight состава |
    | Оркестратор | Worker Git мог открыть чужие refs | Приватные автономные repositories без shared git-dir/alternates/hardlinks |
    | Оркестратор | Разрешение конфликта могло потеряться в финальной сборке | Immutable IntegrationArtifact и provenance, повторное использование принятого resolution |
    | Оркестратор | Незакоммиченные результаты не попадали в diff commits | Полный immutable resultCommit до проверки, включая новые файлы и удаления |
    | Swarm | Freeze не закрывал гонку start/apply и recovery | Worktree barrier, durable worker identities, подтверждения freeze, recovery/thaw и порядок cancel |
    | Swarm | Не учитывался executable bit | Git modes 100644/100755, mode preconditions, журнал/rollback и chmod-only |
    | Swarm | Не определён возврат замечаний владельцам | Маршрутизация владельцам, возврат рабочей фазы, запрет записи при проверке, общие лимиты |
    | Подготовка идеи | Требования/план могли считаться ready при открытом гейте навыка | Durable SkillGate с binding/digest и предъявленной версией, проверки readiness/start |
    | Подготовка идеи | Реальные навыки требуют filesystem/Git/handoffs, несовместимые с одной read-only проекцией | P0 feasibility, приватная document workspace, реальные операции и обязательные handoffs, допуск только доказанных routes |
    
    ## Остаточные ограничения
    
    - Проверить container-runtime и реальные возможности CLI при реализации Fusion F1.
    - Проверить filesystem/approval/handoff каждого начального skill binding в подготовке P0. Unsupported route нельзя показывать доступным или подменять имитацией.
    - Git isolation, freeze/recovery и SkillGate пока являются требованиями плана, а не реализованными гарантиями.
    - Сохранённые планы и отчёт не означают запуск фоновой реализации; она в этом чате не запускалась.
    
    ## Изменение архитектуры после ревью
    
    После независимого ревью пользователь выбрал постоянную основу Pi и отдельные конфигурации ролей вместо универсальной поддержки разных CLI. Четыре плана обновлены этим решением, проверки переведены на Pi-профили; разнообразие моделей Fusion сохраняется. Основание — документация установленного Pi 0.85.1: отдельная config directory, явные skills/extensions, tool allowlist и RPC extension UI. Реальный запуск настроенных профилей ещё не проверен. Это уточнение после ревью не проходило повторное независимое ревью.
    
    ## Повторное ревью после выбора Pi profiles
    
    Дата: 2026-10-01. Четыре независимых read-only субагента, по одному на план. Проверены актуальные документы, релевантные контракты ядра и установленная документация Pi. Реальные прогоны не выполнялись. Семь существенных P2 подтверждены ведущим и исправлены; новых продуктовых решений пользователя не требуется. Исправленные формулировки проверены ведущим, отдельный третий круг ревью не запускался.
    
    | План | Исправление после второго ревью |
    |---|---|
    | Fusion | Search capability зависит от digest полного эффективного профиля, включая extensions/tools/allowlist. Удаление search tool инвалидирует probe. |
    | Fusion | Dependencies готовятся по approved setup/lockfiles в отдельной ограниченной setup-среде; контроллер с Docker socket не выполняет код проекта. Проверяется реальная сборка и смена lockfile. |
    | Оркестратор | Канонический resolution по точным inputs/порядку сборки переиспользуется всеми потребителями; пересекающиеся artifacts проверяются на совместимость. |
    | Оркестратор | Completion/verification/integration проверяют поколение входов; поздний результат не возвращает stale узел в accepted. |
    | Swarm | Полномочия привязаны к attempt/turn/поколению, отзываются при terminal/deadline/stop; durable apply recovery отдельно от новых команд. |
    | Swarm | Подтверждение относится к immutable ревизии текста и круга участников; старые ack не утверждают новую ревизию. |
    | Подготовка идеи | Native RPC диалог получает matching extension_ui_response в живую попытку; только завершённый вопрос переносит ответ в следующий prompt. Recovery создаёт новую RPC identity. |

    170-
    171-| Mode | Use when | Consequence |
    172-|---|---|---|
    173-| `auto` | Normal clarification, added constraint, or preferred direction | Safest native behavior available on the backend |
    174-| `queue` | Current work may finish before guidance is applied | May affect only the next safe boundary; Grok uses a real next-turn FIFO entry |
    175:| `interrupt` | Current direction is wrong and partial work should be abandoned | May cancel the active turn/tool flow; Claude rejects instead of silently downgrading |
    176-
    177:For Grok, `auto`/`queue` is the productive default for additive guidance. Use `interrupt` only to replace direction because each later interrupt supersedes the prompt currently running, including an earlier steer.
    178-
    179-### What Grok actually does with a steer
    180-
    181-Verified against grok 1.0.0 over real ACP runs:
    182-
    183-- `auto`/`queue` never lands inside the running turn. The prompt enters the session FIFO and Grok answers it in a **new turn** with the full session history. If the running turn is mid-generation, it finishes first (`end_turn`) and the steer runs afterwards. If the running turn is blocked waiting on a tool — a long shell command, a background command poll — Grok itself promotes the queued prompt and cancels the running turn with `cancelTrigger=send_now`, so guidance can land within seconds.
    184:- Because of that promotion, the **original task prompt can end as `cancelled`/`superseded` in `auto` mode too**, with no client interrupt involved. That is normal Grok behavior, not a failed run: the steer turn continues the remaining work in the same session.
    185:- `interrupt` cancels the running turn immediately (`cancelTrigger=send_now`) and the steer prompt takes over.
    186-- In both modes every message the agent produces after the steer is attributed to the steer's `promptId`, and the final answer is assembled from the steer turn onward. Expect the final answer to read as the continuation, not as the original plan.
    187-
    188-Practical consequences for the calling agent:
    189-
    190-- Steering a Grok run that is only thinking or streaming text has **delayed effect**: nothing changes until the current turn ends. Do not send the same guidance again; check `status --json` for the steer's `prompt_id` and its lifecycle instead.
    191-- Steering a Grok run that is executing long tool calls has near-immediate effect.
    192-- Make guidance self-contained. The steer runs as its own turn, so state it as an instruction that stands on its own ("from now on … ; continue the remaining steps"), not as a fragment that only makes sense inline.
    193-- Verify semantics through task artifacts, never through the steer status alone.
    194-
    195:### What Devin actually does with a steer
    196-
    197-Verified against devin 3000.10.27 over real ACP runs:
    198-
    199-- `auto`/`queue` are `same_turn`: a second `session/prompt` merges into the running turn instead of entering a next-turn queue, so guidance can take effect without waiting for `end_turn`.
    200:- `interrupt` is `cancel_and_send`: `session/cancel` resolves in-flight prompts with stopReason `cancelled`; the session stays usable and the steer prompt takes over.
    201-- The ack ladder is the shared one — `request_sent` → `completed`/`cancelled`/`failed` by the request's own stopReason; it is never `applied`.
    202-
    203-## Mailbox lifecycle
    204-
    205-| `mailbox_status` | Meaning |
    206-|---|---|
    207-| `accepted` | Persisted locally, not dispatched |
    208-| `delivering` | Supervisor is calling the backend adapter |
    209-| `request_sent` | Written to transport; no application evidence yet |
    210-| `queued` | Accepted by backend but not observed running |
    211-| `awaiting_queue_resolution` | Grok follower cancellation awaits authoritative queue evidence |
    212-| `merged` | Grok combined this guidance into another running prompt |
    213-| `running` | Correlated with an active prompt/turn; does not prove semantic effect |
    214-| `completed` | Steer prompt ended normally; verify task artifacts/result |
    215-| `incomplete` | Steer stopped at an output/token limit |
    216-| `applied` | Backend directly acknowledged replay/injection; still verify task effects |
    217-| `cancelled` | Steer started but was cancelled |
    218:| `superseded` | A later Grok `sendNow` prompt replaced it — a client `interrupt`, or Grok's own promotion of a queued steer over a turn blocked in a tool wait |
    219-| `dropped` | A never-running Grok prompt was absent from later merge evidence |
    220-| `abandoned` | Overall run ended before steer reached a protocol terminal state |
    221-| `failed` / `rejected` | Steer did not complete normally; inspect backend evidence |
    222-
    223-Never interpret `accepted`, `request_sent`, `queued`, or `running` as proof that guidance changed files or the final answer. `completed` proves prompt lifecycle completion, not semantic compliance.
    224-
    225-## Retry-safe steering
    226-
    227-```bash
    228-"$PORCH" delegate steer run_<id> \
    229-  --client-id requirement-cache-backend-v1 \
    230-  --mode auto \
    231-  --prompt-file steer.md
    232-```
    233-
    234-Retry a stable `client_id` only with identical content, mode, and kind. Any mismatch is an idempotency conflict. For an active run, a retry with identical content returns the existing message; a new instruction needs a new client id. A closed mailbox rejects new messages. Reconcile the run outcome first: use `--continue-run` for the latest successful durable Codex run, or deliberately start a new run for remaining work when continuation is unavailable. Failed or uncertain runs require inspection before recovery; never silently replay the original task. Client ids are SHA-256-mapped for paths; the original value remains in JSON.
    235-
    236-Do not put secrets in tasks or steering guidance unless persistence in private raw/audit artifacts is intentional. Large task and guidance bodies travel through files or mailbox JSON, not large argv/env values.
    usage: porch-steer-control steer [-h] [--mode {auto,queue,interrupt}]
                                     [--prompt-file PROMPT_FILE]
